title: Energy Empowerment Program (LEEP)
text: This yearlong internship program equips students with the skills and knowledge necessary to enter the energy sector workforce. Participants engage in personal development, honing their mindset, social awareness, planning, problem-solving, teamwork, and communication abilities. Additionally, they receive guidance for their future endeavors through college counseling and career preparation, ensuring a comprehensive and well-rounded experience that prepares them for success in the energy industry.
requirements: unknown

title: National Summer Transportation Institute
text: The National Summer Transportation Institute offers a complimentary, week-long, non-residential program for high school students entering grades 9-12. Participants delve into the realm of transportation engineering through engaging hands-on activities and collaborative group projects. The program encompasses a tour of the regional traffic operation center and transit authority in the Greater Niagara Falls and Buffalo area, a visit to Buffalo International Airport and its Air Control Tower, a cruise along the Erie Canal in Lockport, and a demonstration of Olli, the self-driving shuttle.
requirements: Application

title: UB/National Grid Leadership Camp
text: The UB/National Grid Camp offers an immersive experience for high school students with a passion for STEM. Designed to foster interest in STEM careers, the camp welcomes students from underrepresented groups. Participants reside in North Campus dorms for three nights, engaging in an engineering challenge that requires teamwork. The program includes a field trip to National Grid, a business lunch with industry professionals and UB faculty, and hands-on laboratory sessions at UB. This comprehensive experience provides students with valuable insights into the world of STEM, fostering their aspirations and preparing them for future success in these fields.
requirements: Application

title: Arkansas Children's Job Shadowing Program
text: Arkansas Children's Hospital's job shadowing program provides high school students with an immersive experience in the healthcare field. Through an online training course, students gain foundational knowledge in their chosen area of interest. They then embark on a 1-3 day shadowing experience, observing the hospital environment and the responsibilities of healthcare professionals. While direct patient care is not permitted, students witness firsthand the diverse roles and duties within the healthcare system. The program aims to foster students' understanding of healthcare careers and inspire their future aspirations in the field.
requirements: 16 years old or older

title: Tufts University Biomedical Engineering Research Scholars (TUBERS)
text: The Tufts University Biomedical Engineering Research Scholars (TUBERS) Program offers high school students with an interest in biomedical engineering research the opportunity to gain practical experience over a six-week summer period. Participants will engage in hands-on work within Tufts' biomedical engineering labs, where they will learn experimental protocols, test hypotheses, and contribute to specific projects. They will receive academic guidance from undergraduate and graduate students involved in the program, as well as their research mentors. The program is provided free of charge and encourages applications from underrepresented backgrounds. While participants are responsible for their own transportation to campus, housing is not available for out-of-area students. The program's objectives include exposing students to a wide range of biomedical engineering techniques, enabling them to delve deeply into a specific scientific field, guiding them through the entire scientific method in their project, providing opportunities for presenting their findings, allowing them to observe the work of professional researchers, and fostering critical and independent thinking. Additionally, students are encouraged to utilize their projects for participation in science competitions, potentially earning honors and scholarship funds.
requirements: To be considered for the Tufts University Biomedical Engineering Research Scholars (TUBERS) Program, applicants must be 16 years old by the start of the program on July 5th, 2023 and show a strong interest in biomedical research. Participants must be committed to working for approximately 6 weeks during the summer in the Biomedical Engineering labs at Tufts, learning about research techniques and a particular field of study in depth while carrying out all steps of the scientific method in their project. Individuals from underrepresented backgrounds are strongly encouraged to apply. Participants are expected to find their own transportation to the Tufts University Medford campus and there is no housing provided for out-of-area students. Students are encouraged to use their projects to participate in local and national science competitions. The program is free and successful applicants will learn a broad array of biomedical engineering research techniques, gain academic guidance from undergraduates and graduate students involved with the program and their research mentors, observe the work of professional researchers, present their findings to others in the program, parents, and teachers, learn to think critically and independently, and gain a deeper understanding of a particular field of science.

title: Teen Council
text: If you possess a passion for art and an inquisitive nature towards museums, consider applying for a summer internship at the Art Institute. This opportunity allows you to collaborate with fellow teens in supporting festivals, gallery tours, and workshops that cater to a vast audience of local and international visitors. As an intern, you will interact with museum professionals, gain exclusive behind-the-scenes access, explore the world-renowned collection, engage with local artists, and contribute to the planning and execution of creative programs.
requirements: For Chicago high school teens who will be at least 16 at the start of the internship

title: AgriTREK/SciTREK and AgDiscovery Summer Programs for High School Students
text: The AgriTREK/SciTREK Summer Institute and AgDiscovery Summer Program are two-week residential programs designed to foster an appreciation for Science, Technology, Engineering, Agriculture, and Mathematics (STEAM) education and related fields. Through hands-on research, leadership development, and personal enrichment activities, these programs aim to engage high school students in the exploration of STEAM concepts and their practical applications. The programs provide a unique opportunity for students to immerse themselves in a dynamic learning environment, collaborate with peers and mentors, and gain valuable insights into the fields of science, technology, engineering, agriculture, and mathematics.
requirements: unknown

title: Chicago Youth Service Corps
text: Chicago Youth Service Corps offers year-round paid opportunities for youth aged 16-24 to participate in community service, project-based learning, and leadership development. The program embraces diversity and encourages participants to contribute their unique experiences, backgrounds, and traditions to their service. By joining Chicago Youth Service Corps, youth can engage in meaningful community involvement while developing valuable skills and fostering their leadership potential.
requirements: Be 16-24 years of age

title: MITES Summer Program
text: The MITES Summer Program is a six-week, on-campus program that immerses US high school juniors in rigorous and rewarding mathematics, science, and humanities courses. Scholars will engage with STEM professionals in seminars and tours of MIT labs and local companies employing MITES alumni. They will also have access to lab tours, social events, and college admissions counseling while developing the academic and personal skills essential for success. The program is free of charge, with students only responsible for transportation to and from MIT. At the conclusion of the program, students will receive a written evaluation from their instructors outlining their strengths, growth areas, and contributions to the class, which some use as supplemental material with their college applications.
requirements: Applicants must be U.S. citizens or permanent residents who are high school juniors. They must have a passion for science, technology, engineering, and math, which should be demonstrated through extracurricular activities, essays, and letters of recommendation. Applicants must also have a strong academic record with good grades.

title: High School Apprenticeships
text: The U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command Army Research Laboratory (DEVCOM-ARL), an integral component of the Army Futures Command, serves as the U.S. Army's foundational research laboratory. Its mission is to operationalize science, conducting research and reconnaissance to inform future Army science, technology, and engineering. By investing in areas that ensure overmatch, DEVCOM-ARL plays a crucial role in foundational research, ensuring the Army's continued technological superiority and readiness for future challenges.
address: U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command Army Research Laboratory (Boston, MA)
requirements: High School (9-12 Grade or within 60 months of completing high school degree, not enrolled in undergrad program).

title: Careers in Science (CiS) Intern Program
text: Careers in Science is a multi-year, year-round program that provides paid internships and youth development opportunities to San Francisco high school students from communities underrepresented in STEM fields. The program specifically targets girls and students of color, aiming to increase their participation and representation in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics. Through hands-on experiences, mentorship, and academic support, Careers in Science empowers students to explore STEM careers, develop their skills, and pursue higher education in these fields.
address: 55 Music Concourse Dr, San Francisco, CA 94118
requirements:
Be currently enrolled full time as a 9th or 10th grade student in an SFUSD school
Maintain a GPA of 2.5 and a grade of C or higher in science and math
Be able to obtain a valid work permit (US citizens and others authorized to work in the US)
Commit to all attendance requirements for 2 or 3 years, through high school graduation
Be able to commute to the Academy and nearby locations after school and on Saturdays during the school year, and on weekdays in the summer (some remote work may be required)
Demonstrate interest and enthusiasm for learning, teaching, and doing science

title: High School Work Study Program
text: Our student programs provide opportunities for students to enhance their knowledge of the NSA, expand their career field expertise, and earn financial compensation or scholarship funds. These programs are specifically designed for students who intend to participate in a school-sponsored work experience program during their senior year. The availability of positions varies based on the specific requirements of each participating site.
requirements: High school juniors who are at least 16 years of age

title: Counselor in Training
text: Our CIT program is designed to provide leadership opportunities within a small group setting while offering a fulfilling camp experience. This selective four-week program requires an interview and involves living in a cabin with campers and a lead counselor. CITs gain practical experience assisting in various program areas, including field games and camp festivals. Additionally, certifications for belay instructors and junior lifeguards are available within this program.
requirements: Must be rising juniors or seniors.

title: The LEAH Knox Data Science and Biomedical Research Summer Internship
text: Successful candidates for this program can earn up to $2,250, along with additional benefits such as STEM teaching internships, mentorship from STEM professionals, and eligibility for paid internship opportunities the following summer in a research setting in the Boston area.
requirements: The LEAH Knox Data Science and Biomedical Research Summer Internship is designed for rising high school juniors and seniors who are interested in pursuing science, regardless of their prior lab or research experience. Applicants must be at least 16 years old and should be fully vaccinated and boosted against COVID-19 (two doses of Pfizer and a booster shot). Students of color and students from low-income backgrounds are strongly encouraged to apply. To be eligible, applicants should have an interest in scientific research, a willingness to learn and work hard, and the ability to commit to the program's full duration, which runs from July 5, 2023, to August 9, 2023, Monday through Friday, from 9:30 AM to 4:00 PM. Successful applicants will learn quantitative methods, data analysis, and coding alongside molecular biology techniques from experienced biology and computer science instructors at MIT. The program includes STEM teaching internships, college and career readiness workshops, and additional academic support. To apply, students must submit an application form, four short answer questions (at least 150 words each), a letter of recommendation from a current/former science or math teacher, their resume, and a copy of their academic transcript. Applications are due on Sunday, March 12th, 2023, at 10:00 PM Eastern Standard Time, and letters of recommendation are due one week later.

title: NLI Challenge
text: NLI is a leadership program designed for youth aged 13-15 residing or attending school in North Lawndale, Gage Park, and New City/Back of the Yards. Each session fosters camaraderie among participants through community-building games and encourages them to explore and discuss issues related to violence in their neighborhoods. The program aims to equip youth with leadership skills and facilitate interactions with adult leaders, including aldermen, to amplify their voices and advocate for the changes they envision within their communities.
requirements: Must be 13-15 years old, as well as go live or go to school In North Lawndale, Gage Park, or New City/Back of the Yards.

title: Alamo Academies Internship
text: SAMA collaborates with Alamo Academies, a provider of high-demand STEM curriculums for high school students, to connect members with internship opportunities. Alamo Academies introduces students to STEM careers in high-demand industries. Through hands-on learning, students gain insights into various career pathways, enabling them to make informed decisions about their post-graduation educational and career aspirations. These internships provide valuable experiences for both manufacturers and students, fostering a mutually beneficial partnership that supports the development of future STEM professionals.
requirements: unknown

title: Congresswoman Sheila Jackson Lee
text: Congresswoman Sheila Jackson Lee provides internship opportunities within her Houston District Office. Interns are responsible for assisting with daily office tasks, including answering phone calls, composing correspondence, and managing media clips. Additionally, they may engage in constituent casework or participate in district-based projects.
requirements: unknown

title: CSExplore Camp
text: The CSExplore Camp, hosted by the Computer Science and Engineering department, is a captivating four-day youth program tailored specifically for female high school students. This immersive summer experience delves into the foundations of computing, encompassing both the intricate hardware of circuits and the abstract logic of software development. To showcase the field's versatility, the camp incorporates activities such as robot programming and video game design. Held on UB's North campus, the camp includes excursions to cutting-edge research labs that demonstrate the practical applications of computing in addressing real-world challenges.
requirements: Application

title: Youth Conservation Corps
text: Youth Conservation Corps members engage in a diverse array of projects in a salubrious outdoor environment, including trail construction, fence maintenance, campground cleanup, wildlife habitat enhancement, environmental education planning and instruction, stream restoration, and historic building preservation. Educational field trips provide opportunities to witness wildlife, explore historical sites, ascend mountaintops, and marvel at ancient ruins.
requirements: Students 15-18 years of age

title: Student Heroes
text: Student Heroes offers a comprehensive program that empowers high school students to develop leadership abilities, enhance their college applications, and make a meaningful impact in their communities. Participants engage in hands-on activities such as training volunteers, organizing food drives, and gaining insights into food insecurity. Additionally, they attend professional development workshops designed to cultivate essential skills. To participate, students are expected to dedicate four shifts per month, totaling 50 hours of service, providing them with a valuable opportunity to contribute to their communities while building their resumes and college profiles.
requirements: unknown

title: Teen Opportunities at the Adler Planetarium
text: The Adler Planetarium offers a range of internship opportunities for high school students to delve into the world of STEAM (science, technology, engineering, arts, and math) in an engaging and supportive environment. The Far Horizons Teens summer program empowers participants with hands-on experience in preventing light pollution through circuitry, computer programming, structural design, and teamwork, culminating in the development of prototype solutions to mitigate its effects. Participants receive a stipend and transportation support via CTA passes. Additionally, the Youth Leadership Council fosters advocacy and leadership skills for young people seeking to amplify "youth voice" within the museum community. This council undertakes projects such as designing and curating a photography exhibition on light pollution. The Adler Planetarium prioritizes the safety of participants by ensuring they are well-informed about COVID-19 safety protocols.
requirements: Far Horizons Teens: enrolled in 8th-11th grade during the 2022-2023 school year, interested in learning new STEM skills, passionate about science, team player. Summer Internship: current high school students, interested in building professional skills in a supportive and fun environment, excited to work collaboratively as part of a team, available for all onsite program dates, able to attend an orientation. Mission Near Space: enrolled in 7th-8th grade during the 2022-2023 school year, attending a Chicago Public School, COVID-19 vaccinated, unless they request and are granted a medical or religious exemption. Youth Leadership Council and Youth Organization for Lights Out programs are subject to certain application timelines that have specific deadlines for when they can apply.

title: High School Internship
text: The High School Internship Program offers a unique opportunity for individuals with diverse interests to explore the intersection of their passions within the realm of art and museum operations. This program provides one-on-one and small group interactions with Museum professionals in various fields, including editorial, marketing, social media, and education. Through these interactions, interns gain valuable insights from peers and professionals, enabling them to discover the convergence of their interests and aspirations within the museum environment.
requirements: The Met High School Internship Program offers paid opportunities for students who are two to three years from graduating high school (in grades 10 and 11) or obtaining their High School Equivalency degree and who, on the application deadline date, either reside in or attend a high school or home school in New York, New Jersey or Connecticut. In accordance with the New York City mandate, applicants interested in interning must be fully vaccinated and able to show proof by the start of the internship program.

title: Internship Program
text: Interns in our office engage in public service by assisting constituents of New Jersey's 4th Congressional District. This internship offers practical experience in administrative and legislative support, fulfilling educational objectives. Through this hands-on involvement, interns gain valuable insights into the operations of the federal government, fostering a deeper understanding of its functions and responsibilities.
requirements: Only open to upperclassman high school students

title: High School Internship
text: This paid high school internship offers students the opportunity to develop both soft and hard skills. Soft skills include leadership and cooperation, while hard skills encompass project coordination and construction. Additionally, students will gain firsthand experience in the significance of community service. Through this internship, students will enhance their abilities in various areas while contributing to the community.
host: Habitat for Humanity of San Antonio
requirements: unknown

title: The Retirement Systems Summer Internship Program
text: As the custodians of the retirement funds for countless Alabamians, we are deeply committed to our mission. Our unwavering goal is to identify and secure the most advantageous investments and services for our members. By doing so, we strive to empower them with the resources and knowledge necessary to navigate the complexities of retirement planning. Our unwavering dedication extends to ensuring that our members are well-equipped to enjoy a fulfilling and financially secure retirement, a testament to our unwavering commitment to their well-being.
requirements: Be a high school student, or a graduate of high school that is enrolled in a college/university.

title: Temple of Understanding Internship
text: Since 2005, the Temple of Understanding has been hosting a Summer Internship program to foster the education of young individuals. This program provides student interns with the opportunity to attend open meetings of the UN Security Council, General Assembly, and various committees. Through this immersive experience, TOU aims to inspire these interns to become global citizens who are passionate about the humanitarian ideals upheld by the United Nations. The program serves as a catalyst for launching their careers in the field of international relations and global affairs.
requirements: Applicants are from different parts of the United States, as well as many other countries. Students accepted into this program meet with different Missions and NGOs for discussions based on their specific questions and interests. Applicants are from different parts of the United States, as well as many other countries, and must be 17 years old by June 20 of the Internship year. Applicants should be no older than 22 at the time of application.

title: Leader-in-Training Program
text: The Leaders-in-Training (LIT) program empowers high school students to develop their leadership abilities by sharing their passion for the natural world with younger campers. As LITs, they assist camp staff in fostering a safe, nurturing, and engaging environment for campers while gaining exposure to careers in education, biology, ecology, and natural resources. Through this program, LITs not only contribute to the enrichment of campers' experiences but also embark on a journey of personal growth and professional exploration in the field of environmental stewardship.
requirements: Must be entering 9th through 12th grade

title: Summer Internship
text: Rising high school seniors with aspirations in biomedical, bioengineering, or health-related fields are encouraged to explore this competitive summer internship opportunity. Participants will receive hands-on training in fundamental laboratory techniques and embark on a research project guided by a scientist or graduate student. The program culminates in a presentation of their research findings, which may potentially contribute to published scientific literature.
requirements: Students with a strong academic track record and an interest in pursuing biomedical, medical, bioengineering, and health-oriented professions are encouraged to apply for this competitive summer internship program.

title: High School Internship
text: Senator Booker's offices in Washington, D.C., Newark, New Jersey, and Camden, New Jersey offer a limited number of internships for high school and college students, as well as recent college graduates, during the fall, spring, and summer seasons. These internships provide an exceptional opportunity for individuals to gain firsthand experience in the inner workings of Congress and contribute to the Senator's legislative efforts.
requirements: Preference will be given to New Jersey residents.

title: Internship Program
text: The Attorney General of Connecticut serves as the state's chief legal officer for civil matters, providing legal counsel to all state agencies. The Office of the Attorney General (OAG) offers unpaid, volunteer internship opportunities to graduate and law students, paralegals, undergraduates, and highly motivated high school students. These internships provide valuable experience in the legal field and contribute to the OAG's mission of serving the people of Connecticut.
host: Connecticut Office of the Attorney General
requirements: Applicants should have an interest in the law, be able to communicate clearly, have strong research and writing skills and computer proficiency.

title: SUMMER HIGH SCHOOL ACADEMIC PROGRAM FOR ENGINEERS
text: Columbia Engineering's Summer High School Academic Program for Engineers (SHAPE) is a selective pre-college program designed for rising sophomores, juniors, seniors, and recent high school graduates. This program is specifically tailored towards students who demonstrate a strong aptitude for STEM (science, technology, engineering, and mathematics). SHAPE provides an immersive experience that fosters the development of students' STEM skills and knowledge, preparing them for future success in engineering and related fields.
requirements: unknown

title: Stanford University Mathematics Camp
text: SUMaC immerses participants in the realm of advanced mathematics through a comprehensive program of lectures, guided research, and collaborative problem-solving. Within an environment dedicated to mathematical exploration, participants delve into contemporary research frontiers, trace the historical evolution of pivotal mathematical concepts, and uncover the multifaceted applications of mathematics across scientific disciplines. This immersive experience fosters a deep understanding of the subject, empowering participants to engage with the complexities of modern mathematics and appreciate its profound impact on various fields of scientific inquiry.
requirements: unknown

title: Paid Summer Internship Program
text: The summer internship program offers paid, part-time internships for middle and high school students in San Antonio. The program aims to foster career exploration and goal-setting. Family Service collaborates with diverse organizations across various industries to ensure that each participant is matched with an organization that aligns with their interests and aspirations. Through this program, students gain valuable work experience, develop professional skills, and build connections within the local business community.

Applicants must be 14 to 17 years of age (Must be 14 by 6/19/2023 or 17 by 7/14/2023)
Student lives in both city council districts 1-8 and;
Must be enrolled in the following eligible school districts: San Antonio ISD, Northside ISD, Edgewood ISD, Harlandale ISD, South San ISD, Southside ISD and Southwest ISD
Copy of social security card
Copy of birth certificate OR Texas ID

title: Science Research Mentoring Program
text: The Science Research Mentoring Program (SRMP) at the American Museum of Natural History provides New York City high school students with the chance to engage in scientific research alongside Museum scientists for a year (August–June). Through SRMP, students receive compensation while gaining hands-on experience in research methodologies.

title: Fire Cadet Program
text: The OCFA Fire Cadet Program provides a comprehensive ten-week Fire Cadet Trainee Academy designed to equip participants with essential firefighting skills. Trainees engage in nine weeks of foundational classes at designated Fire Cadet Posts, culminating in a final exam at OCFA Headquarters during week ten. Upon successful completion, individuals become full-fledged program members and receive ride-along certification. Prospective Fire Cadets initiate the application process by submitting an interest form, followed by a detailed application that includes a current report card. The Fire Cadet Trainee Academies are conducted twice annually, with candidates over 18 years of age required to undergo a background check.
requirements: Must be ages 14-18, but once accepted cadets can stay on until they are 21

title: Seed Crew
text: The Seed Crew dedicates a significant portion of their afternoons to engaging in workshops that delve into a diverse range of topics. These workshops encompass sustainable agriculture practices, exploring the complexities of food accessibility, and examining the multifaceted aspects of social justice. Through these educational sessions, the Seed Crew members gain valuable insights and knowledge that empower them to make informed decisions and contribute meaningfully to their community.
requirements: Must be between ages 14-17

title: Program in Engineering & Technology
text: Established in 1983, the Governor's School of New Jersey is a tuition-free, summer residential program designed for high-achieving high school juniors with a passion for STEM (science, technology, engineering, and mathematics). The program currently operates two distinct tracks: the Governor's School in the Sciences, hosted at Drew University, and the Governor's School of Engineering & Technology, located at Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey.
address: 98 Brett Road, Room B114A Piscataway, NJ 08854
host: The Governor’s School of New Jersey
requirements:
The student must be a New Jersey resident and be a high school junior.
The student must have a very strong interest in engineering and technology and be committed to the acquisition of knowledge and the pursuit of opportunities in that field.
The student must be willing to live on campus for the duration of the program.  Saturdays and Sundays make up part of the program; there will be no weekend leaves of absence.
The applicant must be one of the top students in his or her school. The student should have primarily “A” grades in honors math and science classes and outstanding scores on standardized achievement tests.  Students who have demonstrated very strong abilities in engineering outside the classroom can also be strong candidates for the Governor’s School in spite of weaker standardized test scores.  Competitive candidates often rank in the top 5% of their class and score above the 90th percentile on standardized tests.  A student whose standardized test scores are below the 90th percentile but rank among the best in this/her school may still apply if he or she is otherwise qualified.

title: Saper Law Immersion Program
text: Established in 2013 by Daliah Saper, the Saper Law Immersion Program initially catered to recent law school graduates. However, it has since expanded to include high school and college students, offering them a week-long immersion into the legal profession. Held at Saper Law Offices, the program features instruction from Daliah Saper and her colleagues. The curriculum encompasses negotiation and writing exercises, field trips, and mock legal proceedings. Given Saper Law's specialization in social media and digital technology, the program incorporates case studies related to entertainment, business, and internet law.
requirements: unknown

title: MGH Youth Scholars
text: The MGH Youth Scholars Program empowers students from grades 9 through 12 in Boston, Chelsea, and Revere by fostering their academic aspirations. Its mission is threefold: to ignite their passion for science and healthcare, inspire their pursuit of higher education, and equip them with the academic foundation and confidence to excel in high school, graduate from college, and enter the workforce with a robust sense of academic achievement and self-assurance.
requirements: unknown

title: Summer Teen Volunteer Program
text: The Volunteer Department at The Hospital of Central Connecticut is delighted to offer a Summer Experience program specifically designed for high school students aged 14 and above. This program provides an immersive opportunity for students to gain valuable hands-on experience in a healthcare setting. Participants will have the chance to engage in meaningful volunteer activities, interact with healthcare professionals, and explore various aspects of the healthcare industry. The program aims to foster students' interest in healthcare careers, develop their interpersonal skills, and contribute to the well-being of their community.
requirements: Your parent or guardian must print, read, and complete the Parental Agreement (.doc format) A Teacher or Guidance Counselor will need to complete the Teacher/Counselor Reference Form (.doc format) Provide a Health Clearance Form (.doc format) completed by your primary care physician

title: Teen Volunteer Program
text: Teen volunteers provide invaluable support to hospital operations and fundraising initiatives. Their contributions allow hospital staff to focus on essential tasks, ensuring the smooth functioning and enhanced impact of the hospital. As teen volunteers, they forge meaningful connections with young patients and other teens, fostering a unique bond through activities such as craft projects and event staffing. Their presence and efforts make a tangible difference in the lives of children and families, creating a positive and supportive environment within the hospital setting.
address: 13123 E 16th Ave Ste B-270, Aurora, CO 80045
requirements: Be 13 years old or older

title: Internships
text: Congressman Joaquin Castro offers internship opportunities to high school students in his San Antonio office. Interns are responsible for assisting with various tasks, including daily office operations, answering phone calls, composing correspondence, and conducting research. They may also provide support for constituent casework and district-based projects.
requirements: unknown

title: UVU R.I.S.E Program
text: Utah Valley University's R.I.S.E program provides support for Utah high school students to gain college experience and mitigate the academic impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic. Admitted students engage in college-level coursework alongside success and career exploration workshops. These workshops aim to enhance students' academic performance in high school and facilitate their transition into higher education.
requirements: Utah high school students currently in grades 9th - 11th.

title: High School Community Service Internship Program
text: The Ocean County Historical Society's community service program offers high school students in grades nine through twelve the opportunity to support the organization's volunteers in various tasks essential to the smooth operation of its Museum and Research Center. Through this program, students gain insights into the multifaceted museum environment, including the history and preservation of the Elizabeth Sculthorpe Force House, its research center, adjacent structures, and surrounding grounds.
address: Ocean County Historical Society 26 Hadley Avenue Toms River
requirements: Applicants should have an interest in history or related disciplines, be willing to commit to hours during one school semester, and have a desire to expand their knowledge through a valuable community service project.

title: Student Internship
text: Jerome Home and Arbor Rose extend an invitation to high school students aged 16 and above, as well as college students seeking professional development in the healthcare field. The program caters specifically to undergraduate students pursuing degrees in human services, social work, recreation therapy, and music therapy. By providing hands-on experience and mentorship, Jerome Home and Arbor Rose aim to foster the growth and education of future healthcare professionals.
requirements: Must be at least 16 years old

title: Sugar Land SciTeen Program
text: The Sugar Land SciTeen Program fosters science education at the museum by empowering teen volunteers to lead interactive demonstrations and presentations that captivate visitors of all ages. Through this program, SciTeens acquire valuable skills that enrich their resumes, college applications, and future career prospects. Additionally, they engage in a vibrant learning environment where they forge friendships with fellow teens who share their passion for diverse areas of natural science. During the summer months, SciTeens immerse themselves in a comprehensive program that nurtures their scientific curiosity and provides them with opportunities for personal growth and professional development.
requirements: Commit to a minimum of 4 weeks of volunteering during the summer

title: The Mini Vet School
text: The Mini-Veterinary School is a comprehensive five-week lecture series presented by esteemed veterinary professionals. Each two-hour session delves into a specific subject taught in veterinary school, offering participants an immersive journey into the field. While graduates will not be eligible to practice veterinary medicine, they will gain invaluable insights into their pets' health. Upon completion of the 10-hour program, participants will receive a certificate acknowledging their acquisition of veterinary science knowledge.
address: Daemen University, 4380 Main Street, Amherst, NY
requirements: Application

title: Mayor's Youth Advisory Commission
text: The Mayor's Youth Advisory Commission (MYAC) serves as a liaison between the Mayor and City Council and the youth of the city, providing advice on youth-related matters and disseminating relevant information. Additionally, MYAC fosters civic engagement among youth by promoting education on citizen input, participation, and responsibility in local government. To ensure representation from all city schools, MYAC selects qualified and interested individuals from each middle and high school to fill Commission vacancies. These nominations are then submitted to the Mayor and City Council for approval.
address: Tempe Public Library, 3500 S. Rural Rd., Tempe
requirements: Must be residents of Tempe, AZ, who attend school in Tempe and are enrolled in grades 9-12

title: Internship Program
text: The Museum's internship program offers high school and college students from Fairfield County valuable opportunities to gain practical experience in museum administration and education. Each year, the Museum receives numerous internship requests, and its staff and volunteer educators generously contribute their time, guidance, and training to support interns' professional development. Through this program, interns acquire essential skills that prepare them for future careers in the museum field.

title: High School Summer Internships
text: Writopia Lab, a 501(c)3 nonprofit organization established in New York City in 2007, aims to cultivate joy, literacy, and critical thinking in children and teens from diverse backgrounds through creative writing. High school interns play a pivotal role as mentors, providing guidance and support to young writers aged six to nine through workshops, editorial assistance, and encouragement. The organization's mission is to foster a love of writing, enhance literacy skills, and encourage critical thinking in young minds.
address: 155 West 81st Street, Suite A, New York, NY 10024
requirements:

have taken at least one Writopia Lab 15-hour workshop within the past calendar year (trimester, school break, and summer workshops all qualify), and
commit to at least two week-long summer workshops or one trimester-long weekly workshop.

title: Hk Maker Lab
text: The Hk Maker Lab is an intensive six-week summer program designed to provide participants with a comprehensive foundation in design. With a focus on addressing health-related issues, participants will engage in the design, prototyping, and testing of biomedical devices. Additionally, they will develop associated business plans. The program culminates in a presentation to leading executives from the biomedical community. Projects developed during the Hk Maker Lab may be eligible for incubation at Harlem Biospace, utilizing its state-of-the-art facilities.
requirements:
Hk Maker Lab is committed to serving NYC high school students from low-income communities. The applicant must:
Attend a NYC high school during this academic school year
Note: Due to the rigor and demands of the program, preference will be given to rising juniors and seniors.

Demonstrate economic or educational disadvantage based on the below criteria:
a. Applicant attends a NYC high school with a Free and Reduced Price Lunch (FRPL) rate of 70% or higher
OR
b. Applicant family income qualifies for FRPL, Medicaid, SNAP, TANF, or other similar government aid but attends a NYC high school with a FRPL rate below 70% (you can check your school here). Documentation of Government aid qualification must be provided with application materials.

title: Black 14 Social Justice Summer Institute
text: The Black 14 Social Justice Summer Institute is a multi-day overnight program designed for rising junior and senior high school students. It offers an immersive experience where participants delve into contemporary issues affecting the Black community at various levels. The program aims to enhance college completion rates among Black students, addressing the disparity in six-year college completion rates between Black students (38%) and all college students (54.8%). The institute provides opportunities for curricular and co-curricular engagement, including campus living and dining experiences. Additionally, participants receive guidance on college admissions, registration, and financing, while also gaining exposure to the culture and environment of Wyoming.
requirements: No set requirements

title: Medill Cherubs
text: The Medill-Northwestern Journalism Institute (MNJI), also known as the "cherub program," is a prestigious five-week summer institute designed for rising high school seniors with a passion for journalism. This program provides an insider's perspective on the profession, offering students the opportunity to connect with like-minded peers and gain valuable insights into the field. MNJI is renowned for nurturing the talents of aspiring journalists, many of whom go on to become leading figures in the industry.
requirements: High school junior, strong academic standing, interest/experience in journalism

PAYS scholars participate in a range of activities throughout the academic year, aiming to matriculate into competitive institutions free of charge for their families. The program's multifaceted approach supports students from acceptance through graduation, ensuring their preparedness for higher education.

Through collaborative efforts, they conceptualize programs, organize activities, and promote young artists who are actively making a positive impact on the world. This internship empowers teens to take ownership of their community and utilize their creativity and passion to drive meaningful change.
requirements: This program is open to all NYC high school students, ages 14–19.

title: Wisconsin Maritime Museum Volunteer
text: This program provides high school students with the chance to delve into maritime history and museum operations through hands-on experience alongside professionals at the Wisconsin Maritime Museum. Participants will gain valuable insights into the preservation, interpretation, and presentation of maritime heritage. By working alongside museum staff, students will contribute to the museum's mission of educating the public about the significance of maritime history and its impact on the region and beyond.
requirements: No set requirements

title: Systems Thinkers in STEM Ambassadorship (STiSA)
text: Upon completing the 2-hour workshop, participants will be invited to join the 2023-2024 Systems Thinkers in STEM Ambassador Slack channel. This platform facilitates ongoing connections with the team and the current cohort of ambassadors. Through this channel, participants will receive updates on upcoming opportunities to enhance their systems thinking skills in STEM. These opportunities encompass a blend of virtual and in-person offerings, allowing participants to engage based on their interests and availability.
requirements: Sophomores and juniors in high school.

title: Senate Page Program
text: The North Carolina Senate Page Program offers high school students in grades 10-12 an immersive experience in the state's legislative process. Sponsored by senators, pages witness firsthand the creation of laws and assist senators and staff during the legislative session. Their duties include delivering messages, answering phones, distributing documents, and running errands within the legislative complex. The competitive selection process requires students to be in good academic standing and submit applications to their sponsoring senator. The program spans several weeks throughout the year, with pages receiving a $150 weekly stipend for expenses.
address: North Carolina Senate, Legislative Building, Room 1029, Raleigh, NC 27601-2808
requirements: To be considered for the North Carolina Senate Page Program, applicants must be in grades ten, eleven, or twelve and sponsored by a member of the North Carolina Senate. Applicants must also be in good academic standing at their school and have prior approval from their principal if serving as a page during the school year. The selection process is highly competitive, with senators recommending individuals to be appointed by the President Pro Tempore of the Senate on a first-come, first-served basis. Pages must be able to attend sessions from Monday afternoon to Thursday afternoon of their assigned week, work in appropriate business attire, and receive a stipend of $150 or thirty hours of community service. Pages are expected to participate in daily senate sessions, committee meetings, and provide office assistance. Lodging is not provided, and pages must cover their lunch and personal expenses. Only a limited number of parking spaces are available for self-commuting pages. Finally, Senate Pages are encouraged to be helpful, cordial, and polite, and to avoid wearing jeans, tennis shoes, or thong sandals (flip flops) while on duty.

title: The Mayor's Youth Employment Program
text: The Mayor's Youth Employment Program offers high school juniors and seniors in Stamford the opportunity to gain paid employment experience in the corporate, private, or non-profit sectors. This program provides students with access to real-world job opportunities that would otherwise be difficult to obtain. In addition to their work experience, students receive guidance and training from government employees, ensuring they develop the skills and knowledge necessary for success in the workplace.

title: Strong Future Las Vegas Youth Employment Program.
text: The Strong Future Las Vegas Youth Employment Program empowers young people in Las Vegas with workforce readiness training and employment opportunities. Through a comprehensive seven-session course, participants gain essential skills in resume writing, time management, interview techniques, ethics, and professionalism. Upon completion, youth are connected to summer or after-school jobs and receive ongoing support from adult advisors to foster commitment to both work and education. Employers are encouraged to hire or sponsor youth, contributing to workforce development and providing real-world experiential learning. The program aims to equip youth with valuable skills, connect them to the labor force, and support the economic growth of Las Vegas.
host: Mayor's Fund for Las Vegas Life
requirements: To be considered for the Strong Future Las Vegas Youth Employment Program, applicants must be at least 16 years old and be a resident of Las Vegas. The program offerings include a seven-session workforce readiness training program that provides youth with the skills needed in the workforce. The training includes topics such as resume writing, time management, interview techniques, ethics, and professionalism. The program offers summer and after-school jobs that provide experiential learning opportunities in a variety of industries. Also, the Mayor's Fund is seeking community partners to enhance the program offerings and experience, and businesses can hire and sponsor youth to work at their organizations. Applicants interested in employment opportunities should email strongfutureworks@lasvegasnevada.gov.

title: CSM Summer Academies
text: The College of Saint Mary offers Summer Academy Programs for young women of color in grades ten through twelve. Participants will receive a $500 scholarship to CSM, engage with a STEAM curriculum, meet professional women in the community, participate in cultural experiences, and reside in the residence halls. The academies also provide an opportunity to meet new friends and learn about the process of selecting and applying to colleges. The program runs for one week for each grade level and has a residential component. Space is limited to 30 participants for each week, and there is a $25 registration fee that can be waived. Applicants are required to complete an online application, submit a recent high school transcript, and write a 200-500 words essay about themselves and their interest in participating in the academies.
address: College of Saint Mary in Omaha, Nebraska.
requirements: To be considered for the CSM Summer Academies, applicants must be young women of color in grades 10 through 12. They must complete an online application prior to the deadline, upload a copy of their most recent high school transcript that includes one full academic year of grades, and submit an essay of 200-500 words that answers the prompt: "Tell us about yourself and why you are interested in participating in the academies". Throughout the week-long academies, participants will receive a $500 scholarship to CSM, learn from a STEAM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Art, and Math) curriculum, meet professional women in the community, participate in cultural experiences, and learn about the process of selecting and applying to colleges. There is a $25 registration fee for the entire week of classes and activities, but other costs including activities, transportation, and meals are fully covered by the College of Saint Mary. Applicants must also be prepared to live in the residence halls during the academies. There is space for 30 participants for each week, so applicants are encouraged to apply early for a chance to be accepted.

title: After School Matters
text: After School Matters, an internship program in Chicago, offers over 26,000 opportunities annually to over 18,000 teens. This program allows teens to work with skilled professionals, developing job skills and exploring rewarding careers. Guided by best practices, the program provides industry-specific, entry-level professional experiences with external organizations and companies for teens aged 16 and above. Successful completion of program requirements earns teens a monetary stipend. Eligibility criteria include Chicago residency, being 14 years old by the program's start date, and meeting specific age requirements for internships and assistantships.
requirements: To be considered for an internship program with After School Matters, there are several eligibility requirements. Firstly, applicants must be a resident of Chicago. Secondly, they must be at least 16 years old, and for certain positions, they may need to be at least 18 years old. Thirdly, applicants must have participated in at least three previous After School Matters programs. Fourthly, they must be eligible for employment and complete the required i9 and W4 forms. Lastly, applicants must be prepared for an interview/audition process, although not all programs may interview/audition all applicants. It is worth noting that the organization offers advanced internships, entry-level professional experiences with external organizations and companies, paying an hourly rate of $15/hour allowing teens to be exposed to various high-level career options.

title: Volunteer

title: Collegiate Seminar Program
text: The NYU Collegiate Seminar Program provides high school juniors the opportunity to experience college-level classes at a top-tier research university. Selected students will participate in one or more two-hour seminar-style classes taught by leading NYU faculty in a variety of academic subjects. These classes offer an immersive experience into the rigors of higher education, allowing students to engage with renowned professors and delve into challenging coursework.
requirements: The NYU Collegiate Seminar program is free to attend, and open to U.S. high school students who will be in the 11th grade in Fall 2022.

title: Teaching Assistant Program at the Santa Barbara Museum of Art
text: The Santa Barbara Museum of Art's Teaching Assistant Program offers a unique opportunity for 15-18-year-olds passionate about art and youth engagement. Young artists gain invaluable experience in art-making and education by assisting Teaching Artists in the classroom. Responsibilities include preparing materials, facilitating hands-on art activities, and mentoring children. The competitive program includes an orientation and mentorship, equipping participants with new art techniques, teaching skills, and a connection to the museum. The program runs from June 12 to August 4, providing a summer-long immersion in the world of art and education.
requirements: To be considered for the Teaching Assistant (TA) program at the Santa Barbara Museum of Art, applicants must be between 15-18 years old and interested in art and/or working with children. The positions are on a volunteer basis and count toward required community service hours. The TA's responsibilities include helping the Teaching Artist in the classroom, preparing materials, and assisting children with hands-on art-making. As role models for students and campers, they provide enthusiasm and create a fun environment for art learning. The program is competitive and includes an orientation and mentoring by Teaching Artists, allowing young artists to gain professional skills in art-making and art education. Interested applicants can apply for summer programs through the provided link or get in touch with the community program email or contact number for more information.

title: Teen Council, Teens Leading Change (TLC), and Teen Volunteer.
text: The Los Angeles Public Library provides ample opportunities for teens to engage in their local library through volunteerism. Additionally, Teen Council members have the chance to participate in Teens Leading Change projects, aiming to foster positive community impact. Teen Volunteers, aged 14-19, assist librarians in organizing the teen area, crafting library displays, and providing support as homework helpers or summer reading assistants. Participation in these programs grants community service hours and cultivates valuable skills in leadership, critical thinking, and civic engagement.
requirements: Must complete a Teen Volunteer Intake Form and have their parent or guardian sign a Teen Volunteer Waiver Form. Applicants must be between the ages of 14-19 to be eligible for the program. Internship opportunities vary depending on the location of the library and its current needs. Those selected for the Teen Council will have the opportunity to develop and participate in a civic action project, while Teen Volunteers will assist librarians with various tasks such as organizing the teen area, creating library displays, and assisting with summer reading programs. title: Physics in and Through Cosmology
text: The QuarkNet Workshop program is an annual workshop for high school physics teachers and students with an interest in STEM. The workshop provides an opportunity to delve into cutting-edge research in particle physics and cosmology through presentations by scientists and postdocs from Berkeley Lab. The program fosters a vibrant learning community that values diversity, equity, and inclusion. Discussions cover topics such as the search for dark matter, mapping the universe, measuring dark energy with supernovae, machine learning, and the Higgs boson. Students engage in small group interviews with lab scientists, presenting their findings in short videos or PowerPoint presentations. A highlight of the program is a discussion with Nobel Laureate Saul Perlmutter. Supported by QuarkNet, the workshop is offered free of charge to participants.
requirements: To be considered for the Physics in and Through Cosmology workshop, applicants must be high school physics teachers or highly motivated high school students with a keen interest in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM). The workshop is designed for an inclusive learning community that values diversity, equity, and inclusion. The workshop is free of cost for both the participating teachers and students. The workshop will be conducted remotely with teachers and presenters on zoom. Applicants can contact laurie.kerrigan2@gmail.com or apply directly through the provided link. The workshop offers an intense overview of cutting-edge research in particle physics and cosmology with presentations from Berkeley Lab scientists and postdocs. Finally, students form small groups and interview a lab scientist about the work they are doing, and they present a short video or power point about the scientist’s research.

title: InternNE
text: The InternNE program, established by the Nebraska Department of Economic Development, is a paid internship matching platform designed to facilitate connections between students seeking internship opportunities and employers within Nebraska. Students can register and create profiles to access a database of available internships that align with their qualifications. Employers can similarly create profiles and post internship positions they wish to fill with suitable candidates. The platform also provides internship grants to businesses interested in hosting interns. Whether you are a student seeking internship experiences or an employer seeking qualified interns in Nebraska, the InternNE program offers a streamlined and effective solution for finding the ideal internship match.
requirements: To be considered for the InternNE internship program, applicants must be students who are actively pursuing a degree or certification program at an accredited post-secondary institution, or have graduated from such an institution within twelve months of application. Applicants must also be able to provide proof of residency in Nebraska or attend school in Nebraska, and must have an available U.S. tax ID number. Successful applicants will need to undergo a background check and may be required to provide additional documentation, such as transcripts or letters of recommendation. Additionally, applicants must match with an employer who is listed on the InternNE website and has an available internship position that aligns with their career interests and academic background.

title: Summer Learning Institute (SLI)

Freedom House, a key component of SLI, fosters a college-bound mindset among students by facilitating service projects, college-immersion activities, and cultivating a growth mindset.

title: Summer Biomedical Internship Program
text: The Summer Biomedical Internship (SBI) program pairs high school students with faculty members engaged in research projects during the summer between their junior and senior years. Students collaborate daily with faculty, staff, and fellow SBI participants for 6-7 weeks. The program includes field trips to project sites, local hospitals, and medical facilities, as well as guest speaker presentations and discussions with residents. Through this immersive experience, students gain hands-on research experience, explore career paths in biomedical sciences, and develop their scientific knowledge and skills.
requirements: Must be at least 16 years of age, currently enrolled as a junior in high school, have a 3.0 or better grade point average, and Live in Fresno, Madera, Merced, Kings, Tulare or Mariposa Counties.

title: Health and Society Institute
text: This program delves into the intricate relationship between science, medicine, and the multifaceted experience of health and illness. Through epistemological inquiries, it examines the processes by which knowledge is acquired and established, shedding light not only on the definition and recognition of diseases but also on the power dynamics that shape these outcomes. Drawing upon historical and contemporary examples, the program critically analyzes the unequal distribution of benefits from scientific and medical advancements. It further explores the valuable tools offered by social scientists as potential interventions to address these disparities.
requirements: unknown

SAAMS students engage in interdisciplinary learning experiences that further their education and expose them to innovative approaches to these disciplines.

With an annual cohort of approximately 15-25 interns, the program aims to inspire and empower students to pursue their passions in physics, mathematics, computer science, and engineering.

title: Internship Opportunities
text: FPRI offers internships for students during the Summer, Fall, and Spring terms, providing an opportunity to engage with the foreign relations community and gain valuable experience within a prestigious think tank. Interns are paired with experts in the field, who guide them in developing industry-specific skills and enhancing general professional abilities such as communication, collaboration, critical thinking, and time management. FPRI values its relationships with former interns, maintaining connections long after their internship term.
