title: Genesys Works
text: The Genesys Works Student Internship program provides high school seniors with a unique opportunity to gain valuable business technology training and a paid internship with a major corporation. During an eight-week summer skills training program, students hone their professional skills in areas such as conflict resolution, communication, and business etiquette. Upon successful completion, they embark on a 20-hour per week paid internship, contributing as members of professional teams. The program also offers classroom instruction, individualized college and career counseling, and ongoing support through the Alumni Program to foster students' success in higher education and their careers. Participants earn between $10,000 and $15,000 while building an impressive resume and making a meaningful impact within major corporations.
requirements: Students must apply through the student application portal, which is available on the organization's website. Eligible candidates for this program must be high school students who are starting their senior year. Furthermore, applicants must be committed individuals who can balance schoolwork with a 20 hour per week internship. Students who are interested in this program must also possess a positive attitude and demonstrate a willingness to learn new skills. Additionally, applicants must attend a Genesys Works partner school or reside in the same community where their Genesys Works office is located. Finally, candidates must complete the eight-week summer Skills Training Program, which covers key aspects such as business etiquette, communication skills, and conflict resolution, to be accepted into the program's paid internship.

title: Today’s Interns, Tomorrow’s Professionals (TIP) Internship Program
text: Today's Interns, Tomorrow's Professionals (TIP) is the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston's paid work and learning internship program designed for eligible Boston Public Schools high school students who have completed their sophomore year. The program commences with a comprehensive summer work experience that incorporates job coaching and skill-building workshops. Subsequently, based on available openings and the individual's interest, effort, and performance, select students are chosen for an extended year-round internship program that can span up to three years.
requirements: Contact Dawn Hicks @ Dawn.D.Hicks@bos.frb.org for more information.

title: Clinical Internship Program
text: The High School Internship Program offered by Choice Physical Therapy provides juniors or seniors with an opportunity to explore the field of medical care for physical and occupational therapy. Under the supervision of the Clinical Manager or Practice Director, students observe and participate in day-to-day operations. The unpaid internship lasts 2-4 months, with hours ranging from 6 to 20 per week, accommodating student schedules. Eligible applicants have a GPA of 3.0 or above, an interest in a future medical field, and the physical and mental ability to perform major functions. Intern duties encompass clinical functions like preparing treatment spaces and assisting with patient care, developmental tasks like conducting research and creating clinical protocols, and administrative tasks like scheduling patient treatments.
requirements: The Clinical Internship Program at Choice Physical Therapy offers a unique opportunity for qualified high school juniors or seniors with a GPA of at least 3.0 who are interested in furthering their studies in the medical field. This program provides unpaid exposure, observation, and hands-on experience in physical therapy and occupational therapy under the direction of the Clinical Manager or Practice Director. The program lasts between 2-4 months depending on the student's school schedule, accommodating 6 to 20 hours per week. Applicants must also possess physical and mental abilities to perform the major functions required in the internship, computer literacy preferred, and willingness to learn computer skills required. The activities within the program include clinical functions, development, and administrative functions, depending on the student's capabilities. To learn more about the program or to apply, interested individuals can email Choice Physical Therapy at choiceptri@gmail.com.

title: Youth Volunteer Program
text: Audubon Nature Institute presents a rewarding and engaging volunteer program tailored specifically for young individuals. As Youth Volunteers, these dedicated individuals play a vital role in supporting Audubon's mission to celebrate the wonders of nature. They assist in various capacities, including providing guidance to visitors, engaging in educational activities, and contributing to the overall maintenance and upkeep of the institute's facilities. Through their involvement, Youth Volunteers gain valuable experience in environmental stewardship, wildlife conservation, and community engagement, while fostering a deep appreciation for the natural world.
requirements: Must be 14-17 years old

title: Tisch Future Artists
text: Future Artists is a comprehensive 14-week program designed for high school freshmen, sophomores, and juniors. Throughout the spring academic semester, students engage in full-day classes and workshops held on Saturdays. The program offers a diverse range of disciplines to choose from, including Dance, Photography, Dramatic Writing, and Recorded Music. This immersive experience provides aspiring artists with the opportunity to explore their creative potential and develop their skills in a supportive and enriching environment.
requirements: Eligible applicants will be high school students who are currently enrolled in the 9th, 10th, or 11th grade.

title: The Arete Internship Program
text: The Areté internship program offers three distinct pathways for high school students: Teaching, Arts, and STEM. These pathways provide opportunities for students to delve into potential career paths, hone their job readiness skills, and contribute to their school community through service. By participating in these internships, students gain valuable hands-on experience, develop essential job skills, and make meaningful contributions to the larger school environment.
requirements:
Current high school student at The Laboratory School of Finance and Technology or Walkabout Bronx High School.
Prior internship experience with Arete Education preferred
Arete supervisor recommendation to fall internship preferred
Effective written and verbal communication
Ability to:
manage time effectively
go the extra mile and/or try something new
be empathic and listen to others well
proactively identify and resolve problems
be polite, positive, and professional in all communications

title: Chicago Summer Business Institute Internship Program
text: CSBI pairs Chicago high school students with internships at prominent Chicago companies. This program aims to equip students with the necessary skills and connections to launch their careers as working professionals. Through these internships, students establish relationships with industry experts in diverse fields such as finance, law, government, and beyond. By providing access to these professionals, CSBI empowers students to gain valuable insights, develop their professional networks, and prepare for their future endeavors in the workforce.
requirements: Must be a resident of the City of Chicago. Must be a high school Sophomore or Junior. Must maintain a "B" or 3.0 GPA. Family household income must be below $80k/year.

title: City Council Summer Internship Program
text: The City of Irvine invites ambitious high school juniors and seniors, as well as current college students, to participate in the 2023 City Council Summer Internship Program. This program provides an exceptional opportunity for students with a civic-minded disposition to collaborate with City Councilmembers, conduct thorough research and analysis on diverse topics, and witness firsthand the operations of local government.
requirements: Must be a rising junior or senior with a minimum GPA of 3.3

title: Teenagers Exploring and Explaining Nature and Science (TEENS)
text: The Teenagers Exploring and Explaining Nature and Science (TEENS) program immerses participants in urban ecology and environmental science investigations. They explore the natural wonders within city parks, neighborhoods, and forest preserves, engaging in habitat restoration and ecological stewardship activities. TEENS contribute data to ongoing local, regional, and global research projects, while also developing their own research questions to investigate. Participants utilize smartphones for field data collection and create digital maps and data visualizations. Through hands-on scientific investigations, they gain insights into career paths in ecology, environmental science, and conservation.
requirements: Must be able to attend all program dates Age 14-19 Chicago high school student Chicago resident

title: Summer Intern Program
text: The Camden City School District Students Working to Access Greatness (SWAG) Program is a five-week summer youth employment program designed for middle and high school students residing in Camden City. The program's primary objective is to equip students with a fulfilling summer experience that fosters their preparation for future employment opportunities.
requirements:
Students must be between the ages of 14-19.
Students cannot be failing any core content courses required for graduation (i.e. English/Language Arts, Mathematics, Science, Social Studies, and Health/Physical Education).
All students accepted in the SWAG program must be available to work from the hours of 9:30am-3:00pm, Mon-Thurs., on their respective dates of employment

title: Science Squad
text: The Science Squad internship program at the Oregon Museum of Science and Industry (OMSI) offers teens the chance to hone essential soft skills like communication, leadership, and job readiness. Volunteers engage visitors in interactive science activities at the museum and receive weekly training on various topics. The program spans three sessions (Spring, Summer, Fall) and provides opportunities for continuing volunteers to mentor new ones and develop their science communication abilities by creating demonstrations or videos. The internship fosters curiosity in science while offering a rewarding experience for teenage volunteers.
host: Oregon Museum of Science and Industry
requirements: To be considered for the Science Squad guided volunteering program for teens at OMSI, applicants must apply before the deadline for the session that they are interested in volunteering for. Applicants should have a genuine interest in science and its many applications, as well as a desire to work with visitors of the museum. As part of the program, each applicant must attend trainings on communication, leadership, and job readiness skills. After the training, trainees are expected to lead interactive science demonstrations with museum visitors during their shifts. Applicants who continue with the program beyond the first session can mentor new volunteers, and participate in small group projects that enhance their science communication skills. The Spring, Summer and Fall sessions run once or twice a week on either Saturday or Sunday.

title: AI 4 All
text: Boston University AI4ALL is a three-week program designed to foster diversity and inclusivity in the field of Artificial Intelligence. It targets young women or those identifying as female in their sophomore or junior year of high school in the Boston area. The program immerses participants in AI exploration through collaborative team projects, industry field trips, and presentations from guest speakers. Upon completion, participants engage in a small group research project, culminating in a presentation for friends and family. BU AI4ALL is offered free of charge, with no application fee or tuition, but requires a non-refundable registration fee of $100 for accepted participants. As part of a national organization dedicated to nurturing future AI thinkers and fostering a diverse AI workforce, BU AI4ALL is supported by sponsors including AI4ALL, NSF, BU AIR, and BU Learning Resource Network.
requirements: To be considered for the Boston University AI4ALL program, applicants must be young women or identify as female and currently in their sophomore or junior year of high school in the Boston area. The program seeks to promote diversity and inclusion in the field of artificial intelligence. During the three-week program, participants will be engaged in various activities such as team projects, industry field trips, and presentations from guest speakers in a bid to learn about AI. Successful applicants are expected to pay a non-refundable $100 registration fee as there are no tuition fees or application charges. After the program, participants will present a small group research project to their friends and families. BU AI4ALL not only educates the next generation of AI thinkers but also aims to diversify the AI workforce.

title: Bloomberg Arts Internship
text: The Penn Museum Teen Summer Internship Program combines in-person and remote experiences for high school students. Interns attend the Penn Museum Mondays through Wednesdays, working alongside a specific department to acquire practical knowledge. On Thursdays and Fridays, they engage in professional development and college readiness workshops organized by the Bloomberg Arts Internship remotely. This hybrid format allows interns to gain hands-on experience at the museum while also developing essential skills for their future academic and professional endeavors.
requirements: Resume and application essays

title: T.E.A.M. Student Assistant
text: Arlington County's Department of Parks & Recreation (DPR) is seeking Temporary Part-Time T.E.A.M. Student Assistants for the summer camp program from March through September. These assistants will support all leaders in camp activities and operations, including duties related to various aspects of recreational programming.
host: Arlington County's Department of Parks & Recreation (DPR)
requirements: Must be currently enrolled in High School (between 14-18 years of age).  Applicants must be at least 14 years old to be hired.

title: Jr. Zoo Keeper Program
text: The Cape May County Zoo's Jr. Zookeeper program is a half-day program designed specifically for children between the ages of 10 and 15 who are interested in learning about the various aspects of zoo operations. This unique program provides participants with hands-on experiences and insights into the daily responsibilities of zookeepers, including animal care, feeding, enrichment, and habitat maintenance. Through interactive activities and guided tours, Jr. Zookeepers gain a comprehensive understanding of the zoo's mission, conservation efforts, and the importance of animal welfare.
address: 707 North Route 9 Cape May Court House New Jersey, 08210
requirements: unknown

title: Accounting and Information Management (AIM) Academy
text: The Accounting and Information Management (AIM) Academy is a six-day summer program tailored for underrepresented high school rising juniors aspiring to pursue careers in accounting and information management. The program offers workshops in accounting, finance, entrepreneurship, and professional development, led by university faculty and staff, providing students with direct engagement with business professionals. Additionally, team-building sessions and college readiness workshops foster connections among participants while equipping them with essential skills for higher education. Through this comprehensive and immersive experience, AIM Academy empowers students with the knowledge and abilities necessary to excel in their future business endeavors.
requirements: To be considered for the Accounting and Information Management (AIM) Academy internship program, applicants must be rising high school juniors who are from underrepresented communities. They should have an interest in pursuing a career in accounting, finance, entrepreneurship, or a related field, and be able to commit to attending the six-day summer program. The program is designed to be intensive, with students attending workshops taught by university faculty and staff in accounting, finance, entrepreneurship, and professional development. Additionally, participating students will engage in team-building activities, college readiness workshops, and interact with professionals in the business industry through sessions with industry leaders. To apply, students must submit an application form, a current transcript, a personal essay, and a letter of recommendation from a teacher or counselor.

title: High School Student Volunteers
text: The Cedars-Sinai High School Student Volunteer Program provides an immersive experience for students aged 14-18 aspiring to pursue healthcare careers. This year-round program, commencing March 1, 2023, offers clinical (patient care) or clerical (administrative) volunteer assignments. Students can engage with patients, healthcare professionals, and gain firsthand knowledge of the medical center's operations. The program requires a minimum of 100 hours of commitment, and participants must be enrolled in high school. To ensure safety, annual flu vaccinations, initial and annual health evaluations, and other requirements must be met.
requirements: To be considered for the high school student volunteer program at Cedars-Sinai, applicants must be between the ages of 14-17 and enrolled in high school. They must also submit an application, provide valid proof of COVID-19 vaccination, complete general volunteer orientation, receive initial and annual health evaluations and get an annual flu vaccine. In addition, they must commit to dedicating a certain number of hours each week to their volunteer assignment, typically four hours per week at a set day and time. Volunteers can choose between clinical or clerical assignments, but they will not perform research or assist medical personnel with procedures. Students who wish to gain experience in medical research should review the High School Students in Research Program. Applications are accepted year-round, and processing can take up to one month, so applicants should plan accordingly.

title: PUPP Scholars Program
text: The Princeton University Preparatory Program is a comprehensive, tuition-free college preparation and success initiative designed to empower historically marginalized students. This multi-year program provides holistic support, fostering the development of participants for admission to and success within selective colleges and universities. The program's mission extends beyond college preparation, aiming to equip students with the skills and knowledge necessary for ongoing success in higher education and beyond.
requirements: Students are selected to apply to become a PUPP Scholar during the spring of their freshmen year of high school. PUPP students must come from the following schools: Ewing High School, Lawrence High School, Nottingham High School (Hamilton, NJ), Princeton High School and Trenton Central High School.

title: Office of Internships
text: The Smithsonian Office of Internships offers high school students the chance to gain hands-on experience within the Smithsonian Institution, the world's largest museum, education, and research complex. Students can choose from a range of virtual, hybrid, and in-person internships at various museums, including the National Museum of Natural History, National Portrait Museum, and National Museum of the American Indian, among others. These internships provide opportunities for students to engage with museum professionals, contribute to ongoing research and educational initiatives, and gain valuable insights into the field of museum studies.
requirements: Varies by position

title: Student Internship Program
text: From the hallowed halls of Mark Twain's former residence, where the literary giant penned his transformative works, the Mark Twain House & Museum invites aspiring student interns to join the ongoing dialogue. As a hub for intellectual exploration, the museum seeks individuals who embody Twain's spirit of inquiry and engagement. Through internships, students have the opportunity to delve into the legacy of this American icon, contributing to the museum's mission of fostering a deeper understanding of our nation's history and identity.
requirements: unknown

title: Berkeley Lab K-12 - Director's Apprenticeship Program
text: The Berkeley Lab Director's Apprenticeship Program (BLDAP) is a STEM program designed for high school students in the Bay area, particularly in Alameda, San Francisco, and West Contra Costa counties. The program aims to develop 21st-century skills, provide insights into Berkeley Lab's research activities, offer college and career guidance, and foster a STEM network in a real-world work environment. Through project-based learning, hands-on projects, a computer science short course, and discussions with STEM professionals, BLDAP focuses on enhancing problem-solving, communication, and collaboration skills. The program seeks to reflect the racial demographics of the residential population and strongly encourages applications from underrepresented groups in STEM. Taking place in-person for six weeks during the summer, BLDAP provides college and career guidance, and facilitates the development of a STEM network in real-life work environments.
requirements: To be considered for the Berkeley Lab Director's Apprenticeship Program, applicants must be public school students in 10th or 11th grade in the Bay area, with a priority given to those in Alameda, San Francisco, and West Contra Costa counties who reflect the area's racial demographics. Students from underrepresented groups in STEM, including low-income households, first-generation college attendees, and Black, Indigenous, Latinx, and LGBTQ+ students, are highly encouraged to apply. Applicants must be available to travel to Berkeley Lab for a minimum of six weeks during the summer since this is a non-residential, in-person program. The program objective includes building STEM confidence and identity, cultivating interest in STEM activities and careers, and increasing exposure to STEM professionals, skillsets, and career paths. Successful applicants will participate in hands-on projects, attend weekly discussions with STEM professionals, and engage in a computer science short course. Participants who complete the summer program successfully will have the opportunity to participate in additional short courses, workshops, and special seminars at Berkeley Lab throughout the following fall and spring, while students in good standing before the next summer will receive an invitation to participate in a traditional laboratory internship. Applicants should visit the Berkeley Lab K-12 website to apply for the BLDAP.

title: SheTech Summer Internship Exploration program
text: The annual SheTech Summer Internship Exploration program provides high school girls with the opportunity to explore tech careers in Silicon Slopes companies alongside their peers. The 2023 program will feature a combination of in-person and virtual sessions over a two-week period, offering participants the chance to gain insights into the tech industry, connect with professionals, and discover potential internship opportunities.
requirements: High school students

title: Fresh Coast Ambassoder
text: The Fresh Coast Ambassador Program connects residents aged 15-23 within MMSD's service area, particularly those in the 30th Street Corridor and Kinnickinnic River neighborhoods, to careers in the water industry, watercourse concerns, and green infrastructure. The program fosters personal and professional growth through hands-on experiences in natural resource conservation, urban agriculture, green infrastructure, and trail maintenance. The curriculum aligns with Common Core Standards in English, history, social studies, science, and mathematics, as well as the National Green Infrastructure Certification Program established by the Water Environment Federation.
requirements: Must be 15-23 years old

title: Internship Program
text: The Poetry Society of New York, a non-profit organization, aims to revitalize poetry's significance in society. Internships at the organization offer tailored experiences based on individual interests, ranging from event planning and marketing to fundraising, editorial work, and more. As a small organization, interns are entrusted with substantial responsibilities, fostering lasting connections within the organization.
host: The Poetry Society of New York
requirements:
Hands-on mentality; self-motivated, intuitive, & independent worker
Strong artistic aesthetic & attention to detail
Ability to work remotely & during nonstandard business hours
Demonstrated familiarity with and enthusiasm for poetry, literature, theater, and performance art
Experience using Eventbrite, Canva, Mailchimp, Salesforce, Submittable, Squarespace, Quickbooks, Shopify, and/or Google Workspace

title: Teen Ambassador Program
text: Through an exclusive behind-the-scenes experience at the 9/11 Memorial & Museum, ambassadors delve into the Museum's artifacts, uncovering the ongoing themes and issues raised by the events of 9/11. This immersive exploration serves as the foundation for crafting artifact talks, empowering ambassadors with the knowledge and skills to effectively present these talks to diverse audiences.
requirements: unknown

title: ArtsWestchester Internship
text: ArtsWestchester provides internship opportunities in various specialized fields, offering valuable experience applicable to future careers. Interns develop skills in project management, public relations, professional writing, team collaboration, leadership, and responsibility. Current internship roles include Editorial Intern, Web Content and Database Intern, Grants & Government Relations Intern, Arts in Education Intern, Gallery/Exhibitions Intern, Development/Special Events Intern, and Human Resources Intern.
requirements:
Requirements for ArtsWestchester Internships: 
- Must be a High School Junior or Senior or currently enrolled in college or be a recent graduate (internships can be used for college credit)
- Minimum of 15 hours between 9am-5pm, Monday-Friday
- Must attend a mandatory virtual orientation  
- Must have a desire to learn about all aspects of arts administration

title: High School Internship Program in Integrated Mathematical Oncology
text: The High School Student Internship Program in Integrated Mathematical Oncology (HIP IMO) is an immersive 8-week summer program at the Moffitt Cancer Center in Tampa, Florida. Designed for high school students aged 16 or older, HIP IMO offers interdisciplinary team science research experiences to prepare aspiring scientists for careers in cancer research. Under the guidance of faculty and scientists in the Integrated Mathematical Oncology department, students engage in research projects tailored to their interests and abilities. HIP IMO provides access to necessary computer equipment and software throughout the internship. Selected students receive a $1,000 scholarship and are expected to attend daily from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. They gain oral presentation experience by delivering a 15-minute presentation to department members and guests at the HIP IMO research day and submit a three-page scientific report at the program's conclusion.
requirements: To be considered for the HIP IMO (High School Student Internship Program in Integrated Mathematical Oncology) program, applicants should be high school students aged 16 years or older by the time of the internship, interested in interdisciplinary cancer research careers, and have a keen interest in developing lifelong research skills. The program is designed for motivated students, and applicants should be able to commit to attending the program daily for eight weeks during traditional Hillsborough County public school summer break. Interested students should fill out an application form, which can be accessed either in Microsoft Word or PDF formats, on or before February 1, 2023. The completed applications should be emailed to hipimo@moffitt.org, and teachers should email letters of support by the same deadline to the same email. Notification of acceptance will be sent to applicants by end-February or early March 2023. All HIP IMO interns are subject to a drug screening, background check, and tuberculosis test (TB) before arrival at Moffitt as part of safety and security concerns. The program does not provide a stipend and is not capable of funding intern housing. Selected students will receive a $1,000 scholarship during the first week of HIP IMO.

title: University of Chicago Youth Internship Program
text: The University of Chicago Youth Internship Program is a paid summer employment opportunity for Chicago Public Schools high school students residing on the South Side. Spanning two summers, the program aims to equip students with valuable work experience, a robust peer network, and professional development opportunities. Weekly workshops, guest speakers, social-emotional learning seminars, career exploration activities, and college readiness and access programming are integral components of the program. The first summer emphasizes career and college awareness, exploration, and preparation, while the second summer culminates in a six-week direct internship within one of several University units in health sciences, computer sciences, or IT services.
requirements: To be considered for the UChicago Youth Internship Program, applicants should be motivated, hardworking students with an interest in health sciences, computer sciences, or IT services who want to explore career and college pathways after high school. They should be at least 16 years old by June 26, 2023, and authorized to work in the United States, and also attend a Chicago Public Schools high school and be a current sophomore or junior. Priority will be given to students with at least a 3.0 unweighted GPA who attend a CPS high school in the Office of Civic Engagement's nine-neighborhood focus area on the South Side. The internship program runs from June 26 - August 3, 2023, and interns are expected to work and attend programming Monday through Thursday, 10:00 a.m. – 4:00 p.m.

title: High School Summer Program in Biomedical Sciences
text: This 10-week program offers Texas high school seniors an immersive experience in the field of biomedical research. Under the mentorship of full-time faculty at MD Anderson Cancer Center in Houston, participants engage in a research project, gaining hands-on experience in a research environment. Additionally, they attend seminars covering a diverse range of research topics, providing insights into the various career opportunities available at the renowned cancer center.
host: Carl B. & Florence E. King Foundation
requirements: The program is open only to high school seniors in Texas interested in a career in an allied health discipline.

title: Internship Program
text: TDIndustries offers internship opportunities to high school students in the communities it serves, including San Antonio. Through these internships, students gain valuable insights into careers in the trades, expand their professional networks, and receive practical training in construction, manufacturing, and facilities management. This program provides a unique opportunity for high schoolers to explore potential career paths, develop their skills, and gain hands-on experience in the industry.
requirements: Able to work 40 hours (or more) per week

title: Teen Gallery Guide
text: Teen Gallery Guides at the Getty Villa offers a paid summer internship for Boyle Heights teens seeking to delve into the intersection of art and science. Interns will engage with ancient art, archaeology, art conservation, and scientific processes, developing strategies for interpreting objects within the Getty Villa's collection of ancient Greek and Roman art. They will acquire research methods, audience engagement techniques, and gallery teaching strategies to create and lead STEAM-focused interactive gallery experiences for school-aged visitors. Transportation to and from the Getty Villa is provided, along with a stipend.
requirements: Must be a Boyle Heights teen interested in exploring the connections between art and science, working in community with teen peers, building public speaking skills, and engaging with art professionals and museum spaces in unique ways.

title: Urban Ecology Teen Internship
text: Established in 2012, the Urban Ecology Teen Internship (Urban Eco-Teens) is a remunerated program for high school students, equipping them for higher education, environmental stewardship, and natural resource management careers. Interns collaborate with horticulturists and restoration experts from Van Cortlandt Park and NYC Parks, immersing themselves in the park's diverse flora and fauna. Through hands-on work, laboratory experiments, nature-oriented excursions, and interactions with professionals, they gain invaluable knowledge about local ecosystems, explore green career paths, and develop a deep understanding of the importance of environmental conservation.
address: 80 Van Cortlandt Park South Ste. E1 Bronx, NY 10463
requirements: Ideal applicants are rising Juniors and Seniors who are interested in learning about various green careers while completing hands-on restoration projects.

title: Summer Youth Employment Program
text: The CT Summer Youth Employment Program aims to offer early work experiences for youth aged 14-21 who may not have such opportunities otherwise. However, the program has limited availability, and completing an application does not guarantee placement.

14-21 years old as of July 1, 2023 Must reside or attend school in Meriden, CT

or Family Income within 185% of Poverty Income Levels

title: Brooklyn College Now STEM Research Academy
text: The STEM Research Academy is a two-semester program that combines a spring pre-college science course with a summer research experience under the guidance of CUNY faculty members. This program aims to enhance students' literacy and numeracy skills through hands-on research and authentic inquiry activities. By engaging in these activities, students gain valuable experience in scientific research and develop essential skills for success in STEM fields.

Be a NYC public high school sophomore or junior in good academic standing
CUNY Eligibility Benchmarks (75+ ELA Regents and/or 80+ Math Regents)
Primarily high school juniors

title: Art, Community, Education and Science Internship
text: The ACES internship offers students a unique opportunity to blend practical experience with informal STEAM education and artistic play. As interns, students support the Family Art Project, an intergenerational and multidisciplinary program designed to foster family bonding through nature-inspired art at Wave Hill. This program provides a platform for families to engage in creative activities that promote intergenerational connections and cultivate a love for the arts and nature.
requirements:
Must be enrolled in high school and 16 years old by July 5, 2023, and be eligible to work in the United States
Strong interest in arts and science education
Comfortable interacting with members of the public, including children
Regular weekend availability from 9:00AM–4:00PM
Available to participate for full 13 months, from June 2023 through June 2024

title: Student Leadership & Intern Program - CDC & EMS
text: Students will be assigned to the Department of Public Safety, where they will receive specialized training in either Emergency Medical Services (EMS) or the Consolidated 9-1-1 Center. This comprehensive training, provided at no cost, aims to equip students with the necessary skills for future employment within the agency. The program offers a paid part-time internship, providing students with practical experience and the opportunity to contribute to the community while preparing for a career in public safety.
address: 4045 Bridge View Dr, Charleston, South Carolina, 29405
requirements:
Students must:
Be Committed, Compassionate, Service-Focused, Accountable, Honest and Adaptable.
Be between the ages of 16-20, enrolled as a Junior (will be a rising Senior summer 2023) in a Charleston County Public High School, and a permanent resident of Charleston County.  Students will need to upload their most current school transcripts with the application as verification.
Be responsible in maintaining their grades and attendance throughout the school year. Students must not be on any type of Academic Probation.
Must follow all safety protocols.
Be a US citizen, permanent resident, or possess an Employment Authorization Document (EAD)
Not have any felony conviction(s); misdemeanor(s) will be evaluated on a case-by-case basis and disposition information must be provided.  
Be able to pass a background investigation including but not limited to a driving record, employment history, education, and reference check.

title: Wheaton College Summer Institute
text: The Wheaton College Summer Institute (WCSI) offers an exceptional pre-college experience for high-achieving high school students. Participants engage in rigorous academic study, artistic expression, and spiritual development under the guidance of renowned Christian faculty on the picturesque campus of Wheaton College. Students have the opportunity to earn college credit while immersing themselves in a vibrant community of like-minded peers. Beyond the classroom, WCSI provides a wealth of extracurricular activities, ensuring a well-rounded and enjoyable summer experience.
requirements: Currently a rising high school sophomore, junior, or senior Strong academic record (a transcript is required) Letter of recommendation Apply early to secure course selection Applicants should have their high school transcript sent to WCSI@wheaton.edu

title: Art Speak Internship
text: The Art Speak internship is a paid, ten-month experience from August to May for public high school students in grades 10-12. This internship offers exclusive opportunities and career training. Interns will explore Asian art and cultural traditions, learn from local artists and arts organizations, engage in social justice and youth activism, conduct informational interviews with museum staff to discover careers in the arts, and develop leadership skills by creating and facilitating hands-on art activities.
requirements: Bay Area public high school students in good standing in grades 10, 11, and 12

title: Internship
text: The Spare Parts Intern will gain practical experience in every stage of our second-hand store's operations. They will participate in the intake of materials, ensuring proper handling and organization. The intern will assist in processing donations, evaluating their condition and determining their value. They will contribute to sales floor merchandising, creating visually appealing displays that enhance customer engagement. Finally, the intern will participate in the checkout process, providing excellent customer service and ensuring smooth transactions.
requirements: If you meet the above criteria and wish to Intern at Spare Parts please submit a cover letter, resume and contact information for 3 references to hello@sparepartssa.org by the corresponding deadlines.

title: Volunteer at Denver Health
text: Volunteers play a crucial role in complementing the efforts of professional healthcare staff, allowing them to focus on providing optimal medical, nursing, and support services to patients. By supplementing the team, volunteers contribute invaluable qualities such as empathy, sensitivity, warmth, and friendliness, which enhance the patient experience during hospital stays or clinic visits. Their presence adds a human touch that eases the burden of illness and creates a more positive and supportive environment for those seeking medical care.
requirements:
Be 16 years of age or older
Commit to volunteering 4 hours consistently every week (Pet Therapy/Doula have different shifts, please inquire for details). Commit to 150 hours over a 12-month period. Attend an interview, orientation and additional trainings as needed.
Complete a multi-step medical clearance including a two-step TB test, flu shot and providing a copy of your immunization records.
Be able to successfully pass a background screening.

title: Sustainable Food Institute
text: Barnard's 2-Week Summer Food Institute immerses students in the complexities of the U.S. food system. Through hands-on experiences at farms across New York City and state, students delve into the interconnected aspects of food production, distribution, consumption, and waste management. The institute examines these topics through four lenses: agriculture, health, policy and justice, food systems and climate change, and soil health. By engaging with farmers and experts, students gain a comprehensive understanding of the challenges and opportunities facing our food system, fostering critical thinking and empowering them to make informed decisions about food and its impact on society and the environment.
requirements: This program is open to rising sophomores, juniors in seniors in highschool.

title: The Intern Project
text: The Intern Project, a program by the LA Promise Fund, offers paid internships to high school students in Los Angeles County. This program aims to provide work-based learning experiences that foster growth, connections, and industry exposure. By placing students with dynamic employers, the Intern Project supports their college aspirations and career readiness. With over 490 students placed, 100% have pursued higher education, and 95% are students of color. The program also serves as a talent pipeline for businesses, allowing them to invest in social impact and build a diverse future workforce. Supported by donors like the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation and the Walt Disney Company, the Intern Project empowers students and contributes to a more equitable and prosperous future.
requirements: Must be a high school student from Los Angeles County. They must also have a minimum 2.5 GPA and be at least 16 years old by the start of the internship. In addition to meeting these requirements, applicants must submit a completed application, including a personal statement, a resume, and two letters of recommendation from teachers or community leaders. The selection process involves a review of applications by a panel of community leaders and professionals, followed by an interview with finalists. Additionally, selected students and their families must attend an orientation session and comply with all program guidelines and expectations, including attending regular meetings and events. Ultimately, the program looks for students who are passionate and committed to learning and growing in a work-based setting, and who have a strong desire to succeed in college and beyond.

title: High School Student Worker

title: College Now STEM Research Academy

By engaging in practical research, students develop essential skills in scientific inquiry, critical thinking, and problem-solving, preparing them for future careers in STEM fields.

SEAP provides an immersive experience that allows students to explore the cutting-edge technologies and advancements shaping the future of the Navy while receiving invaluable mentorship from experts in their field.

From courses in mental health, coding, writing, and animal wellness to interactions with experts, unique travel and research experiences, and public speaking platforms, the academy offers a comprehensive curriculum. title: Chicago Philharmonic Paid Summer Internship
text: The Chicago Philharmonic's Community Engagement Programs strive to foster accessibility to classical music for all Chicagoans by bridging the gap between its orchestra and the community. These programs encompass a range of initiatives, including bringing music to public schools, hosting free concerts in public spaces, providing performance opportunities for young musicians, and offering mentoring programs for exceptional young musicians. The Side by Side with the Chicago Philharmonic program presents free symphonic concerts in local parks on the South and West sides. The AMP program embeds Chicago Philharmonic musicians in schools for six weeks, providing music lessons, side-by-side rehearsals and concerts, and technical guidance. The Families to the Phil program subsidizes symphonic concert tickets for students and their families from local public schools, community music schools, and youth orchestras. The Spotlight program offers professional performance opportunities to exceptional young musicians, while the NEXT! initiative showcases emerging musicians to Chicago Philharmonic patrons, musicians, and conductors. Finally, the Chicago Philharmonic Paid Summer Internship provides mentorship and training in arts administration and musical performance to four high school students each summer.
requirements: To apply for the Chicago Philharmonic Paid Summer Internship, high school students from Chicago must complete an online application form and submit their resume along with a cover letter describing their interest in the program, their past experiences, and how they hope to grow as an arts administrator. In addition, applicants must include a letter of recommendation from a teacher, guidance counselor, or community leader. The internship program seeks to provide students with hands-on experience in various areas of arts administration, including marketing, community engagement, and operational support. Furthermore, interns will receive mentorship from professionals in the field and have a musical performance element guided by Chicago Philharmonic musicians. Successful candidates will have excellent organizational skills, strong attention to detail, and a passion for classical music and community engagement.

requirements: Must be 18 years or older, excellent communication skills and customer service skills. Knowledge of Chicago and the Loop, arts and events. Generally able to volunteer 6 – 12 hours per month. Must be reliable and on time. Basic computer knowledge and access to email

title: Citywide Youth Council
text: Citywide Youth Councils (CYCs) empower current 9th-11th graders to actively participate in shaping city policy. Each council comprises 25-30 diverse youth from across the city who engage in team building, leadership development, research, and the formulation of policy proposals. These proposals are then presented to key decision-makers in city government. CYCs provide a platform for youth to contribute to the development, implementation, and evaluation of public policy. Currently, recruitment is underway for the Juvenile Justice Council (JJC), CPS Student Advisory Council (SAC), Teen Health Council (THC), and Youth Safety Advisory Council (YSAC).
requirements: Must be in 9-11 grade

title: High School Summer Volunteer Program at Children's Hospital Los Angeles.
text: Participants will contribute to the hospital's mission of fostering hope and healthier futures by serving patients, families, and staff throughout the facility. They will engage in various volunteer opportunities, including providing administrative support, welcoming patients upon their arrival, guiding them to their appointments, and distributing developmentally appropriate gifts to patients.
address: Children's Hospital Los Angeles in California.
requirements: Completed their freshman year of high school and must be between 15-17 years of age by June 15, 2023. Applicants must be eligible to commit to serving 15 hours per week in four different solid blocks of time and complete a minimum of 105 service hours in the period from June 19, 2023 to August 4, 2023. Volunteer opportunities do not include job shadowing or internship experiences, and do not involve contact with inpatients except for very limited interactions. Applicants must participate in a personal virtual interview with CHLA Volunteer Resources team members accompanied by a parent or guardian, and must be accompanied by a parent or guardian for a health screening and submission of full immunization records, two negative TB tests from within the past year, and drug and alcohol screening clearance. Applicants must also provide proof of full Covid vaccination (including Covid Boosters) and attend a mandatory orientation on Sunday, June 11, 2023, prior to starting volunteer service on the week of June 19, 2023. The application process consists of completing an application form, providing basic demographic information and essay responses, and submitting two teacher/counselor/coach/mentor recommendations.

title: GROW: Greater Boston Research Opportunities for Young Women.
text: The Greater Boston Research Opportunities for Young Women (GROW) program, offered by Boston University, provides a six-week research internship opportunity for young women entering their senior year of high school in Fall 2023. Eligible participants must reside in Massachusetts and attend school within 30 miles of Boston. The program offers hands-on research experience in a lab setting from 9:30-4:30 (M-F), allowing participants to engage in cutting-edge research and collaborate with professionals. Participants will gain valuable knowledge in best research practices, attend guest speaker sessions, and develop communication skills through a culminating symposium where they present their research findings. Upon successful completion of the program, participants will receive a stipend of $1500. The program runs from July 5-August 11, and applications must be submitted by April 15, 2023.
requirements: The GROW (Greater Boston Research Opportunities for Young Women) internship program is designed for young women who will be entering their senior year in Fall 2023. To be considered for this program, applicants must live in Massachusetts and attend school within 30 miles of Boston. The application deadline is April 15, 2023. The program runs for six weeks, from July 5 to August 11, and participants are required to attend an orientation on June 28-29. Participants will work in research labs at Boston University from 9:30 AM to 4:30 PM, Monday through Friday. They will have the opportunity to learn about best research practices, hear from guest speakers, and develop communication skills by presenting their research at a culminating symposium. Upon successful completion of the program requirements, participants will receive a stipend of $1500. For more information and to apply, applicants should visit the program's website.

title: Lead Guide (Educator)
text: Since 2004, Trackers Earth and its Guides have embarked on adventures with children and their extended families. Through stewardship and enduring outdoor skills, they impart the Arts of Tracking. They are committed to fostering opportunities by honoring the diverse backgrounds and values of all participants. Their mission is to expand accessibility to these experiences for families. They define themselves by their profound connection to the natural world, multi-generational nature, and the principles gleaned from moments of solitude in the forest.
requirements:
Completed Vaccinations for COVID-19 (verification required)
Enthusiasm for Trackers and its programs. 16 years & up
Can exercise discretion and independent judgment in remote locations
Interest in developing and sharing outdoor skills with youth
Can adapt to changing logistics and collaborate on solutions in a calm, positive way
Capacity and enthusiasm to learn and teach wilderness skills and techniques
Model professionalism while supporting youth, families, colleagues, and supervisors
Can stand, bend, squat, climb, lift (up to 50 lbs), hike on and off trail (up to 5 miles) per day
For Lead Guides ages 18+ Trackers will complete pre-employment criminal background & references checks
Lead Guides need the following certifications (or able to complete before starting):
CPR/First Aid/Anaphylaxis & Epinephrine Auto-Injector
Food Handlers
(ages 18+) Recognizing & Reporting Child Abuse & Neglect (OR & WA)
(ages 18+) Child Abuse Mandated Reporter Training - General (Oregon)
State fishing license if guiding a program that includes fishing

title: High School Internships
text: The University of Nebraska at Omaha College of Information Science & Technology's Summer High School Internship Program offers an immersive experience in our state-of-the-art labs. Under the guidance of faculty and students, interns delve into cutting-edge fields such as robotics, bioinformatics, software engineering, cybersecurity, public health informatics, database-driven web development, IT innovation, open community participation research, music informatics, iOS/Android app development, and gaming. Supported by a grant from the Bill and Ruth Scott Foundation, the program fosters a hands-on approach to scientific research and development, enabling interns to explore potential careers in IT, acquire new skills, and contribute to real-world problem-solving.
requirements:
High school students interested in math, science, performing arts and/or computer science from participating school districts are eligible to apply. Eligible students must meet the following criteria:

Be entering 10th, 11th, or 12th grade Fall of 2023
Have completed and attained at least a "B" in Algebra I
Obtain parental/guardian consent for participation
Have a weighted GPA of 3.25 or higher (3.00 unweighted GPA or higher)
Be able to provide their own reliable transportation to UNO each morning

title: JA Job Shadow Blended
text: Junior Achievement's Job Shadow Blended Internship Program empowers high school students to explore their career aspirations. Through a career assessment survey, students uncover their strengths, passions, and potential career paths. Informational interviews with professionals refine their options, leading to the identification of top career choices. The program culminates in a workplace visit and job shadowing experience, providing hands-on exposure to various industries. Reflection and analysis are integral to the program, complemented by career-planning tools that enhance students' networking, interviewing, and online profile skills. JA teachers and volunteers can seamlessly integrate the program into classroom-based, remote live, or after-school settings, ensuring flexibility and adaptability to local needs.
requirements: To be considered for the JA Job Shadow Blended program, applicants must be high school students in grades 9-12. The program can be implemented as a classroom-based, remote live, or after-school program. It consists of six 45-minute sessions and two opportunities for site visits, with flexible implementation options depending on local needs. Students will need to participate in career interest assessments, informational interviews, and a multi-hour job shadow experience in a career area of interest. The program also includes extensive self-guided learning experiences and current career-planning tools to enhance networking skills, interview skills, and online profiles. JA teachers and volunteers are encouraged to use the resources available in JA Connect Learning Pathways for this program. Finally, students will need to learn the design-thinking approach, explore their top three career choices, create an elevator pitch, write a professional thank-you note, and research potential employers.

title: Lancaster Performing Arts Center Volunteer
text: Volunteering at the Lancaster Performing Arts Center (LPAC) empowers you to make a meaningful contribution to your community while fostering your passion for the arts. By joining the LPAC volunteer team, you play a vital role in sustaining the Center's mission of enriching cultural life in the Antelope Valley. Through diverse volunteer opportunities, you assist in arts education initiatives, ensuring that the Center continues to provide transformative experiences that nurture creativity, inspire learning, and connect people through the power of the arts.
requirements: Contact for Requirements. Background check required.

title: Summer Volunteer Program
text: High school volunteers play a crucial role at the Houston Museum of Science, assisting teachers and engaging with campers during the Museum's Summer Science Camp classes. Additionally, select volunteers receive training to deliver exhibit hall presentations to visitors, utilizing the Museum's collection of specimens and artifacts. Through their involvement, participants develop valuable skills that enhance their resumes and expand their network of peers who share their passion for science.
requirements: First year Ecoteens commit to volunteer for one two-week session

title: Athena Summer Innovation Institute
text: At Athena, entrepreneurship is recognized as a transformative force for shaping a desirable future. Our approach emphasizes creativity, collaboration, and a deep awareness of the impact on both individuals and society. The Athena Summer Innovation Institute is an intensive three-week boot camp designed specifically for young women. This program equips participants with practical skills and knowledge to cultivate ideas that have the potential to create meaningful change in the world.
requirements: Participants in the Athena Summer Innovation Institute should be creative, motivated young women who have an entrepreneurial spirit. You don’t need to have a business idea (in fact, it’s good if you come in with a clean slate!), but you should be interested in developing ideas for products, services, and experiences that have the potential to challenge the status quo and create social good. You should be genuinely enthusiastic about working collaboratively to learn more about the startup journey and what it takes to be a member of a founding team.

title: The Introductory College Level Experience in Microbiology
text: The iCLEM program is a paid summer science intensive designed for economically disadvantaged high school sophomores and juniors. The program aims to expand students' knowledge of biotechnology, microbiology, and biofuels, as well as introduce them to career exploration and preparation for the college application process. Students will complete a research project in a modern laboratory setting mentored by JBEI researchers and UC undergrads. The program will be hybrid in format, with in-person instruction at the Emeryville, CA laboratory 2-3 days a week and remote instruction on other days. Participants will receive a stipend of $3,000, and they will also have opportunities to learn about college admission requirements and financial aid, and to explore careers through discussions with STEM professionals and visits to local biotechnology and pharmaceutical companies. To apply, students must meet eligibility requirements and submit a transcript, personal statement, "Why are you applying for iCLEM" statement, and a teacher's letter of reference.
requirements: To be considered for the iCLEM internship program, applicants must meet the following requirements: (1) be at least 15 years old by December 31, 2022, (2) be a currently enrolled sophomore or junior at a high school located in Alameda, Contra Costa, or San Francisco County, (3) be a US citizen, permanent resident, or DACA recipient, (4) have a GPA of at least 2.5 and have passed Algebra 1 and Biology, (5) have an annual household income of less than $104,445 in Alameda County, $100,780 in Contra Costa County, or $122,565 in San Francisco County, with possible additions to the income limitations for larger families, and (6) be able to commit to attending the program from June 20, 2023, to July 28, 2023. In addition, applicants must submit a current transcript, a personal statement describing their life goals and background, a statement detailing why they are a good fit for the iCLEM program, and the name and email address of a teacher willing to provide a letter of reference upon request. The application process is highly competitive and rigorous, with emphasis placed on a student's background, teacher recommendations, and desire to do science and work hard during the summer.

title: Crew Member
text: The Green Heart Project's Youth Internship Program offers high school students a unique opportunity to gain valuable experience and contribute to their community. As a Crew Member, interns will assist with farm maintenance and produce sales at the organization's pay-what-you-can farmer's market. They will also participate in educational lessons that explore the interconnectedness of food, health, culture, and the environment. Through hands-on experience on an urban farm that serves as an outdoor classroom and learning laboratory, interns will develop career preparedness and healthy living skills while fostering engaged citizenship.
requirements:
Be 15- 19 years of age by June 12, 2023
Have completed 9th grade
Available to work over the summer during the 8-week program 
Answer all questions on the Internship Application
Provide contact information for two personal or professional references: teacher, employer, coach, counselor, mentor, minister, other (this cannot be a family member) 
Complete an interview with Green Heart
Applicants who have completed an application and provided references by March 31st, 2023 will be interviewed and considered for the position

title: Greehey CCRI Donald G McEwen Memorial Summer Research Program
text: This ten-week summer program immerses high school students in the realm of children's cancer research. Participants delve into the fundamentals of basic science and translational research, gaining hands-on experience in genomics, proteomics, bioinformatics, structural biology, classical genetics, and molecular imaging. Through this comprehensive program, students acquire a deep understanding of the methodologies employed in these fields, fostering their interest in pursuing careers in cancer research and related disciplines.
host: The University of Texas Health Science Center at San Antonio
requirements: unknown

title: High School Initiative in Remote Sensing of the Earth Systems Science  & Engineering (HIRES)
text: Through a grant from the Pinkerton Foundation, HIRES offers an advanced STEM research opportunity to New York City students who lack access to high-quality STEM education experiences. Students from demographic groups traditionally underrepresented in STEM fields, such as women, students of color, and those from low-income backgrounds, are particularly encouraged to apply. This program aims to provide these students with the opportunity to engage in cutting-edge STEM research, fostering their interest and skills in these disciplines.

title: Internships and Volunteer Programs

This process enables students seeking municipal government experience to submit their profiles, which are then stored in a pool of pre-qualified candidates. This pool allows DHR to consider these candidates for available positions, providing students with a valuable opportunity to gain hands-on experience in local government.

title: Learning Intern
text: The Learning Intern will provide support for collaborative learning and social innovation initiatives within the LA Phil's Learning Department. They will assist Learning Department Managers and contribute to the daily operations of Learning programs, particularly focusing on administrative responsibilities related to local Youth Orchestra LA (YOLA) sites. Upon completion of the internship, the intern will have gained familiarity with the operations of a Learning department in a major orchestra, developed proficiency in working efficiently within the fast-paced environment of the performing arts, and honed their ability to prioritize and adapt to a rapidly evolving landscape.
