title: Ronald Reagan Presidential Library and Museum Docent
text: Under the guidance of the Volunteer Program Coordinator, the candidate will be responsible for delivering exceptional service to guests, working a four-hour shift per week, leading tours, staffing museum stations, and completing a series of training classes. A routine background check and fingerprinting are mandatory requirements for this role.
host: Ronald Reagan Presidential Library and Museum
requirements: All candidates (students, retirees, and working adults) are encouraged to apply, however you must be at least 16 years of age. No education is necessary, just a desire to learn and share the legacy of President Reagan. Public speaking and previous working experience in a museum setting is not required.

title: Summer Anatomy Program
text: This intensive scholarly program offers a unique opportunity to delve into the art of anatomical dissection, providing hands-on experience for undergraduate, gap year, and graduate students, as well as high school students who have completed their junior year and are at least 16 years old. Regular attendance and a weekly time commitment are essential for this program, which aims to equip participants with a comprehensive understanding of human anatomy through practical dissection.
requirements: At least 16 years old, rising junior

title: PROMISE Scholars Summer Internship
text: The High School Research Scholars Program at Sanford Research provides a transformative 10-week summer internship for highly motivated high school students passionate about biomedical sciences. Interns collaborate with scientists as integral members of research teams, gaining hands-on laboratory experience. They participate in educational and career development workshops, culminating in the presentation of their research findings at the Sanford Research Symposium. Additionally, participants earn three undergraduate elective credits from the University of South Dakota (BIOC192) and receive a $2,500 scholarship, further supporting their academic and professional aspirations in the field.
requirements: Applicants must be entering their senior year in the upcoming academic school year, be at least 16 years old by June 1, and must commit to participating in the entire program, working a minimum of 35 hours per week. The program requires applicants to submit a project proposal before the start of the program and present their research results in a symposium at the end of the program. Candidates are also encouraged to participate in other Sanford PROMISE programming such as Research Shadowing Program, Teen Science Café, and Community Lecture Series. Students who are accepted into the program receive a $2,500 scholarship and earn 3 undergraduate elective credits at the University of South Dakota.

title: Los Angeles County Student Election Worker Program
text: The Los Angeles County Student Election Worker Program provides high school students with the opportunity to serve as Election Workers in county elections. Participants receive compensation for their service and gain practical experience in the democratic process. The program fosters civic engagement and provides students with a firsthand understanding of the electoral system, empowering them to contribute to their community and make informed decisions about their future.
requirements: Students must meet specific requirements to participate in this program, such as being at least 16 years old by the time of the election, attending a public or private secondary education institution (High School), being a U.S. citizen or legal permanent resident (Green Card Holder) of the United States, having a good academic standing (G.P.A. of 2.5 or greater), and having teacher and parental consent. Additionally, students must be fully vaccinated from Covid-19 and provide proof of vaccination. Participants in this program receive a stipend for their service and get a hands-on introduction to the democratic process. Moreover, they have an opportunity to earn community service/service learning credits and $100 for each day served at the Vote Center, as well as $80 for attending Election Worker training.

title: ESTEEM Summer Academy
text: High school students will delve into college resources and explore burgeoning careers in analytics, bioinformatics, data science, and forensics. They will embark on visits to the Oklahoma Bureau of Investigation, Fusion Center, and Edmond Police, where STEM professionals will provide job shadowing, internship opportunities, and demonstrations of how analytics aids in solving contemporary crimes and environmental challenges. Students will engage in hands-on activities utilizing cutting-edge technologies such as AI, blockchain, ChatGPT, machine learning, and the metaverse, fostering fun and intellectually stimulating experiences.
requirements: Students must be in grades 9-12

title: Summer Operations Intern
text: Galileo's operations rely heavily on Summer Operations Interns, whose adaptability and problem-solving skills are essential for the camp's success. This role demands a positive and proactive mindset, a willingness to take initiative, and a strong commitment to providing exceptional service. Interns must be able to seamlessly transition between tasks on a moment's notice, demonstrating flexibility and a keen eye for detail. This seasonal, part-time position operates Monday through Friday, requiring a dedicated and reliable individual who can contribute to the smooth and efficient functioning of the camp.
requirements: Must be at least 16 years of age by May 26, 2023

title: Junior Conservation Technician Program
text: The Junior Conservation Technician (JCT) Program offers paid opportunities for teens aged 14-18 to delve into the realm of conservation through practical field experiences at the Green Mountain Audubon Center. Mentored by the Youth Leadership Coordinator, JCTs collaborate with Vermont conservation professionals, including foresters, wildlife biologists, environmental educators, ornithologists, and naturalists. This program aims to provide professional learning experiences in conservation for teens, nurturing their passion and fostering the next generation of conservationists.
requirements: Must be 14-17 years old.

title: Teen Arts Council
text: The Teen Arts Council (TAC) program at the Museum of Fine Arts Boston offers Boston-area high school students the opportunity to immerse themselves in art, history, and culture while honing professional skills such as teamwork and workplace engagement. Through tours, workshops, performances, and a culminating Teen Night social event, participants gain insights into potential career paths and professional opportunities. The program also provides a platform for students to advise the MFA on engagement strategies for local teens. Open to rising juniors and seniors in Boston Public Schools or Boston, the TAC program is supported by various foundations and accepts applications on a rolling basis.
requirements: To be considered for the Teen Arts Council (TAC) at the Museum of Fine Arts Boston, applicants must be rising juniors or seniors who either attend a Boston public school and/or live in the city of Boston itself. Applications are evaluated on a rolling basis and must be submitted to teens@mfa.org. Those selected for TAC will work to develop outreach and engagement strategies for the MFA to connect with local teens while learning about a range of professional options and career paths within the arts and cultural sector. Activities will include teen-led tours, workshops and talks with visiting artists, performance events, and Teen Night, an end-of-year celebration hosted by the TAC. Various foundations, endowments, and charitable trusts support the program.

title: Summer Earn and Learn Program
text: The Summer Earn & Learn Program, a statewide initiative, provides work readiness training and paid work experience for students with disabilities aged 14-22. Through a partnership between Workforce Solutions for North Central Texas and Texas Workforce Commission-Vocational Rehabilitation Services, the program offers employability skills training, paid work experience, and reasonable accommodations tailored to each student's needs. Participating employers, who receive orientation prior to placement, play a crucial role in providing these accommodations. The program aims to create pathways to employment, with over 5,000 students statewide (769 within the WSNCT service area) having participated and worked in various positions. Eligible students must have an Individualized Education Plan or 504 Plan, while employers interested in participating can express their interest through the Employer Interest Form.
host: Summer Earn & Learn Program is Workforce Solutions for North Central Texas
requirements: To be considered for the Summer Earn & Learn program, eligible applicants must have an individualized education plan or a 504 plan, must be between the ages of 14 and 22 years old, and must be less than 22 years old as of September 1, 2022. Participants will receive workplace readiness training to prepare them for successful employment and will have the opportunity to build their skills and identify future career goals through paid work experience. Participating employers will cover wages and workers' compensation insurance, and will provide reasonable accommodations required by the student. Employers will also receive an orientation prior to placement. To participate, eligible students can contact the Texas Workforce Vocational Rehabilitation Counselor assigned to their school or call Rosla Hocker at (817) 436-4127 for additional information.

title: City Tech College Now STEM Research Academy
text: The STEM Research Academy is a two-semester program that offers high school students the chance to enhance their literacy and numeracy skills through hands-on research experiences. The program consists of a pre-college science course in the spring semester, followed by a summer research experience where students collaborate with CUNY faculty members on authentic inquiry projects. This immersive program is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in STEM disciplines and foster their critical thinking, problem-solving, and communication abilities.
requirements:
Must be a NYC public school sophomore or junior
Must have an overall high school average of 80+
English scores/grades: ELA Regents 75+ or SAT Verbal/Critical Reading 480+
80+ on Living Environment Regents
80+ on any, one Math Regents
Passed all other required math, science and history regents exams taken so far

title: Summer Internship Program
text: The Brooklyn Navy Yard Development Corporation's Internship Program offers graduating college-attending or college-bound students a gateway to diverse work experiences within the Brooklyn Navy Yard. Interns are matched with Yard-based businesses or BNYDC departments that align with their career aspirations, skillsets, and educational background. This program provides students with hands-on opportunities to explore their interests, develop professional skills, and gain valuable experience in a dynamic and innovative environment.
requirements: unknown

title: NASA Internships
text: The NASA Internships, facilitated by the Michigan Space Grant Consortium, provide immersive experiences for individuals at various academic levels (high school, undergraduate, graduate) and educators to delve into NASA-related research and operational endeavors. Participants engage in scientific or engineering research, development, and operations, or explore non-technical internships supporting NASA's administrative and business processes. These mentor-guided internships aim to enhance participants' professional capabilities and career aspirations through real-time, degree-related experiences. Internships can be conducted full- or part-time at NASA facilities, contractor facilities, or any location contributing to NASA's missions. Mentors include civil servants, contractors, or faculty involved in activities directly related to NASA's assets and ongoing missions. Applications are accepted for four sessions annually, aligning with the academic calendar: spring, summer, fall, and year-long.
requirements: To be considered for the NASA internship program, applicants should be a high school, undergraduate or graduate student or an educator with relevant background or interest in science, technology, engineering and math (STEM) fields. This educational hands-on opportunity offers unique NASA-related research and operational experiences with different NASA centers across the United States. Participants are mentored by career professionals who provides guidance in related degree-related scientific or engineering research, development, and operations activities. Internship participants have the opportunity to engage in a scientific or engineering research project with NASA, while non-technical internship opportunities are also available to engage in administrative and professional activities. Internship sessions correspond to the academic calendar, comprising spring, summer, fall, and year-long internships. Applicants who are interested in participating in the program should apply early as some internships are funded within the centers, requiring outside funding through the Space Grant Consortia or may be available as a Pathways Intern, only introduced to positions to full-time employment upon graduation.

title: Student Public Health Ambassador Program
text: The LA County Department of Public Health's Parent and Student Ambassador Programs empower community members to become advocates for public health by providing virtual training sessions in English and Spanish. These sessions equip ambassadors with knowledge on COVID-19 and emerging virus prevention, mental health support, vaccination access, wellness clinics, mindfulness applications, and youth substance abuse prevention. Certified ambassadors share this information with their peers, promoting community health and wellness by disseminating resources and raising awareness about these crucial topics.
host: LA County Department of Public Health
requirements: To be considered for the Parent and Student Public Health Ambassador Program, applicants must register for and attend a once monthly, 60-90-minute virtual training session offered in English and Spanish. The training is focused on COVID-19 and emergent virus prevention and mitigation, mental health and self-care support, and access to Los Angeles County Department of Public Health and other resources including information about and access to vaccinations, wellness clinics, virtual mindfulness applications, and youth substance abuse prevention. Upon completion of the training, participants will receive a training certificate

title: The Ranger Conservation Corps Internship
text: The Ranger Conservation Corps offers an exceptional urban environmental internship opportunity for high school students with a passion for the natural world and environmental concerns. Interns collaborate with Urban Park Rangers to engage in environmental restoration projects within the natural areas of our renowned parks. Through this experience, they gain invaluable hands-on knowledge and contribute to the preservation and enhancement of these urban green spaces.
host: New York City Department of Parks & Recreation
requirements: unknown

title: High School Alliance
text: The High School Alliance Internship Program is a competitive, year-long program designed for high school juniors and seniors aspiring to pursue careers in medicine, nursing, or other healthcare fields. The program offers various courses during the fall and spring semesters, including biology, healthcare communications, medical terminology, anatomy, and physiology. To be eligible, students must be 16 years old, have a grade of "B" or above in Algebra, Biology, and a physical science course, and be enrolled in a participating high school for the entire school year. Only 65 students are accepted each year, making admission highly competitive. Eligible students must complete an in-person interview and obtain parent/guardian permission. For those who do not meet the eligibility criteria, uBEATS, an online program, is available.
host: High School Alliance program of the University of Nebraska Medical Center (UNMC) and Nebraska Medicine
requirements: To be considered for the High School Alliance internship program at the University of Nebraska Medical Center, applicants must meet certain eligibility requirements. Students must be at least 16 years of age, be a junior or senior in high school, and be enrolled in a participating school district for the entire year. In addition, they must have completed and received a grade of "B" or above in Algebra 1, Biology, and a physical science course, as well as a third year of science. They must have parent or guardian permission to apply, and must be on track for graduation. Finally, applicants must complete an in-person interview, as admission to the program is highly competitive, with only 65 spots available each year.

title: Summer Legal Internship Program
text: This internship program provides paid opportunities for high school juniors and seniors to gain valuable experience in the legal field. Interns are placed in positions at Houston-area law firms, corporate legal departments, and public interest agencies. The program aims to expose interns to potential careers in law, equipping them with the work experience, job readiness, and life skills necessary for a successful future.
requirements: unknown

title: Southwest Airlines High School Internship
text: At Southwest Airlines' Southwest Headquarters Ground Operations, individuals can contribute to personnel support for employees at the station. This encompasses tasks such as assisting with payroll, attendance and leave management, staffing, maintaining personnel records and resources, and coordinating events and meetings. These opportunities provide a valuable means of supporting the smooth functioning of the station and ensuring the well-being of Southwest Airlines employees.
requirements: Must be 16 years old

title: Musée Internship Program
text: Musée Magazine, a vibrant biennial publication and interactive website, offers a unique platform for emerging and established artists. As an intern at Musée, you'll gain invaluable hands-on experience in the digital publication industry. Immerse yourself in the world of photography, connecting with renowned figures, discovering promising talent, attending exclusive film premieres, and experiencing the excitement of gallery openings. Musée is committed to providing interns with unparalleled insights into the creative process and the dynamic landscape of the photographic community.
requirements:
All potential interns must possess:
The ability to work independently and collaboratively
Strong written and verbal skills
Professionalism and punctuality
Familiarity with Musée Magazine. Please take the time to browse our past issues.

title: Museum Apprentice Program
text: This paid internship offers New York City teens an immersive experience in the world of art and art history. Interns will delve into the intricacies of museum education, gaining valuable insights into the field. They will have the opportunity to create their own educational lessons tailored to audiences of all ages, fostering their creativity and communication skills. Through this hands-on experience, interns will develop a deep understanding of the role of museums in fostering cultural appreciation and inspiring future generations.

title: BRAINYAC

BRAINYAC fosters connections with renowned scientists, equipping students with essential research skills and integrating them into the Columbia University community. Through hands-on research, students gain invaluable insights into the field of neuroscience, developing a foundation for future scientific endeavors.
requirements: unknown

Through exploration of the Garden, they delve into nature and plant science, equipping themselves as environmental educators for children and families. This commitment entails a minimum of 125 hours dedicated to training and volunteer service.

title: Applied Research Innovation in Science & Engineering (ARISE)
text: This seven-week program encompasses a rigorous five-week authentic research experience within participating NYU faculty laboratories, where students receive mentorship from graduate or postdoctoral students. Upon completion, participants receive a stipend of at least $750. Additionally, the program includes two weeks of workshops, college advisement, and other activities specifically designed to equip ARISE students with the necessary skills and knowledge for the college application process.
requirements:
Have a passion for science, technology, engineering and math.
Be responsible, highly motivated students who have demonstrated timeliness, persistence, and an ability to fulfill commitments.

title: High School Internship
text: The Donald Danforth Plant Science Center offers a comprehensive suite of K-12 STEM education opportunities through its Education and Outreach Lab. The center's STEAM+Ag curriculum provides authentic research experiences in genetics, molecular biology, and image analytics for students from kindergarten through high school. High school students can also participate in a summer internship program at the center's plant and agricultural research facility. The center's programs include Mutant Millets, Discovering Volvox Development, Genotype to Phenotype, and Soil Health and MO DIRT. Additionally, the center utilizes cutting-edge technologies such as Virtual Reality and Educational Technology Professional Development to foster student interest in STEM careers. The center also focuses on engaging displaced and refugee students in STEM education, providing them with an outlet for coping with trauma and stress. Ultimately, these programs aim to expand access to plant science education and inspire the next generation of scientists.
requirements: Applicants must be 16 years or older at the time of application submission. They must also have a genuine interest in STEAM (science, technology, engineering, agriculture, and mathematics) research. Prior to applying for the internship, it is important for students to research and understand the type of research being done in the labs at the Center. They will be asked to list up to three labs that match their research interests and why they are interested in those labs. Danforth Center scientists work in various settings, including traditional or "wet" laboratories, outdoor field plots, greenhouses, and computational settings, therefore it is important for students to understand which setting aligns with their interests. Students who are accepted into the program will have the opportunity to collect data, collaborate with teammates, disseminate their results, and learn from scientists.

title: JOB1 Summer Internship Program
text: As the flagship program of ROTARY/One, JOB1 equips City of Chicago High School 11th grade and graduating seniors, aged sixteen and above, with the skills necessary for workplace success. Through comprehensive job readiness training, participants develop essential competencies. Additionally, JOB1 offers substantive paid summer internship opportunities with local businesses and non-profit organizations in the Chicago area, providing hands-on experience and valuable connections. This program empowers young individuals to transition smoothly into the workforce, fostering their professional growth and contributing to the economic vitality of the city.
requirements: Applicants must be enrolled in high school in 11th grade or senior year, and are sixteen and older.

Through their involvement, students develop valuable skills in archival research, document analysis, and historical interpretation, while fostering a deeper understanding of their local heritage.
address: 121 M.L.K. Jr Blvd N, Dover, DE 19901

title: Youth Volunteer
text: Boston Cares collaborates with nonprofits and schools to amplify their impact by engaging a diverse volunteer base to collectively address pressing community needs. title: Junior Volunteer Program
text: By volunteering at University Health, you can brighten the lives of patients and their families. title: Voices of Oklahoma
text: Voices of Oklahoma is a summer internship program designed for rising high school juniors and seniors from communities historically underrepresented in archaeology. This academic program introduces students to the field of archaeology, emphasizing its role in complementing traditional methods of understanding heritage, such as historical documents and oral traditions. Each summer's curriculum revolves around a specific theme intended to resonate with the students. For the upcoming summer of 2023, the theme will focus on the history and impact of Indigenous boarding schools.

title: Stanford Medical Youth Science Program
text: The Stanford Medical Youth Science Program (SMYSP) is an academic enrichment program designed for students from underrepresented backgrounds with limited financial means. Over the course of five weeks, participants engage in a comprehensive curriculum that includes faculty lectures, professional development workshops, networking events with Stanford Medicine professionals, and a research project focused on public health disparities.

text: Participants will gain proficiency in academic research methodologies, explore diverse engineering disciplines, and have the opportunity to develop a project for the Utah Science & Engineering Fair. Interns are given the opportunity to develop and lead activities as well as assist with programs.

title: Teen Gallery Guide
text: Teen Gallery Guides at the Getty Center offers a paid summer internship for teens passionate about art. Interns will develop their understanding of artwork, audience engagement techniques, and teaching strategies to lead gallery experiences and activities for visiting school groups. The program fosters community among teen peers, enhances public speaking skills, and provides unique opportunities to interact with art professionals and museum spaces. Transportation to and from the Getty Center is provided, along with a stipend, ensuring accessibility for all participants.
requirements: Must be interested in art, working in community with teen peers, building public speaking skills, and engaging with art professionals and museum spaces in unique ways

title: Broad Summer Scholars Program
text: The Broad Summer Scholars Program (BSSP) offers a transformative six-week experience for highly motivated high school students with a passion for science. Students are paired with renowned Broad scientists to embark on original research projects in cutting-edge fields such as cancer biology, psychiatric disease, chemical biology, computational biology, and infectious disease. Beyond research, the program immerses students in the scientific community through engaging talks, a scientific poster session, a college fair, and social events. Participants gain invaluable insights into scientific careers, connect with peers who share their interests, and develop a deeper understanding of the transformative power of scientific research.
address: Merkin Building 415 Main St. Cambridge, MA 02142
requirements: To be eligible to apply to BSSP, applicants must: Be a rising senior in high school (i.e. students can apply their junior year) Attend a high school in MA within commuting distance to the Broad Have earned a B or better in science and math classes Demonstrate excitement for science!​ No previous research experience is required. Be a US citizen, permanent resident, or non-US citizen with employment authorization (i.e. DACA) Be fully vaccinated against Covid-19 by the program's start date, in accordance with Broad Institute policy. The Broad will allow limited exemptions to this requirement, including for medical or religious reasons. Be available for the entire 6-week duration of the program. Students cannot be enrolled in other courses or programs, or commit to other employment, during program hours. We especially encourage applications from students who meet one or more of the following criteria: Underrepresented in the sciences—these groups include Native Americans or Alaska Natives, Blacks or African Americans, Hispanics or Latinxs, Native Hawaiians or Other Pacific Islanders, as well as individuals with disabilities. Underserved, as indicated by qualifying for free or reduced lunch. Could be the first person in their family to attend college. Demonstrate a commitment to issues of diversity and inclusion through extracurricular and/or community activities that address social, educational, or economic disparities in the United States.

title: High School Internship
text: DPR's Build Up High School Internship in Construction Management offers an immersive 8-week experience for high school students interested in exploring the field. The program provides hands-on learning opportunities in construction management, with participants working alongside industry professionals. The program operates in person, with interns working 35-40 hours per week to gain valuable insights into the construction industry.

title: Accelerate Cancer Education (ACE) Program

Through a comprehensive education and training experience, the ACE program seeks to engage a wide range of students, empowering them with the knowledge and skills necessary to pursue careers in cancer research and related fields.

title: High School Civic Engagement Internship

The High School Civic Engagement Internship Program, a collaborative effort between Rice University and the League of Women Voters of Houston, aims to address this issue by directly engaging with high school students to promote voter registration and civic engagement.

title: GenCyber Summer
text: The Institute for Security, Technology, and Society (ISTS) at Dartmouth College presents an advanced cybersecurity summer program designed to empower students with interdisciplinary knowledge in cybersecurity and privacy. Funded by Dartmouth College and the GenCyber program, a collaboration between the National Security Agency and the National Science Foundation, this program targets students with a demonstrated understanding of cybersecurity concepts and technological proficiency. The curriculum encompasses lectures, interactive activities, and guest speaker sessions, delving into system vulnerabilities, cyber-attack defense, digital forensics, and security awareness. Additionally, students are tasked with completing an outreach project to disseminate cybersecurity knowledge within their school and community.
host: The Institute for Security, Technology, and Society (ISTS) at Dartmouth College
requirements: To apply for the Institute for Security, Technology and Society's GenCyber Summer Program, prospective applicants must be entering 9th through 12th grade in the fall of 2023. They must also demonstrate familiarity with cybersecurity concepts and information technology prowess. The program is generously funded by Dartmouth College and the GenCyber program, a partnership between the National Security Agency and the National Science Foundation, and there is no charge for the program. The advanced program will be held on campus from June 26-30, 2023, and it will focus on understanding system vulnerabilities, defending against cyber-attacks, digital forensics, privacy, and security awareness. In addition to lectures and interactive activities, participants will be expected to complete an outreach project of their own design to spread the word about cybersecurity to their school and community.

title: Musical Electronics Camp

This program aims to introduce participants to the fundamentals of electronics and its application in creating innovative musical arrangements. The curriculum guides learners through a comprehensive process, encompassing the basics of soldering and programming, culminating in the construction of their own music-generating machines. While prior knowledge in music or electronics is not a prerequisite, prospective campers must register and fulfill all application requirements. Upon completion of the program, each student will depart with an electronic instrument they have personally crafted.

MMEN is a program designed to reverse this trend by opening doors to career advancement within medicine to underrepresented communities.

title: Science Honors Program (SHP)
text: The Columbia University Science Honors Program (SHP) is a highly selective program designed for high school students with a deep passion for science and mathematics. The program consists of classes held on Saturdays throughout the academic year, taking place from 10:00 AM to 12:30 PM at Columbia University.
requirements: Applicants for the 2021-2022 school year must now be in the eleventh, tenth, or ninth grade and must apply online. The program is available only to students who attend high schools in New York, New Jersey, or Connecticut and who live within a 75-mile radius of the Columbia campus.

title: Northwestern Pre-College Summer Program
text: Northwestern University's School of Professional Studies provides a Pre-College Summer Program tailored for high school sophomores, juniors, and seniors to prepare them for higher education. Students have the opportunity to acquire college credits through coursework or two-week online seminars encompassing diverse subjects. The program comprises two components: College Preparation and College Bridge. The latter, in collaboration with Chicago Public Schools, enables 25 CPS juniors to enroll in Northwestern's Summer Session, earning college credits while experiencing campus life and academic rigor.
requirements: Applicants must be high school sophomores, juniors, or seniors at the time of application. They should have achieved a minimum unweighted GPA of 3.0 or higher on a 4.0 scale or equivalent. They must submit an online application form, high school transcripts, a letter of recommendation from a teacher, and a personal statement that details their academic goals and why they want to attend the program. Additionally, some programs may require additional materials, such as a writing sample or portfolio. Finally, applicants must pay the non-refundable application fee before the deadline.

title: The Garden Apprentice Program (GAP)

Through a four-tiered program, apprentices engage in hands-on work within one of the world's renowned public gardens. The program empowers teens to develop their knowledge and skills in horticulture, sustainability, and community engagement, while fostering a deep appreciation for the natural world and the role of urban green spaces in our lives.
address:
Brooklyn Botanic Garden
1000 Washington Avenue
Brooklyn, NY 11225

title: Air Force Research Library Scholar Program
text: The Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) Scholars Program provides paid summer internship opportunities for undergraduate and graduate students in STEM fields, as well as upper-level high school students. Additionally, select locations offer internships to university students pursuing education-related degrees and K-12 professional educators. Interns collaborate with AFRL scientists and engineers on cutting-edge research and technology, gaining hands-on experience and contributing to unique, research-based projects. This program offers students the opportunity to develop their skills, explore career paths, and make meaningful contributions to the advancement of science and technology.
requirements:
All applicants must meet the following eligibility requirements:

A grade point average of at least 3.0 on a 4.0 scale is highly encouraged for all applicants. Note: A grade point average of less than 3.0 on a 4.0 scale will not disqualify applicants.
Must be a US Citizen; program is not open to non-Citizens or Permanent Residents
Must be enrolled or accepted at an educational institution taking at least half-time academic course load leading to a degree or certificate for semester immediately preceding internship session. Note:  This does not apply to professional educators.
Must be in good academic standing
Must be at least 16 years of age (by session application deadline) and have a valid driver’s license
Must be available to work full-time (40 hours per week) for summer internship positions
Must be willing to temporarily relocate to physical work location
Must be able to take personal responsibility for arranging transportation to and from worksite each day. Note:  Scholars should not rely on transportation from anyone who does not already have base access. Program administration will not be responsible for making additional arrangements on a scholar’s behalf to provide suitable transportation.
Must be able to pass a background check, potentially resulting in a Secret Security Clearance

title: Biomedical Research Internship for Minority Students

requirements:
Have completed their junior year of high school with a ‘B’ average or better, and have reached their 16th by the start of the program.
Be from groups that have been traditionally underrepresented in the health professions (African American, Hispanic/Latino, Native American, Native Alaskan, Native Hawaiian) or others from disadvantaged backgrounds who meet all eligibility criteria and have a high probability of fulfilling the social and educational goals of this program.
Be from a Connecticut high school that has an on-site School-to-Career or Career-to-Work Coordinator during the academic year, as well as summer months. This does not apply to Connecticut high school graduates or students who will be 18 years of age at the start of the program.
Be a U.S. citizen or permanent resident.

title: High School Exploration Internship
text: In 2007, Scripps and the Health and Science Pipeline Initiative (HASPI) embarked on a partnership to foster the development of future healthcare professionals. Through the Health and Science Pipeline Initiative, high school students with a passion for healthcare are provided with immersive worksite and learning experiences. This five-week internship program welcomes students from across the county, offering them an in-depth exploration of healthcare careers. The program aims to inspire and educate these young individuals, equipping them with the knowledge and skills necessary to pursue their aspirations in the healthcare field.
address:
10666 N. Torrey Pines Rd.
La Jolla, CA 92037
requirements: unknown

title: High School Fellowships
text: During the program, fellows shadow physicians, nurses, and allied health professionals at Stillwater Medical Center and area clinics. They witness surgeries, births, and emergency treatment at SMC. Field trips are typically included to Oklahoma's medical schools and specialized centers such as Dean McGee Eye Institute, Oklahoma Blood Institute, Integris' Paul Silverstein Burn & Wound Care Unit, and Oklahoma Cancer Specialists and Research Institute.
requirements:
The fellowships are open to students who are completing their sophomore, junior, OR senior year of high school.
 
Student applicants must be from a high school within Stillwater Medical's service area, such as: Stillwater, Blackwell, Carney, Coyle, Cushing, Glencoe, Morrison, Mulhall-Orlando, Pawnee, Perkins/Tryon, Perry, Red Rock/Marland, Ripley, or Yale.

title: Internships + Students in Construction
text: The Samet Corporation's internship program caters to students with a passion for construction and an entrepreneurial spirit. Interns gain hands-on experience in both field and office settings, allowing them to discover their strengths. Samet prioritizes mentoring, providing personalized instruction, classroom training, and practical experience. Through their "Students in Construction" initiative, they collaborate with educational institutions to identify and recruit talented individuals. The program encourages interns to explore Samet's culture and career paths, fostering a sense of belonging. Social events enhance the experience, while financial compensation ensures that interns gain valuable income alongside practical knowledge.
requirements: To be considered for Samet Corporation's internship program, applicants are required to be individuals with an entrepreneurial spirit and passion for construction. Applicants should be interested in both the office and field aspects of the business and have a desire to excel in their chosen areas. The program offers corporate office and field experience to help interns explore various career paths within the construction industry. Additionally, interns will receive mentoring and career advice, as well as introductory classroom training and personalized instruction to gain hands-on experience. To be eligible, applicants may submit their resumes and Samet Corporation will provide more information about their internship program.

title: CURIE Academy
text: CURIE Academy is a one-week residential program designed for high school girls, particularly rising juniors and seniors, who aspire to explore engineering within a genuine college setting. The program aims to foster an understanding of engineering as a major field of study at the collegiate level, highlight career and graduate school opportunities in the field, and clarify the admissions process. Through hands-on experiences, interactions with engineering professionals, and exposure to university life, CURIE Academy empowers participants to make informed decisions about their future in engineering.
address: Carpenter Hall, 313 Campus Rd, Ithaca, NY 14853

title: C.Summer Institutes for High School Students
text: The Financial Empowerment Institute offers comprehensive financial literacy education, empowering individuals to take control of their finances and plan for their future. Led by finance professors, students, and professionals, the institute provides essential knowledge on personal financial planning, including money management, budgeting, and goal setting. By equipping participants with these skills, the institute aims to foster financial stability and empower them to make informed decisions about their financial well-being.
requirements: To be considered for the Business Summer Institutes for High School Students program, applicants must be current 9th, 10th, or 11th graders. The program is free and open to students interested in exploring the business world through Financial Empowerment education and expert panel discussions.

title: Teen Creative Agency
text: The Teen Creative Agency (TCA), a program of the Museum of Contemporary Art, empowers teens aged 15-19 to engage with contemporary art and artists. Weekly gatherings at the MCA foster a space for teens to express their ideas and perspectives, while visits to other cultural institutions connect them with peers and professionals. Through these experiences, TCA members develop their agency, collaboration skills, and understanding of public engagement. Guided by Lead Artists Olive Stefanski and Miguel Limon, the program cultivates young people's recognition of their own value and the value they bring to their community, strengthening their creative process and fostering their growth as cultural leaders.
requirements: Must be 15-19 years old

title: Yale Summer Session
text: Yale Summer Session invites ambitious high school students to immerse themselves in Yale College courses for academic credit. Enrolled students will engage in college-level coursework alongside undergraduate peers, adhering to the same rigorous standards. This immersive experience provides an unparalleled opportunity for high school students to challenge themselves intellectually and gain valuable insights into the rigors of higher education.
address: 55 Whitney Avenue, 4th Fl. New Haven, CT 06510
requirements:
Must be entering the senior year of high school (summer after junior year) or freshman year of college (summer after senior year).
Must be 16 years of age or older by their program start date.

title: Volunteering
text: Volunteering at Houston's Museum of Fine Arts offers a diverse range of opportunities for creative high schoolers. Volunteers contribute in various capacities, such as welcoming guests, assisting in the museum shop, performing administrative tasks, facilitating engaging art projects for children, and leading informative tours. This immersive experience allows volunteers to interact with the museum's vast collection, engage with visitors, and contribute to the vibrant cultural landscape of Houston.
host: The Museum of Fine Arts Houston
requirements: MFAH volunteers are a diverse group of people. Just about anyone who has a desire to contribute can volunteer, from teens to stay-at-home parents, and from professionals to retirees.

title: Automotive High School Internship Program
text: Through a partnership with the Department of Education (DOE), DCAS has expanded the Automotive High School Internship program. This program offers paid year-round and summer internships to public high school students. These internships provide students with hands-on experience maintaining high-profile City vehicles. Students will have the opportunity to learn from leading city fleet experts and professionals who service the largest municipal fleet in the United States.
host: NYC Department of Citywide Administrative Services
requirements:
Student must be between 16-22 years of age at start of program. Student must attend school or live in Manhattan or Staten Island
Student must be interested in a career in the health field
Student must provide two recommendations; one from a teacher or faculty member.

title: RISE – Ragon Institute Summer Experience
text: The Ragon Institute Summer Experience (RISE) internship program provides paid, structured, and mentored internships for high school and undergraduate students from underrepresented communities in the Greater Boston area who are interested in medical research and immunology. The program aims to inspire these young people to consider careers in these fields. Interns are assigned to projects in labs led by Ragon faculty mentors. In addition to lab work, interns participate in cohort-level activities coordinated by Education and Outreach staff, which include seminars, workshops, and networking opportunities.
requirements: Interest in learning about immunology and related fields; Ability to meet the work hour requirements and participate in all activities; High school students must be rising seniors or will graduate from high school in 2023 and must be 16 years old or older; Demonstrated interest in STEM fields: coursework, extra-curricular activity, etc.; previous participation in program that supports academic development; Teacher/mentor recommendations; Personal statement of interest

title: Lehman College Now STEM Research Academy
text: The College Now STEM Research Academy at Lehman College is a two-part program designed to foster scientific thinking skills in students through hands-on research experiences. The first component, a high school credit course offered in the spring semester, introduces students to scientific investigation through the "DNA Detectives" curriculum. The second component, a six-week college credit course (BIO189) held during the summer, provides students with the opportunity to work in research laboratories under the guidance of Lehman College faculty and graduate students. Through these experiences, students develop essential skills in scientific inquiry, data analysis, and communication, preparing them for future success in STEM fields.
requirements:
Be a NYC public high school sophomore or junior in good academic standing
Have an overall HS average of 80+
Have received a 70+ on any Common Core Math Regents
Have a strong interest in science
Summer mentorship also requires ELA Regents score of 70+

title: Girls Tech Scholars Program
text: Join a supportive, all-girl environment where you'll delve into the empowering stories of women from diverse backgrounds. Explore how they wielded their influence and sparked change. As a digital changemaker, you'll craft websites that showcase the remarkable contributions of women throughout history. Through this immersive experience, you'll not only learn coding skills but also gain a profound understanding of the power and resilience of women.
address:
New-York Historical Society, 170 Central Park West
at Richard Gilder Way (77th Street), New York, NY 10024
requirements: unknown

title: Urban Barcode Research Program
text: The Urban Barcode Research Program (UBRP), a science education initiative supported by the Pinkerton Foundation and Science Sandbox, engages New York City high school students in biodiversity studies utilizing DNA technology. This student research mentorship program provides opportunities for students to delve into the intricacies of biodiversity, fostering their understanding of the natural world and inspiring their pursuit of scientific careers.
requirements:
STUDENT ELIGIBILITY
Students must be enrolled in grades 9-12 at a public or private high school in New York City. Students must reside in New York City.
Students are required to complete two mandatory courses: Conservation Genetics and DNA Barcoding and Bioinformatics. These free courses are offered after school, during school breaks, and in the summer. 
After completion of the courses, students must submit an online application to be considered for the program.

title: Hutton Junior Fisheries Biology Program
text: The Hutton Junior Fisheries Biology Program, sponsored by the American Fisheries Society (AFS), is an eight-week paid summer internship and mentoring program designed for high school students. This program aims to foster interest in fisheries and aquatic science among underrepresented groups within the field. Through hands-on experiences and mentorship from professionals, the program seeks to inspire students to pursue careers in these areas, ultimately contributing to a more diverse and inclusive workforce in fisheries and aquatic science.
requirements: Students who live and have residency in the United States, Mexico and Canada are eligible to apply. We highly encourage students from traditionally excluded backgrounds in the fisheries profession to submit applications to the Hutton Program. Past participants of the Hutton Program are not eligible to submit an application.

title: QuarkNet Summer Research Program
text: QuarkNet provides summer research opportunities in science and technology for students who have exhibited a strong interest and aptitude in science and mathematics. These students collaborate with scientists for seven weeks on projects directly related to the Fermilab research program.
address: Kirk and, Pine St, Batavia, IL 60510
requirements: High school sophomores, juniors, and seniors when applying. Juniors with experience programming computers or working with mechanical or electrical systems are encouraged to apply. Illinois high school enrollment U.S. citizenship or permanent resident status Evidence of identity and eligibility to work in the U.S. Work authorization if under 16 years of age. This refers to a work authorization for minors (sometimes called a “minor work permit”) that students under 16 must get through their school district. Your high school guidance counselors should have more information. Proof of medical insurance Applicants are asked to commit to attending the entire six-week internship period.

title: Inspiring Future Scientists through Shadowing (IFSS)
text: The Stanford Department of Chemistry's Inspiring Future Scientists Through Shadowing (IFSS) program offers rising high school juniors and seniors an immersive experience in cutting-edge chemical research. Through this program, students are paired with graduate student mentors who guide them through laboratory work, providing hands-on exposure to advanced research techniques and methodologies. The IFSS program fosters a deep understanding of the scientific process, cultivates critical thinking skills, and inspires students to pursue careers in chemistry and related fields.
requirements: Students MUST be over the age of 16 by the start of the program. We encourage applications from US citizens and permanent residents. There is no cost to participate in the program; to preserve this situation, we can only accept local students for whom transportation and living arrangements will not be a significant financial barrier to participation. We do not provide housing for participants, and participants must arrange for their own transportation to/from the Stanford Campus.

title: Queensborough Community College Now STEM Research Academy
text: The STEM Research Academy is a comprehensive two-semester program that fosters essential literacy and numeracy skills through hands-on experiences. It comprises a spring pre-college science course that lays the foundation for students. The program's highlight is a summer research experience where students collaborate with CUNY faculty members on authentic inquiry projects. This immersive experience empowers students to engage in meaningful scientific research, fostering their understanding of STEM concepts and preparing them for future academic and professional endeavors.
requirements:
NYC DOE students who are on track to graduate high school
CUNY Eligibility Benchmarks (75+ ELA Regents and/or 80+ Math Regents)
Primarily high school juniors

title: Teen Art Connect Internship
text: The Teen Art Connect (TAC) Internship offers a year-round paid opportunity for high school students from various backgrounds to immerse themselves in the arts. Through this program, teens collaborate in a renowned arts environment, engaging with art and artists, delving into their own identities and cultures, and producing and leading impactful public events and programs. Additionally, they acquire valuable professional skills, fostering their development as future leaders in the arts and beyond.
requirements: All high school students entering 10th, 11th, or 12th grade in fall 2023 are eligible to apply.

title: Volunteer
text: San Antonio's Magik Theatre offers a unique blend of literature-based theatre and educational opportunities for families. High school students with aspirations in the performing arts, nonprofits, or education are encouraged to explore volunteer internship opportunities at the theatre. By contacting the theatre directly, students can inquire about potential roles that align with their interests and career goals.
requirements: unknown

title: Research Science Institute
text: The Research Science Institute (RSI) is a cost-free summer program at MIT for high school juniors, offering an immersive STEM experience. Students engage in rigorous coursework led by esteemed professors, delving into cutting-edge scientific literature. Simultaneously, they embark on individual research projects guided by experienced mentors. RSI's unique approach combines on-campus coursework with off-campus research, providing students with a comprehensive understanding of the research cycle. Culminating in a conference-style presentation, students showcase their research findings, demonstrating their ability to navigate the entire research process from inception to dissemination.
requirements: Applicants must be high school juniors at the time of their application and must not have participated in RSI before. They must be interested in pursuing a career in science, technology, engineering, or mathematics (STEM) fields, and must demonstrate exceptional academic achievement in these fields, as well as in other areas of study. The application process is highly competitive and includes multiple stages, including the submission of transcripts, test scores, two letters of recommendation, written responses to essay questions, and, for those who pass these stages, an interview. Finalists are selected based on their academic ability, research experience, letters of recommendation, and personal characteristics, and they must commit to attending the entire 6-week program at MIT.

title: The Young Women's Leadership Institute
text: The Young Women's Leadership Institute (YWLI) offers a transformative summer experience in New York City, delving into the intricate relationship between gender and leadership. YWLI seeks curious and passionate individuals eager to hone their leadership skills. Through a feminist lens, participants will explore trailblazing qualities, push boundaries, and develop their potential as leaders. The Institute fosters a supportive environment where young women can cultivate their voices, challenge societal norms, and emerge as empowered and influential leaders.
requirements: unknown

title: Codebreakers
text: Codebreakers, a summer program offered by Boston University, empowers young women in grades 9-10 with a keen interest in computer security. Through a comprehensive curriculum encompassing programming, cryptography, and network security, participants delve into fundamental cybersecurity principles and hone their coding skills in Python. They engage in hands-on activities such as programming games, deciphering ciphers, and analyzing system vulnerabilities. The program also emphasizes the ethical implications of technology, with guest speakers from government agencies and industry professionals sharing their insights. While the program is free, a non-refundable registration fee of $100 applies for accepted participants. Applicants are advised to monitor the program's website for updates regarding the 2023 edition.
requirements: To be considered for the Codebreakers program, applicants must be young women who will be entering 10th or 11th grade at a school in the greater Boston area in fall 2023, and must reside in and attend school in Massachusetts. The program is designed for those who are interested in learning about computer security. Students will be taught basic cybersecurity concepts through lessons in programming, cryptography, and network security. Therefore, a basic understanding of computer language is recommended for applicants. The program teaches Python programming, so prior experience in the language is an advantage. The participants will be required to pay a non-refundable registration fee of $100 once accepted to the program. Finally, applicants must submit an application through the Codebreakers website before the deadline to be considered for the program.

title: Summit Program
text: Throughout the year, students will engage in a diverse range of activities tailored to each season. Weekly service projects will foster a spirit of community involvement, while personal growth initiatives will empower students to develop their skills and character. Community building activities will strengthen bonds among participants, creating a supportive and inclusive environment. The culmination of each year's efforts will be an annual Summit Celebration, a grand event that celebrates the collective achievements and growth of the students.
requirements: Be a student

title: High School Intern
text: This internship program offers high school students part-time paid employment at a sponsoring dealership while they continue their studies. The program is designed for students interested in pursuing a career in the heavy equipment industry and provides them with the opportunity to gain hands-on experience in the parts, sales, and service departments. Through shadowing and working alongside experienced professionals, students can develop a comprehensive understanding of the industry and its various roles.
requirements:
Must be 16 years of age or older.

Maintain acceptable attendance record while in program.

Strong computer skills.
Excellent customer service skills.

title: Internship Program
text: Special Olympics Connecticut (SOCT) invites individuals seeking meaningful employment or academic enrichment to explore its exceptional opportunities. Whether you aspire to make a lasting impact through a career or gain valuable work experience and academic credit through an internship, SOCT offers a rewarding journey. Join the team and immerse yourself in an experience that transcends the ordinary, where you can contribute to the lives of others while fostering your own professional and personal growth.
requirements: unknown

title: Girls Who Code Summer Program
text: Through our free, virtual summer programs, students acquire essential computer science skills that empower them to make a meaningful impact and prepare for successful careers in the tech industry. Participants gain valuable insights into tech professions, connect with influential leaders in the field, and foster a sense of community within our supportive sisterhood.
requirements:
All high school students (now welcoming summer alumni and graduating seniors!!)
6 weeks to complete course projects at your own pace
Now available with new intermediate content!

title: Hospital Placement
text: This internship-based program immerses students in the field of healthcare, fostering their understanding of health careers while strengthening their foundational knowledge in science, research, and communication. Participants engage in daily placements for study and career exploration, delving into library research, attending weekly seminars, and exploring an introductory series on disparities in health and medicine. This comprehensive program aims to equip students with the skills and knowledge necessary to navigate the healthcare field effectively.
address: 1 Gustave L. Levy Pl, New York, NY 10029
host: The Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai
requirements:
Demonstrated interest in science and medicine
Prior experience in a research or medical facility and/or participation in a previous CEYE
program is preferred.
Must be a rising high school senior, with a minimum GPA of 85
Must be an under-represented minority and/or economically disadvantaged

title: Summer Science Corps
text: As a member of the Summer Science Corps, you will contribute to various aspects of museum operations. You will assist in interpreting exhibits for visitors, facilitating educational programs, and coordinating special events. Additionally, you will gain hands-on experience in early childhood education, exhibit interpretation, and museum collections management. Through these diverse roles, you will develop a comprehensive understanding of museum operations and the importance of science education.
host: Delaware Museum of Nature and Science
requirements: Be a high school student 14 years old or up

title: Computer Science for Cyber Security (CS4CS)
text: NYU Tandon School of Engineering's CS4CS program offers a comprehensive introduction to computer science and cybersecurity for high school students. This three-week summer program empowers a diverse group of aspiring engineers with the specialized skills necessary to address the cybersecurity challenges of the present and future. Cybersecurity, a rapidly expanding and in-demand field, demands a solid foundation in computer science. CS4CS provides this foundation, equipping students with the knowledge and abilities to excel in this critical area.
requirements: Eligible applicants will be students currently enrolled in the 8th, 9th, 10th, or 11th grade who live in New York City or neighboring cities, such as Jersey City, Newark, or Hempstead.

title: High School Internship Program
text: High school volunteer student workers are responsible for a variety of tasks, including scanning, photocopying, and shredding documents; answering telephones, typing, filing, and delivering documents; and assembling reports, documents, or manuals. of a parent or legal guardian.

title: River Restoration Internship
text: The Coastal Watershed Council holds the San Lorenzo River in high regard, actively sharing its wonders with the community and taking measures to preserve it. The organization spearheads habitat restoration initiatives along the river, aiming to improve riparian habitats for a thriving and resilient river ecosystem. Additionally, the council fosters community connections with the river through engaging stewardship and volunteer activities, allowing individuals to contribute to its well-being while deepening their appreciation for this natural treasure.
address:
107 Dakota Avenue, Suite 4
Santa Cruz, CA 95062
requirements: Must be able to commit 12 hours per week, have a strong interest in environmental preservation, and have comfort and enthusiasm in leading volunteers.

title: Teen Volunteer
text: The Discovery Cube's Teen Volunteer Program provides high school students with a unique opportunity to delve into STEM fields through hands-on experiences and leadership development. Participants engage with museum visitors through interactive exhibits and educational programs, fostering their understanding of science, technology, engineering, and math. The program is available in both Orange County and Los Angeles, offering students the chance to gain valuable skills, contribute to their community, and explore their passion for STEM.
address:
2500 N Main Street
Santa Ana, CA 92705
requirements: Must be a high schooler ages 15-18

title: TEEN MENTORSHIP
text: Our Mentorship Program is a two-year commitment that provides participants with monthly workshops at the Teen Center on our Goleta Valley Campus. These workshops focus on practical skills such as resume writing, job interview preparation, and financial literacy. During the summer after their first year, mentees complete an internship with a community partner, which can fulfill community service hour requirements. In the second year, mentees continue with monthly workshops and are paired with mentors in the community. Mentees and mentors meet twice monthly via Zoom. The following summer, mentees engage in an in-person internship at their mentor's workplace. Upon completion of their second summer internship, all mentees receive a small grant. The Mentorship Program is offered free of charge, and all applicants undergo an interview process to assess their commitment and suitability for the program.
requirements: Must be in High school. Must interview as a part of the application process. Must be able to commit two years to the program. (If you are a high school senior, you may still apply. Must have Wi-Fi and access to a digital device to log in to Zoom. The participant must attend mandatory once-month in-person workshops at our Girls Inc. Teen Center located at 4973 Hollister Ave, in Goleta. The monthly workshops will focus on helping the youth develop interpersonal and professional skills to equip them for their summer internship.

title: GO Getter Summer Internship
text: The GO Project summer internship offers high school students a unique opportunity to hone their leadership abilities while assisting GO Project students in academic and enrichment classes. Over the five-week GO Summer program, interns will provide support in K-4 classrooms under the supervision of Head Teachers or Enrichment Teachers. This immersive experience allows interns to contribute to the educational journey of younger students while developing their own leadership skills and gaining valuable hands-on experience in the field of education.
requirements:
- Must be at least 16 years old as of July 5, 2023
- High school students in good academic standing (rising 10th, 11th, and 12th graders and 2023 high school graduates) 
- Commitment to and belief in all children’s ability to succeed and thrive.
- Commitment to social justice through educational equity.
- Ability to work collaboratively on a team.
- Strong or emerging leadership skills.
- Punctuality and professionalism.

title: Teen Council & Teen Summer
text: Teen Summer is a four-week paid internship program designed for high school students aged 14-19. This program fosters a collaborative exploration of art, community, and the evolving role of museums in contemporary society. Participants engage in self-reflection on their personal connections to arts and culture, culminating in a media and art exhibition that showcases their insights and perspectives. Through this immersive experience, students gain valuable hands-on experience while contributing to a meaningful dialogue about the impact of art and culture on our lives.
host: The Bronx Museum of the Arts
requirements: unknown

title: Biotechnology for Science & Health Academy
text: The Biotechnology for Science & Health Academy offers students with a scientific background the chance to engage in experiments that showcase the significance of Biotechnology in Health and Science. Through lectures, students gain foundational knowledge and concepts, which they then apply in hands-on laboratory exercises. These exercises encompass gene cloning and product analysis, the role of DNA and protein diagnostics in healthcare, the use of DNA in forensics, and various other Biotechnology applications across industries. The course also explores Biotechnology's practical applications in Medicine and Health, Forensics, Agriculture and Food Science, and Basic Scientific Research.
requirements: To apply to the Summer Programs for High School Students, you must meet the following criteria: Be a current or rising high school freshman, sophomore, junior, or senior during the academic year prior to your summer program Show evidence of good academic standing, with at least a 2.0 GPA For the following Non-Credit Academies, students must be at least 15 years old by the date of check-in (no exceptions): 1-Week Medical Academy 3-Week Medical Academy - Anatomy & Physiology track* Biotechnology for Science & Health *Please Note: This restriction only applies to Anatomy & Physiology and Neuroscience tracks. The Emergency Medicine track does not have an age restriction.

title: High School Internship
text: The Museum of Science in Boston offers internship opportunities for individuals aged 14 and up, including high school students, college freshmen through seniors, and graduate students. Interns engage in diverse projects encompassing science education and behind-the-scenes operations. The program operates during three trimesters: fall, winter/spring, and summer, with paid and unpaid positions available. Internships may be credited towards coursework with approval from the educational institution. Additionally, the program provides weekly professional development workshops, complimentary museum admission, visits to nearby cultural institutions, and discounts on museum merchandise and dining. A summer youth internship program is also available for teens.
address: 1 Museum Of Science Driveway, Boston, MA 02114
requirements: To be considered for an internship at the Museum of Science, applicants must be at least 14 years old and enrolled in high school, college, or be a recent graduate. The Museum offers internships during the fall, winter/spring and summer trimesters. Interns can work in a variety of projects such as science education and behind-the-scenes work. The Museum offers both paid and unpaid positions, and any position can be used for course credit. Applicants must have proof of being fully vaccinated against COVID-19, and the Museum requires interns, staff, and volunteers to comply with this rule. Applicants should apply for specific positions as they become available, as applications are accepted on a rolling basis.

title: Beginner Environmental Leadership Program
text: Georgia Aquarium's Beginner Environmental Leadership Program empowers high school students aged 15-17 to become future leaders in environmental conservation. This program, open to all students with a passion for aquatic ecosystems and a talent for engaging with others, runs three times annually for a four-month duration. Participants can volunteer on any day during the summer or on breaks and weekends throughout the school year, allowing for flexibility in their involvement.
requirements:
To join this program, each teen must:

Be currently enrolled in high school or home school
Confirm and secure all necessary means of transportation before applying
Be available to volunteer at Georgia Aquarium for a four-month time period
Provide a copy of their birth certificate to verify their age at interview
Provide current government or school-issued photo ID
Pay a $45 Administrative Fee at least one week prior to the start of their program
Be available to attend one interview day at Georgia Aquarium
Be available for and attend one full day of training at Georgia Aquarium
Report on time for all training and volunteer positions in proper attire
Provide all Aquarium guests, staff and volunteers with respect, accurate information, and assistance within the Aquarium guidelines
Maintain a strong work ethic and positive attitude
Demonstrate care & concern for wildlife and support for Aquarium’s mission
Abide by Aquarium policies, procedures and code of conduct as set forth by the Georgia Aquarium Volunteer Program including all COVID-19 policies and procedures

title: City Summer Internship
text: This paid career exploration program empowers Boston girls entering ninth grade to delve into careers within the city's thriving economic engine neighborhoods. Through weekly seminars and explorations, interns gain insights into underrepresented career fields for women. The program fosters career knowledge, self-confidence, and an understanding of the diverse opportunities available in Boston's rapidly growing downtown areas. By connecting girls with these vibrant neighborhoods, the program aims to inspire them to pursue careers that align with their interests and aspirations.
requirements: Girls must be entering ninth grade in the fall and be a Boston resident. All applicants must complete an I-9 form requiring two ID’s and have a social security number.

title: Kimberly Querrey Summer Research Program
text: The Kimberly Querrey Summer Research Program, offered by Northwestern University's Division of Pulmonary and Critical Care, provides a competitive, paid research experience for rising high school juniors and seniors, as well as undergraduate college/university students with an interest in biological sciences. This six- to eight-week program combines intensive research training with support for students' academic and professional development. Many alumni of the program pursue advanced degrees in biological sciences or medical school, demonstrating the program's effectiveness in fostering future careers in the field.
address: 676 North St. Clair Street Arkes Suite 2330 Chicago IL 60611
requirements: Must be a rising high school junior or rising high school senior.

title: Volunteer Summer Program
text: The UCLA Health Volunteen Summer Program provides high school students with hands-on clinical experience in a hospital setting. Accepted volunteers engage in essential roles such as patient transport, wayfinding, and floating. Shifts are available weekly, requiring a minimum commitment of 50 hours. Applicants must be at least 16 years old, possess a valid ID, and be fully vaccinated against COVID-19. Additionally, proof of immunity for varicella, MMR, and TB is mandatory. The application process entails attending an information session, submitting necessary documents, and participating in an in-person orientation.
requirements: To be considered for The UCLA Health Volunteen Summer Program, applicants need to be a minimum of 16 years old, have a valid government-issued photo ID, agreement to volunteer 50 hours, proof of Varicella, MMR, TB, and be fully vaccinated and boosted for COVID-19. Students who hold a non-immigrant VISA or VISA Waiver status, our office only processes international students who are full-time matriculating UCLA Students on F-1 Visas issued by Dashew Center. Applicants need to attend a mandatory information session and then applications will be emailed to those who attend the session. After submitting all the required forms, documents, and proof of immunizations online for review and approval, students will attend a mandatory in-person orientation on June 21, 2023. Finally, applicants need to complete 50 volunteer hours by August 31, 2023.
