title: The Apollo Theater Academy High School Internship Program
text: The Apollo Theater Academy High School Internship Program offers paid professional development opportunities for high school seniors interested in administrative, programming, and production careers in the arts and entertainment industries. Interns engage in hands-on training and career development workshops, gaining practical experience in a real-world work environment. They connect with industry professionals and develop valuable skills while exploring various aspects of the entertainment field. The program is highly competitive, and not all applicants will be selected to participate.
requirements: unknown

title: BDL Debate Camp
text: The Boston Debate League's complimentary Debate Camp offers an exceptional opportunity for students to immerse themselves in debate and argumentation during the summer. Participants will hone their public speaking and leadership abilities while delving into the Policy Debate topic for the upcoming year. The camp has proven invaluable in fostering students' growth as debaters, public speakers, and leaders within their debate teams. Camp attendees frequently assume mentoring roles, sharing the skills they acquire with their debate community, contributing to the overall development of the debate environment.
requirements: unknown

title: Los Angeles Medical Center Volunteer Program
text: The Kaiser Permanente Los Angeles Medical Center offers a diverse array of volunteer programs, including the General Volunteer Program, Teen Volunteer Program, and specialized programs such as Red Vest Concierge, Silver Angel Program, Care Extender Program, No One Dies Alone (NODA) program, Gift Shop, Acoustic Remedies Program, and Paws of Love Pet Program. These programs provide opportunities for volunteers to contribute their time and enhance patient experiences in over 40 departments across the campus. To participate, volunteers must commit a minimum of 200 hours over a year, provide proof of COVID vaccination with booster, communicate effectively in English, undergo a background check, and meet age and educational requirements specific to each program.
address: Kaiser Permanente Los Angeles Medical Center
requirements: To qualify for the Kaiser Permanente Los Angeles Medical Center volunteer program, applicants must meet certain requirements. For the General Volunteer Program, applicants must be willing to commit to a minimum of 200 hours over a period of 1 year and be able to communicate well in English (second language skills are a plus). They must be fully vaccinated against COVID-19, boosters included, and able to pass a background check. For the Teen Volunteer Program, applicants must be at least 16 years old and currently enrolled in high school. They must commit to a minimum of 72 hours over a period of 1 year and meet the same language and vaccination requirements as the General Volunteer Program. Applicants must complete an interview, and applications are always accepted, except for two blackout months of July and December. Onboarding is only applicable to the KP Los Angeles Medical Center, and shadowing and hands-on experience are not permitted at that location. If interested, applicants can reach out to the Volunteer Services Department at 323-783-8109 or through email at volunteerservices-kpsunset@kp.org.

title: Chicago EYES on Cancer Program
text: Chicago EYES (Educators and Youth Enjoy Science) on Cancer is a comprehensive cancer research training program designed for high school and college students aspiring to pursue careers in biomedicine. Over two consecutive summers, participants engage in full-time research within the laboratories of renowned cancer researchers at the university. This rigorous training is enhanced by a summer lecture series focused on cancer, year-round workshops for career development and skill enhancement, and a dedicated network of faculty and peer mentors who provide support and guidance throughout the program.
address: The University of Chicago Medicine 5841 S. Maryland Avenue Chicago, IL 60637
requirements: Must be a high school sophomore, junior, or senior at time of application. Must be at least 16 years of age at start of program.

title: VALOR JROTC
text: The VALOR JROTC Program is a highly competitive, paid, six-week summer internship opportunity for Illinois JROTC high school juniors, seniors, and recent graduates. Interns provide routine technical support for their assigned area, typically an experiment or support group. Under the direct supervision of a Fermilab employee, interns collaborate with project teams, scientists, engineers, and support personnel to accomplish tasks in accordance with established policies and procedures.
requirements: Military Veteran / JROTC High School GraduateProof of identity and eligible to work in the United States

title: Future Speakers Summer Session 2023
text: Future Speakers Academy, a volunteer-led initiative, provides a platform for Bay Area middle school students (grades 5-9) to develop their public speaking skills and advocacy abilities. Held annually during the summer at the Joyce Ellington Branch of San José Public Library, the program empowers participants to become confident and effective communicators.
address: 491 E Empire St, San Jose, CA 95112
requirements: Be in Grades 5-9. Have an interest in speech and debate or want to learn more about public speaking.

title: WBA Experiential Learning Opportunity
text: WBA internships provide hands-on learning experiences in various fields, including facility and tournament management, marketing, and youth baseball instruction. These opportunities enhance students' employability by developing career readiness skills. Internships are particularly appealing to students pursuing degrees in Sports Management, Graphic Design, and Marketing. Through direct interaction with the public, interns gain valuable experience in their respective fields, contributing to their professional growth and future success.
requirements: High school and college age

title: Teen Council
text: Artpace's Teen Council program is a nine-month, paid opportunity for high school students aged 15-18 in the San Antonio area to develop their advocacy for contemporary art and leadership skills. Council members collaborate with Artpace staff and artists to design teen-oriented programs, assist with Artpace events, and initiate community-based projects throughout the school year. This immersive experience empowers teens to become active participants in the local art scene and make a meaningful impact on their community.
requirements: The program is open to high schoolers between the ages of 15 and 18 who live in Bexar County.

title: Mayor’s Office Internship Program
text: Interns are invited to apply to the department that aligns most closely with their interests. Upon selection, interns will be assigned to their chosen department for the duration of their internship. During their tenure, interns will have the opportunity to collaborate with staff and engage in a diverse range of projects. These projects may encompass research, meeting attendance, inquiry management, data analysis, briefing preparation, event staffing, outreach assistance, and support for special initiatives.
address: City Hall Park, New York, NY 10007
requirements:
Must be 16 years of age or older.
Must have current working papers/employment certification at the time of application.
Must be enrolled in high school or accepted to an undergraduate degree program.

title: Internship Program
text: Our comprehensive internship program offers paid opportunities in various departments, including engineering, operations, workforce, and marketing/communications. Interns gain invaluable industry experience, participate in professional development workshops, and engage in networking events. This immersive program fosters personal growth and provides a platform for interns to contribute to our organization while developing their skills and knowledge.
address: 222 Pitkin St STE 101, East Hartford, CT 06108
requirements: unknown

title: Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory Secondary School Field Research Program
text: This field and laboratory science internship program immerses high school students in genuine, demanding research projects. The Piermont Marsh, a component of the Hudson River National Estuarine Research Reserve, serves as the primary research site. Students collaborate in teams under the guidance of Columbia researchers and technicians, conducting a variety of environmental and ecological studies, including sediment accumulation, groundwater chemistry, nutrient cycling, bacterial levels, fish species, fish feeding patterns, and invasive and native plant distributions.
requirements:
Must be enrolled in one of the partner schools (see website for an updated list of partner schools)
Each participating school has assigned a science teacher to act as liaison with the program, typically someone who is also participating in the field work

title: High School Internship
text: High school interns at PAWS Chicago engage in diverse responsibilities under the guidance of staff members. These responsibilities encompass assisting with cleaning and shelter maintenance, ensuring the well-being of dogs through feeding and walking, and contributing to other tasks as assigned.
requirements: To participate in the high school internship program, students must be at least 16 years old and be able to commit to a recurring weekday schedule (between 8am - 6pm) over the course of a six-month internship, with a minimum of 8 hours of service each month.

title: High School Explainer Program
text: The High School Explainer Program at the Exploratorium is a distinguished youth program that provides a distinctive work-based educational experience for high school and early college students. As Explainers, participants actively engage with museum visitors on the exhibition floor, guiding them through interactive exhibits, conducting demonstrations, addressing inquiries, and fulfilling various other responsibilities. This program fosters a dynamic learning environment where students develop their communication, problem-solving, and critical thinking skills while sharing their enthusiasm for science and discovery with the public.
address: Pier 15 Embarcadero at, Green St, San Francisco, CA 94111
requirements:
Candidates must be high school aged students (including students in traditional and alternate post-high school programs – between the ages of 15 and 18 for first time Explainers, and up to the age of 20 for returning Explainers.)
Must be able to obtain a valid work permit.
Must be able to attend all basic training dates

title: Pre-Med Summer Scholar Program
text: The Pre-Med Summer Scholar Program, offered by Volunteer Services at UCLA Health, is an educational program designed for US citizen high school students aged 16 or older who have not yet attended college. The program aims to provide exposure to various medical professions, aiding students in making informed decisions about their future in medicine. Participants engage with medical guest speakers and participate in hands-on activities, gaining a practical understanding of the field. Housing accommodations are not included. The program fee is $1200, with scholarships available based on financial need. Applications must be submitted by March 30, 2023, and successful candidates will be notified by April 17, 2023.
requirements: The Pre-Med Summer Scholar Program is designed for US high school students who are interested in pursuing a career in medicine. Applicants must be at least 16 years old and not yet attending college.

title: Get Inspired Houston (GIH) Internship
text: Get Inspired Houston (GIH) is an annual summer internship program designed for young adults and college/university students who are passionate about supporting immigrant and refugee communities. This program offers a unique opportunity for participants to develop their professional skills in non-profit management while actively contributing to Sewa's ongoing community projects. Through GIH, young adults gain hands-on experience in various aspects of non-profit operations, including program planning, fundraising, outreach, and community engagement. The program empowers participants to make a meaningful impact on the lives of vulnerable populations while fostering their personal and professional growth.
requirements: unknown

title: High School Summer Internship Program (HS-SIP)
text: The Summer Internship Program offers young individuals the chance to engage in full-time biomedical research alongside renowned scientists in a dedicated biomedical research environment. Interns are expected to contribute significantly to their research groups, working alongside postbacs, graduate students, and postdocs. Their efforts are crucial to the success of the group's research endeavors, as they are held to the same high standards of productivity and accountability as their more experienced colleagues.
requirements:
The 2023 High School Summer Internship Program is for students who
are seventeen (17) years of age or older by June 15, 2023 (No exceptions will be made.),
are high school juniors or seniors at the time of application,
are U.S. citizens or permanent residents (U.S. citizens may apply if they are enrolled at least half-time in high school. Permanent residents must be enrolled in a high school in the U.S. to be eligible.), and
if they will be 17 years of age on June 15, 2023, at the time of application live within 40 miles of the NIH campus on which they will intern. (This requirement does not apply to applicants who are 18 and older.)*
*NHLBI, NCATS, and NIEHS will not host high school summer interns during summer 2023

In order to be approved for logical and physical access to NIH facilities and systems, candidates must be able to pass a Federal background check, using Standard Form-85 (read SF-85). NOTE: Section 14 of the form asks “In the last year, have you used, possessed, supplied, or manufactured illegal drugs?” The question pertains to the illegal use of drugs or controlled substances in accordance with Federal laws, even though permissible under state laws.

title: Internship Program
text: Oak Hill offers a comprehensive suite of services tailored to individuals with disabilities, catering to all ages from infancy to advanced years. Internships are available in diverse areas, including Chapter 126 Sports & Fitness, the New England Assistive Technology Center, Group Homes, Day Programs, Oak Hill School, Administrative/Office, and Summer Camp. These internships provide students with hands-on experience in supporting individuals with disabilities, fostering their growth and understanding of the field.
requirements: unknown

title: Malott Family Zoo Intern Program
text: The Malott Family Zoo Intern Program offers a paid seven-week internship for Chicago high school students aged 15-18 who are interested in exploring animal and conservation science at Lincoln Park Zoo. Interns will engage with researchers and Animal Care staff, gaining insights into potential careers in animal science. They will also develop a culminating project that investigates informal education techniques and effective communication of conservation messages to zoo visitors. To be eligible, applicants must be Chicago residents, legally authorized to work in the US, and available for all training days during the first two weeks of the internship. Interested students can attend informational sessions or a job fair at the zoo, or participate in a virtual opportunity fair hosted by Adler Planetarium.
requirements: To be considered for the Malott Family Zoo Intern Program, an applicant must meet certain requirements. First, they must be a City of Chicago resident. Second, they must be entering grades 10-12 or their freshman year of college in fall 2023. Third, they must be 15-18 years old by June 26, 2023. Additionally, they must be legally allowed to work in the United States and have proof of identity and authorization to work in accordance with federal law. If hired, 15-year-old interns must obtain a student work permit. Program participants must also be available for all days of training during the first two weeks of the program. Planned absences that do not occur during training are possible with supervisor approval, but long absences may disqualify a candidate from the program.

title: Mikva Summer Fellowship
text: As a Mikva Summer Fellow, you will engage in a paid summer internship within the office of a city, county, state, or federal lawmaker. Working 30 hours weekly for six weeks between late June and early August, you will receive $15 per hour. Beyond the internship, you will join a professional development cohort dedicated to honing work readiness skills such as communication, collaboration, critical thinking, public speaking, and teamwork. Weekly meetings with Mikva staff will guide you in setting career goals, completing workforce readiness assessments, and monitoring your progress throughout the program.
requirements: To apply to this program, you must be between 17-20, live in Chicago or Cook County, and meet IDHS criteria for employment.

title: Technology Support – Student Interns
text: The Building Technology Support – Student Intern assists the Building Technology Specialist and District Technology Support Services by providing technical support to students and staff. Responsibilities include answering technology-related inquiries, repairing damaged hardware such as computers, Chromebooks, and tablets, and offering general technology assistance. This internship is exclusively available to high school students enrolled in the Career Launch program.
address: 6101 Scandia Trail N. Forest Lake, MN 55025
requirements: unknown

title: LLRISE Workshop
text: The Lincoln Laboratory Radar Introduction for Student Engineers program (LLRISE) is a two-week summer workshop designed for rising high school seniors. This free, project-based enrichment program is tailored for exceptional students currently in their junior year of high school. LLRISE provides students with an immersive experience in building small radar systems, fostering creative problem-solving strategies. Participants collaborate with highly skilled scientists and engineers to develop the necessary skills for constructing a Doppler and range radar. The program takes place on both the MIT campus in Cambridge, MA, and Lincoln Laboratory in Lexington, MA. Students reside in MIT dormitories from Sunday, July 9th, to Saturday, July 22nd. While the program is free of charge, participants are responsible for their transportation arrangements. To be eligible, students must be US citizens with a strong passion for science, math, and engineering.
requirements: The Lincoln Laboratory Radar Introduction for Student Engineers (LLRISE) program selects outstanding students who are passionate about science, math, and engineering and currently completing their junior year in high school. As the program is intended for U.S. citizens only, foreign citizens who are permanent residents are not eligible. The program is free of cost, however, participants have to pay for their transportation to and from MIT. LLRISE is a two-week summer workshop, typically held in the last week of July, where students acquire hands-on experience to build small radar systems while working with highly talented scientists and engineers. To be considered for the program, the applicant must apply online , and upload their supporting materials (transcripts, copy of test scores, and essays), and their math and science teachers must fill out the recommendation form.

title: Vocational Internship Program
text: The Vocational Internship Program (VIP), offered by the Massachusetts Clean Energy Center, provides paid clean energy internships for vocational high school students during the academic year. Through this program, students gain valuable work experience and compensation while attending school. Additionally, they establish connections and network with professionals in the clean energy industry, enhancing their prospects for future employment. The internship duration aligns with the school year, and students may commence their internship after the session start date with the approval of their Co-Op Coordinator and the Clean Energy Employer. Eligibility criteria include being a rising senior actively enrolled in a Massachusetts vocational or technical high school and having approval for co-op participation from the school administration.
requirements: The Massachusetts Vocational Internship Program (VIP) seeks to place students in paid clean energy internships during the academic year. To be eligible for the program, applicants must be a rising senior attending a vocational or technical high school in Massachusetts and be approved to participate in a co-op program by their school's administration. Individuals who are not in good standing with their school, current full- or part-time employees of the potential host employer, or family members of employers or owners of the host employer are not eligible to participate in the program. The program lasts for the duration of the school year, and students can start their internship after the session start date if this arrangement is agreed upon with their Co-Op Coordinator and the Clean Energy Employer. To apply, students must have their Co-op Coordinator submit an online application on their behalf and must have a profile in the student database for employers to confirm their eligibility with MassCEC for the program.

title: 8-Week Summer Internship for Rising Seniors
text: ISB offers a paid 8-week summer internship exclusively for current 11th graders, providing approximately 300 hours of formal work experience. Interns will engage in research projects aligned with ongoing ISB initiatives, guided by expert mentors. Potential internship topics encompass computational biology in healthcare and environmental contexts, microbial interactions, complex systems resilience and collapse, the microbiome, microbial evolution, cancer, systems medicine, and bioengineering with algae. Through these projects, students will gain insights into systems biology and apply their knowledge to real-world research endeavors.
requirements: Rising high school seniors eligible.

title: AMRI High School Summer Research Program
text: The AMRI High School Summer Research Program offers an exclusive 8-week experience for high school students to engage in research alongside esteemed scientists in fields including chemistry, physics, materials science, and engineering. Participants have the flexibility to pursue individual research projects or collaborate as part of a team, delving into both fundamental and applied research topics. This immersive program provides students with hands-on experience, fostering their scientific curiosity and equipping them with valuable skills in experimental design, data analysis, and scientific communication.
requirements: Must be in high school

title: Executive and General Positions
text: At Medicine Encompassed, a student-led 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization, we welcome high school students (grades 9-12) from diverse backgrounds worldwide. Our mission is to provide opportunities for students with a passion for STEAM, biology, and medicine. We believe that fostering their interests in these fields is crucial for their future careers. Our organization accepts members on a national and international scale, ensuring that all students with a prospective career in medicine have access to our resources and support.
requirements: We are seeking multifaceted individuals with a fervor for biology, medicine, the sciences, and/or the general branches of STEM, and also fully support our mission statement! We encourage everyone to apply for a general department position, or medical committee position - we are always looking for diverse applicants that will complement our growing team.

title: SeA Bilingual STEM Camp
text: The SeA Bilingual STEM Camp, sponsored by Berkeley Lab K-12, is a complimentary four-day program tailored for English learning/Spanish-English bilingual high school students (grades 10-12) with an interest in STEM and Berkeley Lab career opportunities. The program encompasses guided tours of Berkeley Lab facilities, professional career discussions with scientists, and workshops held at both Berkeley Lab and UC Berkeley. The SeA program is a hybrid program, commencing online on April 5th and transitioning to on-site activities at Berkeley Lab and UC Berkeley on April 6th-7th and 8th, respectively. Participants will be transported from downtown Berkeley, and all necessary materials and meals will be provided. Berkeley Lab K-12 also offers additional programs catering to various grade levels, including virtual options.
requirements: To be considered for the SeA Bilingual STEM Camp at Berkeley Lab, applicants must be English-learning/Spanish-English bilingual students in grades 10 to 12 who are interested in STEM and career opportunities at Berkeley Lab. The program is free and provides all materials and meals. Applications are open from December 5 to February 12, and volunteers can also apply. The program includes tours of Berkeley Lab facilities, career talks with scientists, and workshops both at Berkeley Lab and UC Berkeley, and it is expected to be a hybrid program, starting online and moving on-site to Berkeley Lab and UC Berkeley. The schedule currently includes a virtual program on Wednesday from 6pm-8pm, and on-site programs from Thursday to Saturday from 9am-5pm with virtual alternatives from 9am-3pm. All participants are required to follow COVID-19 protocols, including proof of vaccination and/or testing.

title: Young Scientist Program (YSP) Summer Focus
text: Since 1991, the Summer Focus program has offered eight-week summer research internships at Washington University in St. Louis to highly motivated high school students in the Greater St. Louis area. Each Scholar is paired with two scientists: a Mentor, who guides them on a specific laboratory project, and a Tutor, who provides support throughout their research experience. Scholars also enhance their science communication skills and college application preparation through two courses. Washington University graduate students, post-doctoral associates, laboratory staff, and principal investigators serve as Mentors and Tutors, ensuring a comprehensive and supportive research environment for the Scholars.
host: Division of Biology & Biomedical Sciences at Washington University in St. Louis
requirements: Applicants must be rising juniors or seniors, reside in the St. Louis metropolitan area, have a minimum GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale, and have completed at least one year of biology or chemistry. Additionally, they must be interested in pursuing a career in science, technology, engineering, or math (STEM) and be committed to attending and actively participating in all program activities, which include scientific lectures, lab training, research projects, and presentations. Finally, they must submit a completed application form, academic transcripts, two letters of recommendation, and a personal statement explaining their interests, goals, and qualifications for the program. The selection process is highly competitive and based on academic excellence, motivation, dedication, and potential for success in STEM fields.

title: Riverside Teen Corps Horticulture Internship Program
text: Riverside Park Conservancy offers a paid experiential learning program during the summer for high school volunteers seeking to acquire fundamental horticultural knowledge and skills. Under the guidance of Conservancy staff, volunteers engage in the upkeep of crucial park areas, contribute to ecological restoration initiatives, and prepare sites for upcoming fall planting projects. Through this program, volunteers gain hands-on experience in horticulture, contribute to the preservation of the park's ecosystem, and develop a deeper understanding of the importance of urban green spaces.
address: 475 Riverside Dr Suite #455, New York, NY 10115, United States
requirements: unknown

title: Student Internship
text: The Bergen County Sheriff's Office provides internship opportunities for qualified high school and college students, offering them practical experience in law enforcement. Interns work in various settings within Bergen County's largest law enforcement agency, gaining valuable insights while developing their individual talents and skills. This program allows students to contribute to the community while enhancing their knowledge and abilities in the field of law enforcement.
requirements:
Be a current resident of or attend school in Bergen County
Be enrolled in a high school or college internship program
Contact your high school or college internship coordinator to ensure that all school requirements will be met
**Prior to submitting an application, please call the Community Outreach Unit at 201-336-3540 to ensure we are accepting applications for the semester in which you are interested.**

title: High School Apprenticeship Program
text: The High School Apprenticeship Program provides New York City public high school students with an immersive experience that combines academic study with hands-on work in the Museum. After rigorous spring training, Apprentices engage in part-time employment (four days per week) during the summer, gaining exposure to various Museum departments. They lead tours, delve into curatorial and educational practices, and explore administrative and operational aspects of the institution. Through this program, Apprentices gain a comprehensive understanding of Jewish heritage and the inner workings of a museum, fostering their personal and professional growth.
address: Edmond J. Safra Plaza, 36 Battery Place, New York, NY 10280
requirements: unknown

title: Simons Summer Research Program
text: The Simons Summer Research Program provides academically exceptional and driven high school students with the opportunity to immerse themselves in hands-on research in science, mathematics, or engineering at Stony Brook University. Under the guidance of renowned faculty mentors, Simons Fellows acquire laboratory techniques and tools, integrate into active research teams, and experience the dynamic environment of a research university. Through this program, students gain invaluable insights into the research process, foster their scientific curiosity, and develop a deeper understanding of their chosen fields.
requirements:
Students interested in science who have demonstrated independence, creativity and an aptitude for doing hands-on work are especially encouraged to apply. Applicants must currently be in their junior year (11th grade) of high school at the time of applying; must be US citizens and/or permanent residents; and must be at least 16 years of age by the start of the program.
(no exceptions )

title: KU Medical Center Educational Experience (KEE)
text: The research experience provides an immersive glimpse into the realm of medical research. Participants can choose their level of involvement: Research Observational Learners observe research activities without hands-on participation, while Research Active Learners actively engage in research tasks. Clinical observation experiences offer the opportunity to witness healthcare professionals in action, with no hands-on involvement allowed. Academic credit is not awarded for these experiences, which are limited to 12 hours. Eligibility is restricted to University of Kansas Medical Center employees and students, as well as health system employees. Health system employees should coordinate directly with the sponsoring department, bypassing the KEE application process.
requirements: You must be a U.S. citizen, permanent resident or DACA recipient age 16 or older to participate in the program. Minors, those less than 18 years of age, must have the permission of their parent(s) or guardian(s) to participate. Background checks are required for all program participants age 18 and older.

title: Adler Planetarium Teen Internship Program
text: The Adler Planetarium offers a range of STEAM-based programs tailored for teenagers, fostering personal growth and scientific exploration. Far Horizons Teens engages high school students in workshops on electronic circuitry, computer programming, structural design, and teamwork, tackling the issue of light pollution. The Summer Internship Program immerses students in professional museum roles. Mission Near Space, a summer camp, transforms teens into engineers and astronomers, launching scientific payloads into the stratosphere via high-altitude balloons. The Youth Leadership Council (YLC) empowers young advocates with a platform to amplify "youth voice" within the museum community. Lastly, the Youth Organization for Lights Out (YOLO), in collaboration with Enlace Chicago, provides after-school STEAM learning and environmental justice initiatives, with a focus on light pollution.
requirements: To be considered for the Adler Planetarium's summer internship program for high school students, applicants must be currently enrolled in high school during the 2022-2023 school year (8th graders and college students are not eligible). They must demonstrate an interest in building professional skills in a supportive and fun environment and show excitement towards working collaboratively as part of a team. Applicants must be available for all on-site program dates and attend an orientation. In addition to the summer internship, the Adler Planetarium offers other teen programs throughout the year, each with their specific requirements, such as the Mission Near Space program, which is open to applicants in 7th-8th grade attending a Chicago Public School. All participants must be COVID-19 vaccinated, unless they request and are granted a medical or religious exemption.

title: Grant Intern
text: This internship opportunity at NAMI Mississippi will contribute significantly to the organization's preparation for the upcoming fiscal year's grant proposals. The intern will be responsible for updating the organizational overview, developing separate templates for each program, conducting research to identify new grant prospects, and assisting with grant management. The well-written templates created by the intern will provide staff with the flexibility to respond promptly to grant opportunities throughout the year, ensuring that NAMI Mississippi can continue to secure funding for its vital programs and services.
requirements: unknown

title: Art Institute of Chicago Teen Council Leadership Program
text: The Art Institute Teen Council invites 15 creative high school students to join their ranks and contribute their unique perspectives to the museum. As part of this council, teens will collaborate to develop programs and resources that enhance the Art Institute's appeal, accessibility, and relevance for Chicagoland youth. Past Teen Council initiatives have included teen art exhibitions, overnight museum stays, teen-oriented parties, and an audio guide specifically designed for teenagers. By joining the Teen Council, participants will have the opportunity to shape the future of the Art Institute's offerings for young people, leaving a lasting impact on the museum's connection with the community.
address:
Art Institute of Chicago
111 South Michigan Avenue
Chicago, Illinois 60603
requirements: Must be a Chicago high school teen who will be at least 15.

title: Los Angeles County Office of Education's Career Technical Education
text: The Los Angeles County Office of Education (LACOE) provides technical assistance, curriculum/professional development, and monitoring/documentation/reporting services to school districts throughout the county through its Career Technical Education (CTE) internship program. This program aims to equip students with the knowledge and skills necessary for career training, post-secondary education, and the workforce. The program offers courses that integrate technical training and academics, emphasizing problem-solving and real-world relevance in 15 highly employable industry sectors. For further information, schools and individuals can contact LACOE's CTE program at (562) 922-6850 or directly email CTE staff using the email addresses provided in the newsletter.
address: Contact the Career Technical Education department at (562) 922-6850 for further information.
host: Los Angeles County Office of Education's Career Technical Education
requirements: Have a strong interest in career technical education and workforce development. Candidates must have excellent communication and organizational skills, be able to work well independently and as part of a team, and have proficient computer skills. Additionally, candidates should have a demonstrated interest in education and be committed to improving access and equity in educational opportunities. Candidates must also be able to provide their own transportation to the internship site, which may be located in various parts of Los Angeles County.

title: Stanford Medical Youth Science Program
text: The Stanford Medical Youth Science Program (SMYSP) is an academic enrichment program designed for students from underrepresented backgrounds with limited financial means. Over a five-week period, participants engage in a comprehensive curriculum that includes lectures from Stanford Medicine faculty, professional development workshops, networking events, and a research project focused on health disparities. This program aims to provide students with an immersive experience in the field of medicine, fostering their interest in pursuing careers in healthcare and addressing health inequities.
requirements: Open to low-income, first-generation high school juniors who live in Northern California.

title: THE ACT PROGRAM AT SLO REP TEEN INTERNSHIP
text: The internship program at ACT provides leadership opportunities for teens aged 14-18 within the theatre and classroom settings, supporting ACT's programs. This mutually beneficial experience allows interns to collaborate with professional actors, directors, choreographers, and instructors, gaining valuable teaching artist training and mentoring. Interns can enhance their resumes, fulfill volunteer hour requirements, serve as role models for young actors, and share their theatrical knowledge. Additionally, they receive discounted tuition for their own ACT classes or camps, further enriching their artistic development.
address: 888 Morro Street, San Luis Obispo, CA 93401
requirements: As a volunteer intern, you can work the hours and weeks that best fit your schedule. When you fill out your application, you’ll have the option to select a full day (8:45am-4:15pm) or half day (mornings 8:45am-12:15pm or afternoons 12:45-4:15pm). Please note, however, that we will prioritize working with interns who are able to commit to a full week (or more) of camp. During the application process you’ll be asked for your experience working in theatre and with kids (if you don’t have any experience, please don’t let that deter your from applying!). You’ll also be asked for your general availability. Once we’ve received your application, we’ll be in touch to set up a short and informal video interview.

title: High School Honors Science, Math and Engineering Program (HSHSP)
text: The High School Honors Science, Engineering, and Mathematics Program (HSHSP), hosted by Michigan State University, is a non-credit enrichment program designed for mature high school juniors with a keen interest in science, mathematics, or engineering. As the oldest continuously running program of its kind in the United States, HSHSP offers an unparalleled opportunity for students to delve into challenging problems and experience the multifaceted nature of the research process. Participants engage in research under the guidance of university researchers, fostering a deeper understanding of inquiry-based learning. The program spans seven weeks, with selection based on academic excellence, maturity, demonstrated interest in STEM fields, and completion of specific high school coursework. While the participant fee is $4,000, scholarships are available for those with financial need.
address: Michigan State University Campus - East Lansing, Michigan
host: Department of Teacher Education of Michigan State University
requirements: The program typically accepts 24 participants who will spend seven weeks in Michigan State University’s campus, working on their individual research projects mentored by researchers and graduate students.

title: Seasonal Positions & Front Office Openings
text: The Hartford Yard Goats, a Minor League Baseball team based in Hartford, Connecticut, are renowned as a leading employer within the Eastern League. The Yard Goats have cultivated an exceptional reputation for providing unparalleled service to their community. Their clientele consistently engages in business with the team due to the exceptional experiences they offer. The Yard Goats attribute their success to the exceptional staff they employ, who are dedicated to delivering a top-notch experience for all.
requirements: Requirements vary by position

title: York College Now STEM Research Academy
text: The College Now STEM Research Academy at York College offers an immersive research experience for students. Spanning two semesters (spring to summer), the program begins with a spring Backyard Toxicology course, where students develop foundational skills in formulating research questions, designing experiments, conducting literature searches, and interpreting scientific literature. This prepares them for the subsequent summer research component, where they engage in authentic research projects under the guidance of faculty mentors.
requirements:
Must be a NYC public high school students in good standing
Have an 80+ on Math Regents and 75+ on the Living Environment and ELA Regents
Be a high school junior and recommended by a high school administrator or teacher

title: STEM Academy at Oak Ridge
text: The ARC Appalachian STEM Academy at Oak Ridge offers immersive summer programs for high school and middle school students, as well as teachers. High school students and teachers participate in a two-week program, while middle school students engage in a one-week experience. Participants delve into hands-on, inquiry-based projects in STEM fields, collaborating with experienced educators to leverage technology in answering research questions. The program exposes students to college opportunities and the cultural and historical significance of the Appalachian region. The culmination of the program features group presentations where students and teachers showcase their projects and research findings. Additionally, the Bridge Program provides a two-week residential experience for 8th graders who have completed the middle school program but are not yet eligible for the high school program.
address: 5200, 1 Bethel Valley Rd, Oak Ridge, TN 37830
host: ARC (Appalachian Regional Commission) Appalachian STEM Academy at Oak Ridge
requirements: To be considered for the ARC Appalachian STEM Academy at Oak Ridge internship program, applicants must be middle or high school students or teachers from the Appalachian region with an interest in STEM-related fields. To qualify for the high school program, applicants must be able to commit to the two-week summer program, while middle school students are required to participate for one week. Those who have completed the middle school program as eighth graders can apply for the Bridge Program, which is also a two-week residential experience. The program includes hands-on learning experiences that involve working with scientists from Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) and other STEM experts in the region. Participants are expected to work on inquiry-based, applied projects in science, math, and research-related computer technology. The program also promotes teamwork, exposes students to college opportunities, and cultivates cultural richness and historical importance of the Appalachian region. The program culminates in group presentations where students and teachers discuss their projects and research findings.

title: Junior Curators
text: The Junior Curators program offers an immersive internship experience for high school students (grades 9-12) with a passion for conservation, animal care, and field biology. Participants collaborate with like-minded peers to actively support the North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences' conservation initiatives. The program encompasses educational programs, field experiences, and the care of the Museum's live animal collection. It runs from September to April and includes mandatory monthly meetings with Living Collections staff and two group meetings with guest scientists, researchers, and curators. Optional trips, field experiences, and service projects across North Carolina and beyond are available, along with an annual group retreat and graduation event. The program requires a $75 annual fee, which covers meeting snacks, a Junior Curator t-shirt, and program equipment. Scholarships are available. The application deadline is March 20, and the program is highly competitive.
host: The North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences
requirements: To be considered for the Junior Curator program at the North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences, applicants must be in grades 9-12 during the 2023-2024 school year. They should have an intense interest in conservation, animal care, and field biology. Junior Curators must commit to attending one required monthly meeting with Living Collections staff, two required monthly group meetings with guest scientists and researchers to explore natural science topics, optional trips, field experiences, and service projects across North Carolina and beyond at an additional fee, and an annual group retreat in August and graduation event in May. The fee for the program is $75 per year, which covers equipment, snacks for meetings, and a Junior Curator t-shirt. Scholarships are available upon contacting Lynn Cross for more information. The application deadline is Monday, March 20 at 5:00 pm, and group interviews will be held on March 27, 28, and 29. The program is highly competitive, and selected applicants will be expected to uphold the required volunteer time commitment and attend all meetings and volunteer shifts.

title: CATALYST Academy
text: CATALYST Academy offers a transformative one-week residential experience for aspiring high school juniors and seniors seeking an immersive introduction to engineering. Participants reside in Cornell dormitories, engaging with current Cornell Engineering students and faculty. They connect with a diverse cohort from across the nation, fostering a vibrant learning community. Through hands-on projects, interactive workshops, and campus tours, CATALYST Scholars gain firsthand insights into the field of engineering, exploring its applications and the challenges it addresses. This immersive program provides a unique opportunity for students to experience college life, expand their knowledge, and ignite their passion for engineering.
address: Carpenter Hall, 313 Campus Rd, Ithaca, NY 14853

title: Summer High School Institute
text: Since 1985, Wyoming's rising junior students have been presented with the UW Summer High School Institute (HSI), an opportunity to experience college life firsthand. HSI's mission is to foster holistic development in young adults, extending beyond academic pursuits. The program's philosophy emphasizes the cultivation of the whole person, recognizing that growth encompasses intellectual, social, and personal dimensions.
requirements: Be in the 10th grade at a public or private high school in Wyoming or homeschooled; Be current residents of Wyoming; intend to return to a Wyoming school for the next term; and be committed to participate fully and remain for the entire three weeks of the program.

title: Wayne State Discovery to Cure High School Internship Program
text: The Wayne State Discovery to Cure High School Internship Program is an 8-week program designed for rising high school seniors aged 16 or older. Located at Wayne State University's C.S. Mott Center for Human Growth and Development, this program offers students the opportunity to conduct high-quality life science research and explore biomedical research careers. Upon acceptance, interns are paired with a mentor and assigned an individual research project, which they work on for at least 6 weeks. Interns are required to attend mandatory training and seminars and participate in Research Presentation Day/Closing Ceremonies, where they present their research findings in a 10-minute oral presentation. The program does not provide housing or transportation, and students are responsible for their own arrangements.
address: C.S. Mott Center for Human Growth and Development in Detroit, MI
host: C.S. Mott Center for Human Growth and Development at the Wayne State University School of Medicine
requirements: To be eligible for the Wayne State Discovery to Cure High School Internship Program, applicants must be rising seniors who are at least 16 years old at the time of the program (during the summer between junior and senior year of high school). The program is highly competitive and interested students should attend the Open House in March and fill out the online application. The program typically lasts 8 weeks from June to August, though students are required to be in attendance for at least 6 weeks. Throughout the program, students are assigned a mentor and individual research project in one of the departments of the School of Medicine. They are expected to attend all mandatory training and seminars and fulfill their research obligations, culminating in a 10-minute oral presentation on Research Presentation Day. While the program cannot provide assistance for housing, transportation, or visa processing, international students can receive an acceptance letter for visa application purposes. Participation in other summer programs that interfere with the Discovery to Cure Internship Program is not permitted.

title: High School Intern Program
text: Engage in cutting-edge biomedical science research under the guidance of a dedicated mentor, delving into fields such as infectious disease, neuroscience, molecular biology, immunology, cancer, stem cell research, and developmental biology. Hone your science communication abilities and expand your professional network through interactions with scientists and the UCSF community. Join a cohort of 25 High School Interns and benefit from college counseling support, including personal statement writing workshops and individual meetings to navigate college applications and explore higher education options.
host: UCSF Science and Health Education Partnership
requirements: Current high school juniors Enrolled in SFUSD or an SF charter school or College Track SF participant. Individuals from backgrounds underrepresented in the sciences.

title: Summer Challenge
text: For rising high school sophomores, juniors, and seniors, an exceptional residential summer program awaits. Immerse yourself in college life for two unforgettable weeks, tackling academic challenges on campus. Alternatively, for those unable to attend in person, a limited selection of remote Summer Challenge seminars offers the opportunity to engage in the program from home.
requirements: Rising high school sophomore, junior or senior

title: Youth Community Groups
text: Teens Making A Difference (TMAD) is a Service Club that empowers students aged 12-18 to make a positive impact in their schools and communities. Through TMAD, students engage in service projects, develop leadership abilities, and work towards improving their surroundings. The club has received national recognition for its innovative approach to local government, earning the Transforming Local Government Innovation Award. TMAD's mission is to foster a spirit of service and empower young people to become active and engaged citizens, making a tangible difference in their communities.
requirements: High school youth ages 14-18.

title: Youth Arts Enterprise
text: Artists For Humanity, a Boston-based nonprofit, provides artistic job opportunities for teens. Through mentorship, teens collaborate on client-tailored solutions in various creative studios, including painting, 3D design, graphic design, printmaking, creative technology, video production, and photography. Applications are open to teens with a passion for creativity and community service, regardless of prior artistic experience. To qualify, teens must attend a Boston Public School or reside in Boston, be at least 14 years old, commit to regular program hours, and complete an unpaid apprenticeship before becoming paid employees. Interested teens can attend Open House tours to learn more about the organization and meet the team.
requirements: To qualify for the Teen Jobs - Artists for Humanity internship program, applicants must be at least 14 years old and either attending a Boston public school or residing in Boston. They must be able to attend the program's regular hours, which are Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday from 3:00 p.m. - 6:00 p.m. during the school year, and Monday-Friday from 12:00 noon - 5:30 p.m. during summer. Additionally, they must be able to complete an unpaid apprenticeship period of 36 hours before becoming a paid employee. The apprenticeship doubles up as community service hours. Applicants with a passion for creativity and learning on the job, regardless of their artistic experience, are encouraged to apply. Finally, interested teens should attend one of AFH’s Open House tours, fill out an online job application, complete an Orientation & Interview, and successfully complete their apprenticeship.

title: Research Science Institute (RSI)
text: The Research Science Institute (RSI), hosted at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), is an intensive summer program designed for high school juniors with a passion for science and engineering. As the first cost-free program of its kind, RSI offers a comprehensive experience that combines on-campus coursework in scientific theory with off-campus research internships. Participants engage in the entire research cycle, from reviewing current literature to drafting research plans and presenting their findings in conference-style reports. The program comprises a week of STEM classes led by renowned professors, followed by a five-week internship where students conduct individual projects under the mentorship of experienced scientists and researchers. The culmination of the program is a week dedicated to preparing and presenting written and oral reports on their research projects. RSI provides an exceptional opportunity for high school students to gain invaluable research experience, explore their scientific interests, and prepare for a future in science and technology.
requirements: The Research Science Institute (RSI) is a cost-free summer science and engineering program for high school juniors interested in hands-on experience in scientific research. The program combines coursework in scientific theory with off-campus research work that allows participants to experience the entire research cycle from start to finish. To be considered for RSI, high school juniors need to submit their applications by the deadline specified each year. Applicants must be high school juniors at the time of application and must demonstrate high academic achievement, particularly in science and math courses. Acceptance to RSI is highly competitive, with only 100 students selected each year from a pool of outstanding applicants.

title: High School Intern Program Research
text: NIST research is divided into six organizational laboratories that conduct research in a wide range of physical and engineering sciences. These laboratories respond to industry needs for measurement methods, tools, data, and technology. Notably, six of these laboratories participate in the SHIP program, which provides opportunities for high school students to engage in hands-on research experiences and gain valuable insights into the field of science.
host: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
requirements: Interested students must want to participate in scientific research. In addition, they must currently be juniors or seniors (at time of application) who will have advanced to senior status or graduated from high school by the start of the program. A minimum GPA of 3.0 is required for consideration into this program

title: Explorers Teen Program
text: The Explorers Program is a comprehensive college, career, and life readiness program designed for Newark-area high school students. Through a curriculum that leverages the Museum's extensive collections, resources, and staff, the program empowers students to develop essential skills and enhance their self-confidence. By engaging with the Museum's unique offerings, students gain valuable experiences that prepare them for success in higher education, the workforce, and beyond.
requirements:
Must be a rising freshman, sophomore, or
junior within Newark-area

title: Louis Stokes Internship Program
text: The Louis Stokes Internship Program, offered by the Cleveland Clinic, is a competitive summer internship opportunity for high school students. This program aims to provide an immersive research experience in the biomedical field, allowing students to delve into the Cleveland Clinic's research environment. Through this program, students gain hands-on experience in biomedical research, fostering their interest in the field and equipping them with valuable skills for future endeavors.
requirements: Must have completed the 8th grade and be enrolled in a high school

title: M.I.N.D.S. (Medical Internship Navigating Diversity and Science)
text: M.I.N.D.S. (Medical Internship Navigating Diversity and Science) is a six-week paid internship program designed for underrepresented or financially disadvantaged high school juniors and seniors who aspire to pursue a career in medicine. This immersive experience provides participants with hands-on exposure to the medical field through rotations in various healthcare settings, including hospitals, clinics, and research laboratories. The program aims to foster a diverse and inclusive environment that supports students from underrepresented backgrounds and empowers them to succeed in their future medical endeavors.
requirements:
Must begin their junior or senior year in September 2023
Must identify as African American, Latinos/Hispanic American, and Native American (American Indian, Alaska Native, or Native Hawaiian), first generation, OR financially disadvantaged
Must complete an application
Must submit an unofficial transcript with a cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher

title: Social Justice Internship
text: City Mission's Social Justice Internship Program empowers high school students and recent graduates to become agents of change in Boston. Through a hybrid model offered in summer (6 weeks) or fall/spring (12 weeks), interns engage in group collaborations and independent research to dismantle systems of oppression. They participate in conferences and workshops, amplify their voices for collective liberation, and work on a presentation project of their choosing. Positive news discussions, event collaborations, and conversations with local and national leaders foster growth, connections, and learning. The program adapts to interns' interests and ideas, offering a stipend of $15 per hour for 15 hours per week (summer) or 5 hours per week (fall/spring).
requirements: To be considered for the Social Justice Internship Program at City Mission, applicants must be high school students who will be going into grades 11 and 12 and selected sophomores in and around the city of Boston. The internship program requires a commitment of 5 hours per week for 12 weeks. Applicants will be selected based on their commitment to creating change and their interest in gaining work experience in a small nonprofit organization that works towards dismantling systems of oppression and creating collective liberation. The program is designed to provide a safe, diverse, and social activism-oriented space for high school students to learn about ongoing events related to social justice issues, amplify their voices, and create changes in their communities. The interns will participate in conferences, workshops, and activities to educate and train them to become effective change-makers. The program also invites local and national leaders to have conversations with the interns so they can learn, grow, and create connections.

title: Upward Bound Math Science Summer Program
text: The Upward Bound and Upward Bound Math Science Summer Program provides high school students with an immersive college experience. This six-week residential program, offered at no cost to participants, introduces students to college-level academics through hands-on experiences. The program fosters a sense of community and creates lasting memories while equipping students with the knowledge and skills necessary for success in higher education.

title: High School Health Careers Program (HSHCP)
text: The High School Health Careers Program (HSHCP) is a four-week, tuition-free, residential program designed to provide current sophomore and junior high school students with an immersive experience in the fields of Biomedical Research, Biotechnology, and the health professions (BBHP). This program aims to enhance participants' academic study and communication skills while exposing them to the diverse career opportunities within the BBHP sector.
requirements: The program targets Massachusetts high school sophomores and juniors from groups that are under-represented in BBHP and/or disadvantaged backgrounds. The program is open to Massachusetts residents who are sophomores or juniors in a Massachusetts high school.

title: Art Institute of Chicago Summer Internship
text: For art enthusiasts and museum enthusiasts alike, the Art Institute offers a summer internship opportunity for teens to collaborate with peers and contribute to the museum's vibrant offerings. Interns will assist with festivals, gallery tours, and workshops, engaging with museum professionals, exploring behind-the-scenes operations, and immersing themselves in the world-renowned collection. They will have the chance to interact with local artists, plan and execute creative programs, and gain valuable insights into the museum's mission of serving local and international visitors.

Art Institute of Chicago

Chicago, Illinois 60603

title: Health Sciences Enrichment Institute
text: The Health Science Enrichment Institute (HSEI) is a five-week summer program hosted on the University of Kansas Medical Center campus. Designed for incoming college freshmen and sophomores, HSEI provides additional instruction and exposure to various science courses and personal development topics. Academic components include Biology, Anatomy, Microbiology, Introduction to Research, and Introduction to Medicine. Non-academic components encompass Time Management and Study Skills, sessions with a diverse student population and practicing health professionals, and Clinical Skills Training.
requirements: Acceptance to or current enrollment as a freshman or sophomore in an institution of higher education. A minimum of 3.0 G.P.A. on a 4.0 scale is required at the college level or 3.0 G.P.A. at the high school level. Completion of at least one science course, one math course and one English course or its equivalent at the college level, or completion of at least two sciences and two math courses at the high school level is mandatory. Applicants must demonstrate a commitment to diversity.

title: Observers/Job Shadows
text: The Children's Hospital of Wisconsin offers job shadowing opportunities for high school students who aspire to pursue healthcare careers. This program allows students to observe healthcare professionals in various roles within the hospital setting, gaining firsthand experience and insights into the field. Additionally, the program incorporates educational seminars that provide students with a comprehensive understanding of healthcare professions, career paths, and the latest advancements in the industry. Through this immersive experience, students can explore their interests, develop valuable skills, and make informed decisions about their future in healthcare.
requirements: Must be 18 years old or older

title: Student Leader Program
text: As a Student Leader, you will embark on an eight-week paid internship at a local nonprofit organization, gaining firsthand insights into community needs and the vital role nonprofits play. This experience will equip you with invaluable civic, social, and business leadership skills. Additionally, you will attend the Student Leaders Summit in Washington, D.C., where you will delve into the collaborative efforts of government, business, and the nonprofit sector in addressing critical community challenges.
location: Locations Across the US, California, New York , New Jersey, Vermont, Massachusetts, Connecticut, Texas, Alaska, Arizona, Colorado, Alabama, Delaware, Arkansas, Idaho, Hawaii, Georgia, Illinois, Indiana, Kansas, Florida, Louisiana, Maryland, Michigan, Mississippi, Minnesota, Kentucky, Nevada, Montana, New Hampshire, New Mexico, North Carolina, North Dakota, Ohio, Nebraska, Oklahoma, Pennsylvania, Missouri, South Carolina, Tennessee, Virginia, Washington, West Virginia, South Dakota, Rhode Island, Utah, Wisconsin, Oregon, Iowa, Wyoming
requirements:
Currently be a junior or senior in high school
Live in one of the eligible markets listed
Be able to participate in an 8‐week paid internship at a local nonprofit/charitable organization and work 35 hours a week*
Be legally authorized to work in the US without sponsorship through the end of September 2023
Be able to participate in a week‐long Student Leadership Summit in Washington, DC (July 17-24, 2023) (All expenses paid as part of Student Leaders. This week will be part of your 8‐ week experience.)*
Be a student in good standing at your school

title: Education Curatorial Intern
text: This activity is open to all high school students who are interested in learning more about the field of engineering. Participants will have the opportunity to engage in hands-on activities, interact with industry professionals, and gain insights into the various disciplines within engineering. The program will provide a comprehensive overview of the field, covering topics such as mechanical, electrical, civil, and chemical engineering. Students will also have the chance to explore career pathways and network with potential employers.

title: The AEOP High School Apprenticeship
text: The AEOP High School Apprenticeship offers an unparalleled opportunity for students to immerse themselves in cutting-edge research and advanced laboratory environments. Through this unique program, apprentices spend their summer in university research labs or U.S. Army Research Laboratories and Centers, gaining hands-on experience alongside professional scientists and engineers. This immersive experience provides students with access to state-of-the-art facilities, mentorship from experts in their field, and the chance to contribute to groundbreaking research.
requirements: All participants must be current high school students who are U.S. citizens or permanent legal residents. Additional eligibility requirements vary by location.

title: Learning at the Bench (LAB) Jumpstart
text: The Lab Jumpstart program is designed to foster research skills and laboratory culture among students. From March to June, students engage in small-group laboratory experiments at the RockEDU teaching laboratory during after-school sessions. These experiments aim to enhance content knowledge and scientific abilities in preparation for their summer mentored research experience. The program culminates in an oral presentation where students showcase their research findings and demonstrate their scientific prowess.
requirements:
