Must be 16 years old at the start of the program
Must have a genuine interest in scientific research
In order to be eligible for participation, students must commit to the entirety of the program which runs from March through August

title: Work Study ND - High School Program
text: Our work-study internship program offers high school students a practical and immersive experience in the heavy equipment, agricultural equipment, and diesel technology industries. This program aims to provide students with firsthand knowledge and skills before they commit to a formal education and career in diesel technology. By participating in this internship, students gain valuable hands-on experience, allowing them to make informed decisions about their future educational and professional paths.
requirements:
Must be 16 years old, or older.

Must be present and on time for work

Pre-employment drug testing is conducted

High School students exploring diesel technology or parts/warehouse fields

Desire to explore diesel technology or parts warehouse area’s with intent to continue education in this field

title: High School Internship
text: The Brooklyn District Attorney's Office provides internships for high school, college, and legal students throughout the year. These competitive internships grant students the opportunity to experience the inner workings of a district attorney's office. Interns may assist in investigations, attend trials, prepare and compile documents and financial data, conduct and analyze legal research, and support community outreach programs.
address: 350 Jay Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201, DA's Action Center
requirements: unknown

title: HighTech Bound
text: The High School Summer Internship Program- HighTech Bound is a seven-week program designed for academically outstanding high school students seeking to earn income and gain invaluable computer technology experience. Hosted by the University of New Hampshire InterOperability Lab, the program offers students the opportunity to collaborate with global networking companies like Cisco, Hewlett Packard, Microsoft, and Motorola. Interns are exposed to disciplines in computer science, electrical engineering, and computer engineering provided by the University of New Hampshire. The program provides hands-on experience, visits to high-tech corporations, and one-on-one mentorship with UNH-IOL engineers. This internship is ideal for students entering their senior year of high school with an interest in computer networking, computer programming, and exploring career opportunities in STEM fields. Applications for the program must be submitted by February 28, 2023.
host: University of New Hampshire InterOperability Lab (UNH-IOL)
requirements: To be considered for the High School Summer Internship Program- HighTech Bound, applicants must be entering their senior year of high school and meet the academic requirements set by the University of New Hampshire InterOperability Lab. Additionally, applicants should be highly motivated, academically outstanding, and demonstrate an interest in computer technology and networking. The program is highly competitive, and preference is given to students who have experience in computer science or engineering. Interns should be able to work well in a team-oriented environment and possess excellent problem-solving and communication skills. Successful applicants will be offered a paid seven-week internship program and will have the opportunity to work with major networking corporations such as Cisco, Hewlett Packard, Microsoft, and Motorola.

title: Congresswoman Anna Eshoo's Student Advisory Board
text: The Student Advisory Board comprises high school students residing or studying within the 18th Congressional District. Previous boards have engaged in research and student polling on issues of youth significance, providing recommendations on proposed legislation in Congress. Their recent reports have delved into crucial topics such as alternative energy, economic matters, human rights, and the Innovation Agenda, demonstrating their commitment to addressing contemporary concerns and shaping the future.
requirements: Candidates are current high school freshmen, sophomores, juniors or seniors residing or attending school in the 18th Congressional District and are responsible, creative, enthusiastic, and dedicated.

title: Charleston Tours & Events Intern
text: Charleston Tours & Events offers a comprehensive range of top-rated experiences in Charleston, South Carolina. As a family-owned business, they provide 90-minute narrated Harbor Tours on the Carolina Belle, 2-hour Sailboat Cruises on the Schooner Pride, and Private Charters on the Charleston Lady and Charleston Princess. Additionally, they conduct Historic Bus Tours in downtown Charleston and to Boone Hall and Magnolia Plantations. Their services include a Customer Service center in their office and a Customer Service Kiosk at the Charleston Maritime Center. Successful candidates for their paid position will rotate through the organization, gaining experience in Customer Service, Sales & Marketing, and Operations on the docks and onboard their vessels. This opportunity provides insights into the hospitality industry and the entrepreneurial aspects of the tourism sector.
address: 11 Isabella St. Unit B, Charleston, SC 29403
requirements: Applicants must be rising seniors

title: High School Internships
text: The Marquette-Alger Regional Educational Service Agency Internship Program provides high school seniors with a non-remunerated work experience of 6-10 hours weekly at a local business or agency aligned with their career aspirations. Over 150 internship sites have hosted students in recent years, and successful completion of the Work-Based Learning Experience earns students high school credit. The internship offers invaluable real-world experience, networking opportunities, and assistance in determining a college major. Students are required to adhere to both internship and business site regulations and are responsible for their own transportation. To apply, students must submit an application, resume, and a recommendation from their school counselor. The internship program coordinator and the business or agency will then conduct an interview with the student.
host: Northern Michigan University's Career and Technical Education Department
requirements: To be considered for the high school internship program, applicants must be seniors and enrolled in the Marquette-Alger Regional Educational Service Agency (MARESA) Internship Program. The internship program is related to the student’s career pathway and students will intern between 6-10 hours per week in a non-paid work experience with a local business or agency. Students will receive high school credit for successful completion of the internship. Prior to the start of the internship, the student, parent, school, and business must all approve the training schedule and tasks. Additionally, students are expected to follow both the internship and business site attendance rules and policies and are responsible for their own transportation to and from their training site. The application process requires completion of an application, resumé, and a recommendation from the school counselor. If accepted, the student will interview with the internship program coordinator and then with a business or agency. High school juniors interested in applying for an internship during their senior year should contact their high school guidance counselor. Must be a high school senior, having a GPA of 2.5 or higher, following the attendance rules and policies of the internship and business site, being responsible for transportation to and from the training site, completing the application process including submitting a resume and recommendation from the school counselor, and interviewing with the internship program coordinator and a business or agency. The internship program is available only through MARESA and is specifically designed for students within the Marquette-Alger region in Michigan, USA.

title: Office of Workforce Development Student Training Program
text: The Office of Workforce Development Student Training Program at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute offers Boston public school students professional experience in healthcare through paid internships aligned with their interests. Available as both an academic-year commitment and a summer opportunity, the program provides valuable professional and personal skills development. Students benefit from mentorship, student retreats, and college tours, fostering positive community relationships. Graduating seniors are eligible for scholarship funding. To participate, students must maintain a minimum GPA of 2.0, have good attendance records, and be affiliated with selected Boston schools or organizations. The program has received positive feedback from both students and supervisors, highlighting its effectiveness in providing young people with meaningful healthcare experiences.
requirements: To be considered for the Office of Workforce Development Student Training Program offered by the Dana-Farber Cancer Institute in Boston, MA, applicants must have a 2.0 GPA and good school attendance record, be a Boston resident, and be affiliated with one of the following high schools: Fenway High School, John D. O’Bryant School of Mathematics & Science, Madison Park Technical Vocational High School, Sociedad Latina, or Youth Enrichment Services. Rising sophomores or higher who are interested in clinical, research or health administration careers are eligible to apply. Summer commitment requirements include participation in an all-day orientation, working 30 hours per week for 7 weeks, and taking mandatory weekly college and career readiness workshops and college tours. Graduating seniors are also eligible for scholarship funding. Successful summer program participants may apply for the academic-year program, which requires working 8 to 15 hours per week from October to June, attending the summer program, and participating in twice-monthly college and career readiness workshops and field trips.

title: Teen Advisory Board
text: The Noguchi Museum's Teen Advisory Board (TAB) offers a paid internship opportunity for high school students. Through this program, interns delve into the life and artistry of Isamu Noguchi while collaborating on projects that foster dialogue and inclusivity within the Museum. This year's TAB interns will center their discussions on social justice and the empowerment of communities and cultures, drawing inspiration from the global influences that shaped Noguchi's life and work.
address: 9-01 33rd Road (at Vernon Boulevard), Long Island City, New York 11106
host: The Isamu Noguchi Foundation and Garden Museum
requirements: unknown

title: Summer Science Research Program
text: The RockEDU team is thrilled to introduce an innovative model for the SSRP, drawing upon insights gained from remote mentored research experiences during the pandemic. SSRP scholars will embark on a journey of designing and executing their own research projects within the framework of themed research tracks. This transformative approach empowers students to delve into their research interests, fostering critical thinking, problem-solving, and scientific inquiry skills.
address: 1230 York Ave, New York, NY 10065, United States
requirements:
To be eligible for SSRP participation, students must be enrolled as a junior or senior in high school, and must be at least 16 years old at the start of the program.  All participants must be fully vaccinated against COVID-19, and be willing to wear a mask and practice social distancing as per university and CDC guidelines dictate. We cannot make exceptions.

In order to participate in the SSRP, students must commit to the entirety of the seven-week program — we can not accommodate attendance gaps. Please be aware: students are prohibited from using any aspect of work performed during the SSRP for science competition submissions.

title: Montana Models
text: We firmly believe that everyone possesses ingenuity, creativity, and expert knowledge that they can contribute to solving problems they care about. However, for some, math is often perceived as a subject of rote memorization and rule application without meaningful context. We challenge this notion, asserting that math is inherently creative and beautiful. Furthermore, we believe that the most effective solutions arise from collaborative efforts. Therefore, we extend an invitation to groups of 4-6 youth, accompanied by a mentor (4-H or otherwise), to embark on a transformative camp experience where they can collectively explore the wonders of math.
address: Montana State University in Bozeman, MT.
requirements: Montana Models is for students entering grades 7th to 12th in the fall 2022. Our camp is a little bit different because we invite teams of youth along with an adult mentor. If you are interested, contact your 4-H County Agent, or other potential adult leader then reach out to us!

title: Teen Creative Agency Apprenticeship
text: This one-year, part-time staff position for Teen Creative Agency (TCA) alumni serves as a bridge between youth programs and museum careers. Apprentices develop their professional portfolios by designing programs and facilitating discussions on pressing social issues for staff and audiences of diverse ages and backgrounds. Their responsibilities encompass working across MCA's Learning Programs, curating and producing public events, acting as youth ambassadors and advocates within and outside the museum, and leading workshops and training sessions.
requirements: Must be an alumni of TCA

title: InterseXtions: Gender & Sexuality
text: This paid internship offers New York City LGBTQ+ youth aged 14–19 an opportunity to delve into the intersection of gender, sexuality, and art through an activist perspective. Participants will engage in collaborative efforts to organize programs specifically tailored for other queer and trans youth. The internship fosters a space for youth to explore their identities and contribute to the empowerment of their community through artistic expression and activism.
requirements: This program is open to all NYC teens, ages 14–19, who identify as lesbian, gay, bisexual, trans*, two-spirit, nonbinary, gender nonconforming, questioning, queer, intersex, and/or asexual.

title: NDSU Temp Plant Pathology Summer Intern
text: The NDSU Williston Research Extension Center conducts agricultural research to enhance crop health and the sustainability of the food production system in northwest North Dakota. The plant pathology department prioritizes reducing plant disease through practices like crop rotation, genetic resistance, and fungicide selection in crops such as durum wheat, chickpeas, peas, and lentils. Additionally, research focuses on soil health and beneficial bacteria. The plant pathology research intern will assist with all aspects of the plant pathology research program, including outdoor field research on small crop plots and laboratory-based research.
requirements:
High school student

Over the age of 16

Valid driver’s license or reliable transportation to work

Positive attitude and willingness to work hard

Interest in agriculture, research and outdoor work

Ability to work a full-time schedule in the summer

title: Academy/DPHA Internship
text: This program will guide you through the process of describing the characteristics of a public health-based problem, referencing public health data sources and identifying gaps in information, making community-based inferences using qualitative and quantitative data, collecting, storing, retrieving, and analyzing qualitative and quantitative data, and using public health theory to inform program implementation. You will also learn how to create a programmatic logic model for use in implementation and evaluation, and present qualitative and quantitative data to address public health issues in writing.
address: Suite L10, 4765 Ogletown Stanton Rd. (Route 4), Newark, DE, 19713
requirements: Be a student of an academic institution

requirements: unknown

title: Summer Neuroscience Program
text: The Summer Neuroscience Program (SNP) is a two-week course designed for NYC public high schoolers, led by Rockefeller graduate students. The program delves into ongoing neuroscience research, providing participants with an understanding of brain function and its relevance to daily life. The curriculum aims to introduce students to contemporary neuroscience while fostering their exploration of the field's unsolved mysteries. Through this immersive experience, students gain insights into the complexities of the brain and its role in shaping our thoughts, behaviors, and experiences.
requirements: Applicants must be enrolled in a New York City public school, and must be at least 16 years of age by the start of the program — we cannot make exceptions!

title: Internships
text: The World Affairs Council of San Antonio offers internship opportunities for students passionate about foreign policy. Interns engage in projects and develop expertise in marketing and communications, event planning, and organizational management. Beyond gaining practical experience, interns connect with San Antonio's international leaders, providing valuable insights into global affairs.
host: World Affairs Council of San Antonio
requirements: unknown

title: Mining & Explosives Camp
text: The Mining and Explosives Camp is a comprehensive, week-long program tailored for high school juniors and seniors with a keen interest in the science of explosives. This immersive experience delves into the fundamentals of explosives, encompassing the chemistry behind detonations and the intricate calculations involved in designing blasting patterns. Through hands-on activities, field trips, and workshops, students gain practical knowledge of how engineers harness explosives to extract minerals, reshape landscapes, and even create monumental sculptures like Crazy Horse and his horse head from mountainsides.
address: 501 E St Joseph St, Rapid City, SD 57701
host: The South Dakota School of Mines & Technology
requirements: To be considered for the Mining and Explosives Camp at South Dakota School of Mines and Technology, applicants must be current high school juniors or seniors for the 2022-2023 academic year. Interested individuals must complete an online registration and provide a statement as well as a teacher letter of recommendation. These documents must be submitted by March 30, 2023, to complete the summer camp application. The camp is free to attend, but students are required to sign waivers. In case of cancellation, applicants must notify Brittani Webb at Brittani.Webb@sdsmt.edu or 605-394-6144. The day camp will run from 9 AM to 4:30 PM from June 5-8, 2023, and lunch will be provided. Parents are invited to attend the Thursday 1 PM parent reception.

title: Eight Judicial District High School Internship Program
text: The Eighth Judicial District Summer High School Internship Program is a three-week summer program scheduled to commence on Thursday, July 6th, and conclude on Thursday, July 27th. Interns are expected to work Monday through Thursday from 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM. This summer internship provides students with the opportunity to gain knowledge about various careers within the court system, collaborate directly with judges, judicial chambers staff, and other dedicated professionals in the non-judicial ranks of the Unified Court System, and participate in professional development programs.
address:
New York State Supreme Court
25 Delaware Avenue
Buffalo, New York 14202
requirements: Cover Letter, Resume, Proof of Covid-19 Vaccination, Application

title: New York Bioforce
text: New York Bioforce is a workforce development internship program tailored specifically for New York City high school students. This program offers hands-on laboratory training designed to align with the requirements of biomedical research labs, biotech start-ups, and biopharmaceutical companies. Throughout the program, students will receive 100 hours of research training, encompassing both practical biomedical research techniques such as PCR, gel electrophoresis, and microscopy, as well as essential science communication and networking skills.
requirements:
Must attend a NYC public high school during the academic school year
Must demonstrate economic or educational need based on the following criteria: Student attends a NYC high school with a Free and Reduced Price Lunch (FRPL) rate of 50% or higher OR Student qualifies for FRPL but attends a NYC high school with an FRPL rate below 50%
Please note that preference will be given to current juniors and seniors due to the rigor and demands of the program.

title: State Pre-College Enrichment Program (S-PREP)
text: The State Pre-College Enrichment Program (S-PREP) is a tuition-free preparatory program for high school students in grades 7-12 who aspire to pursue careers in medicine or related STEM fields. Its mission is to bolster the representation of historically underrepresented and economically disadvantaged students in higher education, particularly in mathematics, science, technology, health-related disciplines, and licensed professions. The program aims to enhance their college readiness and increase their participation rates in these fields.
requirements:
Students must be:
Enrolled in Grades 7-12
A New York State Resident or a Permanent Resident residing in the state.
Economically disadvantaged*, or Black/African American, Hispanic/Latino, Alaskan Native or American Indian; and will benefit from academic enrichment.
Maintenance of an 80% grade average particularly in math and science
A strong interest in medicine or STEM
The ability to commit to the program schedule
A mature personality- Conduct him/her/themselves in a manner conducive to their own learning, and to the learning of others.

title: Junior Summer Volunteer Program
text: Boston Medical Center's Junior Summer Volunteer Program (JSVP) provides rising juniors and seniors in high school with an immersive opportunity to explore the patient care experience. Through interactive engagement and consultation with hospital and clinical professionals, students gain valuable knowledge and insight into the healthcare field. The program fosters a deeper understanding of patient care and the complexities of the healthcare system, equipping students with a foundation for future careers in medicine or related fields.
address:
One Boston Medical Center Place
Boston, MA 02118
requirements: Must be in high school and a rising junior or senior.

This commitment allows volunteers to make a significant impact on the lives of those they serve while also gaining valuable experience and personal growth.

Interns will assist with environmental educational programs tailored for kindergarten through high school students. Additionally, they will engage in administrative tasks behind the scenes. Interns may also have the opportunity to work at the Newport Aquarium or afterschool programs, subject to their interests, the season, and availability.

title: Pre-Baccalaureate Program
text: Spend your summer immersed in the vibrant academic community of Barnard College. Join esteemed Barnard faculty and fellow students in engaging classroom experiences, earning college credit through our Pre-Bacc program. This program is designed specifically for high school juniors, seniors, and gap year students, providing an exceptional opportunity to explore college-level coursework and gain a head start on their academic journey.
requirements: unknown

title: Beaver Works Summer Institute
text: The Beaver Works Summer Institute (BWSI) is a project-based internship program that offers courses in engineering, current research topics, and building autonomous systems. The program provides both in-person and virtual courses. In-person courses include Autonomous RACECAR, UAS-SAR, Autonomous Underwater Vehicles, and Build-a-CubeSat. Supported by generous sponsors, the program is free for students to attend. BWSI is committed to providing students with depth and experience in project-based courses. The program offers a valuable opportunity for students to learn and interact with current technology while being mentored by experienced engineers.
requirements: To be considered for the Beaver Works Summer Institute (BWSI), applicants need to submit an application form, have a minimum GPA of 3.5, be a high school student, have completed pre-requisite coursework, and submit at least one letter of recommendation from a teacher. The program is free, but students and families accepted for in-person courses will be responsible for accommodations or commuting to the MIT campus for classes.

title: UW Allen School Changemakers in Computing
text: Changemakers in Computing (CIC), a summer 2023 program hosted by the University of Washington's Allen School, aims to empower Washington State high school students from underrepresented backgrounds. Mentees will join groups led by current UW undergraduate Mentors, engaging in culturally relevant project-based learning to develop coding skills. They will explore diverse areas of computing, recognizing the transformative impact technology can have on society. CIC provides support for students to continue their learning journey and fosters a community of changemakers who share a passion for using technology to make a positive impact.
requirements: Washington State High School Student

title: Mayor's Youth Council
text: The Mayor's Youth Council (MYC) is a program that fosters civic engagement among Boston's high school students. Comprising 86 council members, the MYC operates through eight committees and neighborhood working groups, each led by co-directors and co-liaisons. Representing every neighborhood in Boston, council members are appointed by Mayor Wu after an application and interview process. Serving one-year terms, they collaborate with the Mayor's Office, community leaders, and city officials. The MYC empowers youth voices in city governance, aiming to implement positive solutions through civic engagement, foster connections among youth leaders, and inspire social change and justice initiatives within their communities.
requirements: To be considered for the Mayor's Youth Council, applicants must be high school students from any neighborhood in Boston. They must apply and go through an interview process. All council members are approved by the mayor and must serve a one-year term.

title: SF YouthWorks & MYEEP
text: SF YouthWorks offers paid job readiness workshops, training, and internships at various San Francisco City Departments, including the Public Utilities Commission, the Public Library, and the SF International Airport. These opportunities provide high school students with valuable hands-on experience, preparing them for future employment.
requirements: Must reside or attend school in SF. MYEEP is for 14-18 year olds & SF YouthWorks is for rising Juniors, rising Seniors, and graduating Seniors.

title: New Victory Usher Corps
text: At New Victory, high school juniors and seniors have the opportunity to join the award-winning Usher Corps, a rigorous year-to-year creative youth development program. This program provides flexible paid employment, fostering personal and professional growth. Participants join a supportive team of young adults from across the city and engage in professional training and workshops. They gain hands-on experience working with children and families in a lively, fast-paced environment. Additionally, the program offers opportunities to witness live theater from around the world, enriching the participants' cultural experiences.
requirements:
Be enrolled as a junior in high school or the equivalent in an HSE/GED program.
Be able to work a three-shift minimum each week (between shifts in the theater and workshops), including day, evening, and weekend shifts.
Be able to attend select mandatory weekday after-school workshops.

title: The Gatton Academy
text: The Carol Martin Gatton Academy of Mathematics and Science in Kentucky is a residential program designed for exceptional Kentucky high school students with a passion for science, technology, engineering, and mathematics. Located on the campus of Western Kentucky University, the academy provides students with the opportunity to enroll in college-level courses, participate in faculty-led research projects, and engage in study abroad programs. The Gatton Academy fosters a supportive community where students can develop their creativity, curiosity, and reasoning abilities, leading to independent thinking and action. The program aims to instill integrity in its students, enabling them to make meaningful contributions to society. Ultimately, the academy's mission is to prepare Kentucky's brightest young minds for leadership roles in the Commonwealth by providing them with an advanced educational environment that nurtures their scientific and mathematical talents.
address: 1509 College Heights Blvd, Bowling Green, KY 42101
requirements: Be a current domiciled resident of the state of Kentucky as stated by the Kentucky Council of Postsecondary Education, be a sophomore or have achieved sophomore status (as stated by their sending school) at the time of application (February 1), be a junior (as stated by their sending school) at the time of enrollment to The Gatton Academy (August 1 of the same application year), complete Algebra I, Geometry and Algebra II prior to enrollment, score a minimum 22 math on the ACT or score a minimum 540 math on the SAT, and submit all required materials no later than February 1, 2023

title: Woodland Ecology Research Mentorship (WERM)
text: The Woodland Ecology Research Mentorship (WERM) program at Wave Hill provides New York City high school students with the opportunity to engage in citywide ecological monitoring efforts in local woodlands and conduct genuine research under the guidance of experienced field scientists. This comprehensive 14-month program commences with an immersive academic science learning experience, equipping students with the foundational knowledge necessary for their research endeavors. Through hands-on field work and mentorship, students gain valuable insights into the ecological dynamics of urban woodlands, contributing to the advancement of scientific understanding and fostering a passion for environmental stewardship.
requirements:
Applicant Qualifications:
Currently enrolled in high school with a strong interest in scientific research and the urban environment
16 years old by July 5, 2023 and is a New York City resident eligible to work in the United States
Able to make a 14-month commitment from June 2023 through August 2024, including Saturdays during the school year
Due to several factors, including the challenges of long travel times, preference will be given to WERM applicants who live in the Bronx or Upper Manhattan.

title: High School and College Student Internship Program
text: The East Baton Rouge Parish of East Baton Rouge High School internship program offers high school students the chance to acquire practical work experience in diverse industries. This program allows students to delve into their career aspirations, hone their abilities, and forge valuable connections with professionals in their chosen fields. By participating in this program, students gain hands-on experience, explore their interests, and develop their skills, setting them on a path towards a successful future in their desired career.
host: City of Baton Rouge, Parish of East Baton Rouge
requirements: Must be at least 16 years old, enrolled in a secondary educational institute within the East Baton Rouge Parish.

title: The Summer Youth Employment Program
text: Project Self-Sufficiency's Summer Youth Employment Program provides rising high school sophomores and juniors with comprehensive job preparation. Participants undergo skills assessments, learn resume and cover letter writing, explore workplace etiquette, practice interview techniques, and master job application completion. The program culminates in paid on-the-job experience, equipping youth with practical knowledge and confidence for future employment.
requirements: For rising high school sophomores and juniors; Family income at 250% of the Federal Poverty Level or less; Need transportation (i.e., cannot own a car); Willing to learn & work hard; Must be vaccinated against Covid-19.

title: Urban Design and Planning Pre-College Fellowship
text: The Urban Design and Planning Pre-College Fellowship is an immersive program designed for high school students with an interest in pursuing careers in urban planning and design. Through this pre-college experience, students will gain firsthand exposure to the field, engaging with renowned professionals and peers in the Boston area and beyond. The program aims to provide a comprehensive introduction to urban planning and design, fostering a deeper understanding of the principles and practices that shape our built environment.
requirements: High school student

title: Next Generation Pathways to Computing Program (NEXTGENCOMPUTING)
text: The NextGen Pathways to Computing Program offers high school juniors, seniors, and recent graduates in Anderson, Blount, Knox, Loudon, and Roane counties the opportunity to delve into foundational computer and computational science skills. Mentored by ORNL research and technical staff, participants gain exposure to ORNL's advanced research facilities, including the world's most powerful supercomputer. The program emphasizes solving complex scientific and technical problems in energy and security, aiming to equip participants with essential skills for successful careers in computing fields. Open to students from public, private, or home-schooled institutions in eligible counties, the program provides a weekly stipend of up to $500 and optional professional development activities. To qualify, students must maintain a minimum GPA of 3.0/4.0, secure recommendations from a STEM teacher and principal, and complete pre- and post-appointment surveys.
address: 5200, 1 Bethel Valley Rd, Oak Ridge, TN 37830
requirements: The NextGen Pathway to Computing Program is an ORNL internship program that offers high school juniors and seniors as well as recent graduates from accredited high school or home school programs located in Anderson, Blount, Knox, Loudon, and Roane counties the opportunity to learn foundational computer and computational science skills. Applicants must be at least 16 years old at the time of appointment and have a minimum GPA of 3.0/4.0. Participants are expected to participate 40 hours per week and can miss a maximum of 5 days without stipend. Applicants must be U.S. citizens or legal permanent residents, and rising juniors/seniors or recently graduated seniors who have not yet enrolled in college. The program benefits include a weekly stipend of up to $500, professional development activities and opportunities to learn from ORNL's research and technical staff. Applicants must complete an online application through Zintellect, obtain at least one recommendation from a STEM teacher and a principal or curriculum coordinator, and complete pre- and post-appointment surveys. Finally, participants are required to behave in a responsible and professional manner, avoid activities that interfere with the appointment period, and complete a report at the end of the appointment, as a rubric will be provided.

title: Be Your Own Boss Internship
text: Through the Be Your Own Boss Internship, aspiring entrepreneurs can embark on a four-week journey to develop and pitch their own business ideas while earning compensation. This immersive program provides a comprehensive crash course in entrepreneurship, fostering collaboration among ambitious teens from diverse backgrounds. Participants will engage in hands-on activities, gaining practical experience in building their own businesses from the ground up.
requirements: Only for high school students of Chicago public & charter schools.

title: Environmentor Program
text: Environmentor is a science research mentorship program designed for high school students in grades 9-11 who reside or attend school in the Rockaway Peninsula area. Under the guidance of scientists from local universities and research institutions, students engage in authentic research projects centered around the Rockaway shoreline. The program is conducted entirely in person, providing students with hands-on experience and the opportunity to contribute to scientific knowledge while exploring the unique environmental challenges and opportunities of their local ecosystem.

host: Rockaway Initiative for Sustainability and Equity

Must be in the 10th or 11th grade
Must live or go to school in the Rockaway Peninsula (or adjacent city neighborhoods)
Must be able to commit to the full program timeframe (January - August)

title: Governor's Scholar
text: The Governor's Scholars Program, established in 1983, is a summer residential program for exceptional Kentucky high school seniors. Recognizing the potential of the state's brightest minds, the program aims to foster future civic and economic leaders. Through a partnership between the Governor's Office, the Kentucky State Legislature, and private enterprise, the program provides financial support for selected students to attend without charge. Since its inception with 230 students on a single campus, the program has expanded to accommodate over 1,000 students across three campuses, showcasing its unwavering support and commitment to nurturing Kentucky's next generation of leaders.
address: 600 W Walnut St, Danville, KY 40422 or 150 University Blvd, Morehead, KY 40351 or 1375 Chestnut St, Murray, KY 42071
requirements: Be in the 11th grade at the time of selection and intend to return to a Kentucky school district for the next school term.  (Students skipping their senior year to enter college are not eligible); Be a current resident of Kentucky; Have taken the ACT, PSAT, or SAT in the 9th, 10th or 11th grades.

title: Young Adult Leadership Council
text: ArtsWestchester's Young Adult Leadership Council is a comprehensive career and college readiness program designed for youth aged 16-22. This council empowers youth with a platform to contribute their perspectives to ArtsWestchester's educational initiatives. Council members convene bi-monthly at the ArtsWestchester gallery in downtown White Plains, where they actively engage in planning, evaluating, promoting, and developing teen programs. These programs include the ongoing Teen Tuesday & Thursday program, providing youth with opportunities to participate in arts-based activities and workshops.

Reliable
Flexible

title: Internships

These internships offer hands-on involvement in various fields, including finance, event planning, sponsorships, marketing, communications, videography, and youth programs. Through these opportunities, students gain valuable work experience while gaining insights into the operations of a nonprofit dedicated to promoting sports and youth development.

title: Teen Conservation Leaders

Through this program, participants develop essential job and life skills, enhance their self-confidence, and contribute to their community by earning service hours. The program commences with an intensive week-long training session, where both new and returning TCL students engage in team-building activities, delve into the fundamentals of marine biology, and explore critical ocean conservation issues.

Carter Journalism Institute at New York University to engage in a rigorous and enriching experience that will equip them with the skills and knowledge necessary to excel in the field of journalism.

title: Center for Imaging Science Summer High School Intern Program

The program encompasses professional development activities, team-building exercises, and at least one field trip, all provided free of charge.

title: Aspirnaut Summer Research Internship at U-M
text: The Aspirnaut Summer Research Internship Program at U-M is a six-week program designed to foster interest in basic science research among high school students from underprivileged backgrounds. Selected students from rural and socioeconomically disadvantaged areas in Michigan will engage in hands-on research projects under the guidance of U-M researchers. Interns will conduct their own research, present their findings, and receive housing, meals, and a stipend. The program also provides professional development opportunities, access to university resources, and a supportive environment with supervision from research supervisors, undergraduate resident advisors, and program staff. The Aspirnaut program adheres to a Code of Conduct and aims to inspire participants to pursue college and career paths in the sciences.
requirements: High school students must be present and on campus for the duration of the program, have health insurance coverage for the duration of the program, and be responsible for transportation to and from the program. They must also have an interest in basic science research, and be willing to become immersed in a hands-on science laboratory experience. The program welcomes students from rural and socioeconomically disadvantaged communities. The interns should be committed to conduct their own research project, gather results that contribute to cutting-edge research, and present their findings to peers and mentors at the end of the experience.

title: Online Courses for High School Students
text: Through Cornell's online learning platform, students can enroll in regular Cornell courses, engage with university faculty in virtual classrooms, and earn academic credits that will be reflected on an official Cornell transcript. This immersive online experience provides access to the same rigorous coursework and esteemed instructors as on-campus students, allowing learners to advance their knowledge and skills from the convenience of their own location.

title: Santa Clarita Valley Historical Society Docent
text: Docents, trained volunteers at the Santa Clarita History Center, welcome visitors, sharing their expertise on the Santa Clarita Valley's history and folklore through guided tours of the museum and restoration projects. They also present to groups of students, Scouts, and community organizations, fostering a deeper understanding of the region's past.

title: Summer Youth Internship Program
text: The Museum of Science in Boston offers internships during three trimesters: fall, winter/spring, and summer. These internships provide hands-on experience in areas such as science education and behind-the-scenes operations. Applicants must be enrolled in high school, college, or graduate school, or be making a career change, and must be eligible to work in the United States. Internships may be paid or unpaid, and can be completed for course credit if approved by the educational institution. Additionally, the Museum offers a summer youth internship program for students aged 14-19, which includes paid working hours, professional development workshops, and free admission to the Museum's exhibits and venues. The Museum of Science is committed to equal opportunity and provides a work environment free from discrimination and harassment.
requirements: Applicants interested in the Museum of Science's internship program must meet certain requirements. The program is open to high school students aged 14-19, college students (freshmen, sophomores, juniors, and seniors), graduate students, recent graduates, and career changers. The Museum offers paid and unpaid positions, depending on the internship. All applicants must be fully vaccinated against COVID-19, and exemptions will be granted for qualifying medical disabilities or sincerely held religious objections. Students who wish to receive course credit must obtain permission from their educational institution. The Museum does not provide housing or relocation assistance, and interns are responsible for their own costs. Finally, intern benefits include free parking, free admission to the Museum's exhibits and shows, and discounts on Museum store and café purchases.

title: Oschner STAR Summer Scholars Program
text: The Ochsner STAR Program provides a cost-free opportunity for high school students to delve into the healthcare field, particularly those facing limited access and resources. This program aims to expose students to the diverse aspects of healthcare, fostering their interest and equipping them with valuable knowledge and skills.
requirements:
Must be at least 16 by the start of the program. 
Must be residents of and attend high school in Louisiana
Open to students advancing into the 12th grade [graduating seniors are no eligible]

title: Women Empowered Through Business (WEB) Institute
text: The Women Empowered Through Business (WEB) Institute is a week-long summer internship program designed to introduce high school female rising juniors to the technology and business fields. Over six days, students participate in workshops led by university faculty and staff, covering coding, computer technology, entrepreneurship, personal branding, supply chain management, business analytics, and professional development. These workshops showcase women leaders in technology and business. The program also includes team-building sessions and college readiness workshops to support students' future academic paths. Additionally, participants engage with industry leaders through sessions that provide insights into the business world.
requirements: To be considered for the WEB Institute internship program, applicants must be female rising juniors in high school who are interested in pursuing a career in technology and business. They must be from under-represented communities, including low-income households and/or communities of color. Applicants must demonstrate academic excellence, leadership potential, and a strong interest in technology and business. The selection process will be highly competitive, and the top candidates will be selected based on their application, essays, and recommendations. In addition, applicants must be able to attend the six-day program sessions in person and be committed to fully participate in all aspects of the program.

title: PopHealthExperience
text: The PopHealthExperience immerses rising 8th-12th graders in the multifaceted field of public health. Guided by Boston University School of Public Health faculty and graduate students, participants delve into core concepts and explore specialized areas such as Biostatistics, Environmental Health, Epidemiology, and Public Health Advocacy and Policy. Hands-on research activities and case studies foster critical thinking and problem-solving skills. Students analyze public policy examples and visit the Massachusetts State House to understand the impact of policy on health. Throughout the program, mentorship supports students in identifying community health challenges and developing digital media advocacy pieces to raise awareness and propose solutions.
host: Boston University School of Public Health
requirements: The PopHealthExperience summer enrichment program was designed for rising 8th to 12th graders (ages 12-17).

title: Pathways Internship Program
text: The U.S. Department of State's Pathways Internship Program encompasses the Internship Experience Program (IEP) and the Internship Temporary Program (ITEP). These programs cater to U.S. citizens pursuing education at various levels, from high school to graduate school and professional academic programs. Both IEP and ITEP offer students the chance to gain insights into Federal careers while receiving compensation for their contributions.
requirements:
U.S. Citizenship
Must be at least 16 years of age by the closing date of the announcement
You will be subject to random drug testing
Be able to receive with a Secret or Top Secret security clearance
Must maintain student eligibility for duration of internship*
Cumulative GPA of 2.0 at time of application and throughout internship appointment

title: The Norman Mineta Bay Area Summer Academy
text: MTC, the metropolitan planning organization for the Bay Area, provides high school students with an exceptional opportunity to delve into the intricacies of government service. Through this program, students gain firsthand insights into the inner workings of urban planning, transportation, and environmental sustainability. By participating in this immersive experience, they embark on a career path in public service, fostering their understanding of the critical role government plays in shaping the future of our communities.
address: Bay Area Metro Center, 375 Beale Street, Suite 800, San Francisco, CA 94105-2066
requirements:
Live in the Bay Area and attend a local high school
Must be at least 16 years old and have completed the ninth grade by the beginning of the Academy
Be able to attend online seminars and present on a topic related to the seminars
If the student is under 18, have the permission of a parent or guardian to participate

title: Einstein Montefiore Summer High School Research Program
text: The Einstein-Montefiore Summer High School Research Program provides an immersive experience for high school students aged 16 and above, fostering their interest in scientific research. Through this program, students gain firsthand exposure to cutting-edge scientific advancements, inspiring them to consider a career in science while still in high school. The program aims to ignite a passion for scientific inquiry and equip students with the skills and knowledge necessary to pursue future endeavors in the field.
requirements: All participants must be U.S. citizens currently attending high school in the United States. We strongly encourage minority students from underserved populations to apply.

title: Young Leaders Academy
text: Kentucky high school students who have completed at least one year of high school are eligible to apply for the Young Leaders Academy, a summer residential leadership conference held at the University of Louisville. This annual program, offered by the McConnell Center, is designed for outstanding students to enhance their leadership abilities and deepen their understanding of American history. The conference's theme, "Revisiting American Constitutionalism," will provide participants with a comprehensive exploration of the principles and foundations of the U.S. Constitution.
address: Ekstrom Library Second Floor, West Wing University of Louisville Louisville, Kentucky 40292
requirements: unknown

title: Media Makers
text: Through the Media Makers internship, interns delve into the realm of media production, honing their skills in various areas while simultaneously addressing pressing social issues within their communities. The program equips interns with a comprehensive skillset encompassing digital illustration, graphic design, animation, public artwork creation, and social media strategy. Interns gain proficiency in utilizing drawing tablets and Adobe Photoshop, navigate diverse graphic design platforms, create engaging animations, design community-centric artwork, and leverage social media for advocacy purposes.
requirements: unknown

title: TECH360 Summer Bootcamp Program
text: The TECH360 Summer Bootcamp is an intensive, three-week program designed to equip students with the foundational skills of web design and development. Participants will delve into industry-aligned technical and professional practices, gaining proficiency in essential coding languages and frameworks such as HTML, CSS, and Bootstrap. Through hands-on projects and expert guidance, students will acquire a comprehensive understanding of web development principles, enabling them to build and maintain dynamic and user-friendly websites.
requirements:
Rising high school juniors and seniors between the ages of 15-19 currently attending a New York City (all boroughs), Los Angeles County, or Miami / Broward high school are eligible to apply.  Graduating high school seniors (Class of '22) would not be eligible to participate in the program.
AOT prioritizes candidates who:
Self-identify as Hispanic / Latinx
Self-identify as African American / Black ​
Self-identify as females and/or girls and/or non-binary
Self-identify as LGBTQIA+
Attend a NYC, LA, or Miami / Broward high school that meets our Economic Needs Index

title: iCLEM Student Intern
text: The High School Leadership Academy is a six-week summer program designed to develop leadership skills in high school students. The program is open to students entering grades 9-12 and will be held at the University of California, Berkeley. Students will participate in workshops, discussions, and activities designed to enhance their communication, problem-solving, and decision-making abilities. They will also have the opportunity to interact with successful leaders from various fields and learn about different leadership styles. The program culminates in a final project where students will apply their newfound skills to a real-world problem.
requirements: unknown

title: Lancaster Museum of Art and History Volunteer
text: The Lancaster Museum of Art and History (MOAH, MOAH:CEDAR, and WHM) is currently accepting volunteer applications. Volunteers are passionate about art and history and make valuable contributions to the museum at all levels. As a volunteer, you will be an integral part of the museum, working directly with staff and gaining real-world experience.
host: Lancaster Museum of Art and History
requirements: Volunteers will be subject to fingerprinting and will undergo a criminal background check. Volunteers must also submit a PPD Skin Test (TB) clearance before starting a volunteer assignment.

title: Clinical Internship Program
text: The Clinical Internship at Vermont Sports Medicine Center offers qualified high school juniors or seniors hands-on experience in the medical fields of Physical Therapy and Occupational Therapy. Under the guidance of the Clinical Manager or Practice Director, interns will observe and participate in daily operations, gaining exposure to the profession. The internship schedule can be tailored to accommodate student school schedules, with hours ranging from 6 to 20 per week.
requirements: High School Junior or Senior with GPA of 3.0.

title: Odysea Aquarium  Internship Program
text: The OdySea Aquarium offers an unpaid internship program in various departments, providing hands-on learning experiences. These internships align with the semester calendar and require a 3-4 month commitment, with a minimum of 3-5 days per week. Interns have the opportunity to gain valuable knowledge and skills in different areas of aquarium operations, including animal care, conservation, education, and guest services.
requirements: unknown

title: Environmental Internship for High School Students
text: The internship program focuses on training interns in naturalist skills and hands-on techniques for environmental assessment, conservation, and stewardship. Aligned with the Land Trust of North Alabama's mission to preserve ecological resources through education, advocacy, and recreation, the internship aims to cultivate responsible land stewards. Practical training is provided in soil analysis, water quality monitoring, and plant identification, with an emphasis on outdoor education. Theoretical components are kept to a minimum, with the majority of instruction taking place in field settings.
requirements: unknown

title: Volunteer Services
text: This activity is open to high school students who are interested in exploring the field of engineering. Participants will have the opportunity to engage in hands-on projects, interact with industry professionals, and gain insights into the various disciplines within engineering. The program includes workshops, field trips, and mentorship opportunities, providing students with a comprehensive understanding of the field and its career pathways. Specific details and registration information can be found on the website.
requirements: unknown

title: Pre-College Research Internship for Students from Minority Backgrounds [PRISM]
text: The UAB PRISM program provides high school students from minority backgrounds with invaluable hands-on research experiences under the guidance of experienced surgeon mentors. This internship not only exposes students to the diverse opportunities within medical careers but also emphasizes the profound impact of research on patient care. By engaging in this program, students gain a competitive edge in their college applications while simultaneously fostering their interest in science and medicine.
host: The University of Alabama at Birmingham
requirements: Be a high school junior

title: Discovery Program
text: Northwestern Medicine's NM Discovery Program aims to foster the next generation of healthcare leaders by providing STEM career exploration opportunities to students who may not otherwise have access to them. The program exposes students to various healthcare careers through tours, guest speakers, group discussions, and hands-on projects. It also emphasizes character and professional development, life skills, community service, leadership experience, and mentorship and networking opportunities. Meetings are typically held on Saturday mornings from 9:00 am to 12:00 pm during the school year. The Central region offers a two-year program, while all other regions offer a one-year program for applicants entering the 2022-2023 school year.

Students with a GPA below 3.0 can explain any unique circumstances on their application and may still be considered.Commit to the program, including attendance at all Discovery Program meetings and community service activities. No more than two excused absences are permitted.Commit to abide by all Discovery Program guidelines and policies, including providing proof of COVID-19 vaccination.Submit the completed application to the appropriate chapter.

title: VALOR
text: As an extension of its VetTech internship program, the U.S. Department of Energy's Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory has launched the VALOR (Veteran Applied Laboratory Occupational Retraining) program to further support U.S. military veterans. This workforce development initiative aims to provide Junior Reserve Officer Training Corps (JROTC) high school cadets and veterans transitioning to civilian careers with practical training experiences. The program seeks to facilitate full-time technical career placement and security at Fermilab, offering veterans and cadets valuable opportunities to apply their skills and contribute to the laboratory's mission.
requirements: The VALOR Apprenticeship is a highly competitive, paid, six-month fall/spring training and career exploration program for military veterans at the beginning of their civilian careers and recent Illinois JROTC high school graduates. During the program, participants build and enhance their technical, computing, or business proficiencies. Assuming apprentice-level expertise, general military experience and/or knowledge based on academic study, the opportunity offers a wide range of placement options. The apprenticeship may allow the participant to fabricate, assemble, calibrate, operate, test, repair or modify electronic or mechanical equipment, systems, devices, or databases. Exposures may also include experiences with information technology, procurement, or environmental, safety and health.

title: Youth Conservation Corp Crew Member Application
text: Past summer work projects have encompassed a wide range of tasks, including the development of nature trails, the planting and maintenance of native flora, the restoration of stream banks, and basic outdoor maintenance. Additionally, workers have engaged in the construction of trail bridges, soil retaining walls, and canoe launches. Beyond these practical tasks, the program also imparts essential work and life skills, environmental construction techniques, and a heightened environmental awareness.

Through hands-on experiences, they immerse themselves in American history, deepening their understanding of its complexities and significance.

title: Summer Youth Internship - Charleston County
text: The Summer Youth Internship Program (SYIP) offered by Charleston County Government provides an opportunity for young adults aged 16-21 and residing in Charleston County to gain hands-on experience in county government operations. Participants develop workplace readiness skills and gain exposure to the work environment while earning $15 per hour. Eligible candidates must be high school or college students, possess a functional email account and voicemail for communication, and complete the online application. Job opportunities are available with Charleston County government, the Public Library, the Charleston Animal Society, and the Public Works Department. The program runs from June 16th to July 27th, with training commencing on June 16th. Graduates receive soft skills training throughout the program and work an average of 4-hour shifts per day, totaling 120 hours. The application deadline is May 5th or upon reaching 125 applicants, whichever occurs first.
address: 4045 Bridge View Drive, Suite 207 in North Charleston
requirements: To be considered for the Summer Youth Internship Program (SYIP), applicants must meet the following requirements: must be between the ages of 16-21 at the start of the program, currently enrolled in high school or college, and a resident of Charleston County. Additionally, applicants must have an active email and voicemail account and respond promptly to communication, complete an online application to the program by May 5th, and must be available to work from June 16th until July 27th, with an average of 4-hour shifts per day. Applicants also need to attend training on June 16th and graduation on July 27th. The program will offer job opportunities at Charleston County Government, the Public Library, Charleston Animal Society, and the Public Works Department. Please note that applying for the jobs does not guarantee selection as the program typically has more applicants than jobs.

title: Women in Engineering Summer Program (WIESP)
text: The Women in Engineering Summer Program (WIESP), generously supported by Knowles Corporation, Motorola Solutions, and the National Science Foundation, is a complimentary, three-week, non-residential program designed to provide high school students with an exceptional opportunity to delve into the realm of engineering through engaging hands-on projects and visits to corporate partners. Participants will benefit from the guidance of renowned professors, interact with current College of Engineering students, forge new friendships, and upon successful completion of the program, receive a stipend.
requirements: Must be in 11th or 12th grade by Fall 2023. Overall grade point average of 3.2 or higher. Grades of As and Bs in math and science classes. Be an active member of a STEM related club or organization

title: Research Mentorship Program (RMP)
text: The Research Mentorship Program, offered by the University of California, Santa Barbara, is a competitive summer program designed for exceptional high school students worldwide. From June 20 to August 4, 2023, participants engage in hands-on, interdisciplinary university-level research. Students are paired with mentors from various disciplines and select research projects from a diverse range offered annually. Through this program, students foster close relationships with their mentors, gain insights into professional research opportunities, develop research techniques, and refine their academic aspirations. The GRIT talks lecture series provides access to renowned researchers from the UC Santa Barbara community, showcasing groundbreaking research and innovative technology. Additionally, students experience university life and connect with peers who share their curiosity and ambition.
host: The University of California Santa Barbara
requirements: The Research Mentorship Program offered by the University of California, Santa Barbara is a highly competitive summer program that engages qualified and high-achieving high school students from all over the world in interdisciplinary, hands-on, university-level research. Students participating in the program are required to attend the program in its entirety, including the virtual component from June 20 – 23, 2023. The program is open to high school students who have completed their sophomore, junior or senior years at the time of application. Participants are paired up with a mentor (graduate student, postdoc, or faculty) and choose a research project from a large list of disciplines offered by the program each year. Along with academic benefits, students will also have the opportunity to be immersed in university life and network with equally ambitious and curious peers. Pre-college students are required to be vaccinated for COVID-19 as they will be participating in in-person courses or programs at UC Santa Barbara during Summer Sessions.

title: BioBus Junior Scientist Internship
text: BioBus fosters immersive scientific experiences through mobile and community laboratories. Students collaborate with scientists in hands-on exploration during in-school, after-school, weekend, and summer programs, as well as internships. This initiative empowers K-12 and college students in New York City to engage with science, fostering their curiosity, exploration, and pursuit of scientific endeavors.
requirements:
Available for the full duration of the 12–month internship
Currently enrolled in 9th, 10th, or 11th grade in New York City high school
Have a genuine interest in scientific discovery, performing science research and have an interest in working with the public to cultivate their scientific curiosity
Leadership and teaching experience are a plus

title: Summer Program
text: BESt summer programs are four-week immersive experiences designed to ignite students' passion for STEM-based professions. With a focus on STEM-based curriculum, these programs aim to cultivate a diverse pipeline of healthcare providers for the St. Louis Region. By fostering students' interests in STEM fields, BESt programs strive to address the need for a skilled and diverse workforce in the healthcare industry.
requirements:
Full-time, under-represented minority(1) freshman (BESt I), sophomore (BESt II), or junior (BESt III) student currently enrolled in a St. Louis regional high school (St. Louis City, St. Louis and St. Charles, MO counties, and Madison, St. Claire, IL counties). Cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher based on a 4.0 scale. High-potential students, participating in at least one extra-curricular activity or organization.
BESt IV applicant must be: successful high school graduate, under-represented minority(1), accepted and fully committed to attending a university or college as an incoming freshman.

title: Emma Bowen Foundation Internship
text: The EBF Internship program provides aspiring professionals in media and tech with an immersive experience to launch their careers. Whether your aspirations lie in production, journalism, web development, engineering, business management, public relations, sales, or any other related field, this program offers a gateway to success. Selected candidates will have the privilege of working closely with esteemed organizations, gaining invaluable knowledge, developing their skills, and accelerating their path towards a fulfilling career in the industry.

Are interested in pursuing a career in media and tech

Speak and write English fluently

title: Health Careers Summer Internship Program
text: Since its inception in 2004, Hawaii Pacific Health's Health Careers Summer Internship program has provided over 900 high school juniors, seniors, and college students with the opportunity to gain valuable experience in the healthcare industry. This paid, six-week program offers interns the chance to interact with experienced healthcare professionals, explore various healthcare professions, and gain insights into hospital systems. Internships are available at Hawaii Pacific Health and its network of medical centers in Hawaii, including Kapiolani Medical Center for Women & Children, Pali Momi Medical Center, Straub Medical Center, Wilcox Medical Center, and Kauai Medical Clinic.
requirements: At least high school juniors or seniors

title: Youth Summer Program
text: Our students engage in a paid 7-week, 30 hour-per-week job experience at the Brigham and Women's Hospital (BWH) campus. This program emphasizes professional development, healthcare career exploration, community health, and health equity. Students are placed in various departments, including radiology, transport, materials management, and research labs, gaining hands-on experience in the healthcare field.
requirements: Enrolled in High School, 16 years old by June 1, 2023, A resident of the City of Boston, MA, COVID vaccination required

title: Teen Volunteer Program
text: The Boston Public Library Teen Volunteer Program offers high school students (grades 9-12) the opportunity to develop essential job skills that will benefit them in future paid employment. Through volunteer roles within the library, teens gain hands-on experience in customer service, interpersonal communication, and working with diverse individuals. The program also includes a resume building program and an interview skills workshop, equipping teens with the necessary tools to prepare for the job market. By participating in this program, teens not only contribute to the library but also enhance their employability and gain valuable skills that will serve them well in their future careers.
requirements: Must be in grades 9-12.

title: RCPD Internships
text: The RCPD Internship Program offers unpaid opportunities for post-secondary students seeking careers in law enforcement. To qualify, students must be eligible for college credit, submit an application, sign a ride-along waiver, pass a criminal history background check, and adhere to the department's dress code. Interns collaborate with Field Supervisors to establish goals and expectations, and are required to complete a project. Priority is given to students actively pursuing careers in law enforcement or police work. Interested candidates should review department guidelines, download and complete the internship application, and submit it with a cover letter expressing their desire to intern with the Rapid City Police Department.
requirements: To apply for an internship with the Rapid City Police Department, post-secondary school students must be eligible to receive college credit for completing the internship. They are required to submit an application, sign a ride-along waiver, pass a criminal history background check, and comply with the Department dress code. The student intern, University Internship Coordinator, and Police Department will work together to determine goals and expectations. Interns will be assigned a project, and they must successfully complete it. Due to limited resources, priority is given to students pursuing a career in law enforcement or police work. Students interested in interning within the RCPD's Evidence Section/Forensic Labs, follow the detailed application procedure outlined on the department's website.

title: Laboratory Learning Program
text: The Laboratory Learning Program offers high school students a comprehensive, tuition-free research experience in science or engineering. title: Next Gen High School Internship Program
text: In response to the underrepresentation of underrepresented minorities (URM) in STEM fields, Emory University is launching a paid summer internship program for high school students in the Atlanta metropolitan area commencing in 2022.
