Must have an overall 80+ average
Must have an overall 80+ English average, 80+ Math average AND 80+ Science average
Although the STEM Research Academy is primarily designed for high school juniors, 10th graders who meet the above criteria will be considered

title: Coastal Classroom
text: City Parks Foundation offers a fellowship program for ambitious 11th or 12th grade high school students to gain practical experience in environmental education. Interns will contribute to the stewardship of waterways and coastal areas while developing their knowledge of the field. Through hands-on work, they will apply their skills, expand their understanding of environmental issues, and gain valuable work experience that will prepare them for future endeavors in the environmental sector.
requirements:
To be selected, you must be enrolled in High School and:
- Be at least 16 years old or older (and will be 16 by July 1, 2023)
- Demonstrate knowledge of coastal ecology
- Have an interest in working with upper elementary and middle school-aged kids
- Be able to commit to attending the summer training and internship work schedule

title: Junior Science and Humanities Symposium
text: The Junior Science and Humanities Symposium (JSHS) program invites high school students from Northern and Southern New England with a passion for STEM (science, technology, engineering, and mathematics) to showcase their original research through oral or poster presentations. Participants engage in networking with peers, explore research laboratories at the University of New Hampshire, and interact with STEM professionals. The program fosters intellectual growth, recognizes student achievements, and awards scholarships to those who excel in presenting their research before judges and an audience. JSHS offers opportunities for career exploration, peer collaboration, and networking, with the potential for significant scholarships and recognition. Additionally, students may qualify for advancement to the national symposium. The program is free to apply and participate, with an application deadline of February 15, 2023.
host: Junior Science and Humanities Symposium (JSHS) Northern and Southern New England Regions
requirements: To be considered for the Junior Science and Humanities Symposium (JSHS) Northern and Southern New England Regions internship program, applicants must be high school students in grades 9-12 who are conducting research in STEM disciplines, including biology, chemistry, computer and electrical engineering, environmental sciences, mathematics, medical sciences, molecular biology, physics, and plant sciences. Applicants must present the results of their original research efforts in either an oral or poster session before a panel of judges and an audience of their peers. There is no registration fee to apply or participate, and the application deadline for the program is February 15, 2023. By participating in the regional and national symposia, students have the opportunity to honor their individual achievements in STEM, network with peers who share similar interests, develop skills for undergraduate and graduate pursuits in STEM fields, and qualify for significant scholarships and other recognition.

title: Veterinary Sciences Placement
text: This internship-based program immerses students in veterinary sciences within a biomedical research setting, fostering their understanding of basic science principles and language arts proficiency. Participants engage in daily hands-on experiences at their placement, exploring career opportunities in veterinary medicine while enhancing their knowledge and skills. The program aims to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the field, equipping them with the necessary foundation for future endeavors in veterinary sciences.
address: 1 Gustave L. Levy Pl, New York, NY 10029
host: The Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai
requirements:
Demonstrated interest in science and veterinary medicine
Prior experience in a health or medical facility is preferred
Must be a rising high school senior, with a minimum GPA of 85
Must be an under-represented minority and/or economically disadvantaged

title: Discovery Squad
text: Teens aged 14-17 are eligible to join the Discovery Squad at the Children's Museum Houston as volunteers. Members of the Discovery Squad provide assistance with exhibits, activities, and programming during both the summer and the academic year.
requirements: unknown

title: Youth Employment Services (YES) Program
text: The Youth Employment Services (YES) Program is a first-time employment job training program designed for low-income or high-risk teenagers between the ages of 16 and 18 (or 15 to 19 during the summer months) who reside in Santa Clarita. Through partnerships with local businesses and agencies, the City of Santa Clarita provides job training opportunities for these teens, enabling them to gain valuable work experience and develop essential skills for future employment.
address:
23920 Valencia Blvd Ste. 130

Santa Clarita, California, 91355
requirements:
Must be 16 to 18 years old and still in high school  (15 to 19 summer only).
Must have no previous work experience.
Low Income - receive a modified lunch program at school.
High-Risk - low grades; on probation; recovering from addiction; in the DCFS or foster care system; behavioral issues; or have trouble finding a job.
Students must have a minimum of 2.0 GPA in order to be issued a work permit by the school.
Must reside in Santa Clarita.

title: Berkeley Lab K-12 - Experiences in Research
text: The Experiences in Research (EinR) internship program provides paid, six-week summer internships for high school students in Northern California who seek to enhance their STEM skills and gain practical experience. Interns collaborate with Berkeley Lab professionals on cutting-edge projects encompassing diverse STEM fields, including administration, data science, and experimental research. Students can indicate their interests and project preferences during the application process to align their internships with their desired areas of expertise. The program is accessible to current 10th, 11th, and 12th graders with experience in independent work. Interns commit approximately 20 hours per week and receive a stipend. Applications typically open in early February and close in early April.
requirements: To be considered for the Experiences in Research (EinR) internship program, applicants should be current 10th, 11th, or 12th-grade students enrolled in a Northern California educational institution. The program accepts students with independent work experience who are interested in gaining hands-on experience with professionals at Berkeley Lab in various STEM fields, including administration, coding-dependent work, data science, experimental research, and more. Applicants are required to complete the six-week program from June 20 - July 28, 2023, and work for about 20 hours a week. The program is paid, and former EinR interns are ineligible to apply. Applications open in early February 2023 and close on April 3, 2023, and must be submitted through the Application Page.

title: SAGE Summer Camp Director's Apprenticeship Program
text: The Science Accelerating Girls' Engagement in STEM (SAGE) Summer Camp is a one-week program designed to inspire Northern California high school students to delve into the diverse opportunities within STEM fields. Hosted by National Laboratory scientists and engineers, the program seeks to engage intelligent, creative, and passionate young women and other marginalized genders in the STEM community. Through job shadowing, hands-on projects, and professional development, students gain insights into the STEM community, explore and balance their interests, and connect with women in STEM at various career stages. Sponsored by DOE National Labs, the program aims to foster innovation, expand the STEM community, and empower underrepresented students in STEM.
requirements: To be considered for the SAGE Summer Camp program, applicants must be high school students aged between 14 and 17 years, who are interested in pursuing careers in STEM fields. The program is designed to engage curious and passionate female and other marginalized gender students who are underrepresented in STEM fields. Applicants should have a passion for discovery, innovation, and a strong desire to become part of the STEM community. The program aims to demonstrate that there are diverse opportunities available to those pursuing STEM careers, and that STEM fields allow individuals to balance multiple interests. Applications for the camp are open from October 15, 2022, and the deadline for submission is March 15, 2023, at 11:59 pm PST.

title: Internship Program
text: Internships with the World Affairs Council provide valuable hands-on experience in a fast-paced work environment. Available during Spring, Fall, and Summer, these internships typically span three months. The Fellowship position, on the other hand, offers a longer duration of 9-12 months. It is important to note that all CTWAC internships and fellowships are unpaid positions.
address:
World Affairs Council of Connecticut 1049 Asylum Ave
Hartford, CT 06105
requirements: unknown

title: GGG Teen Entrepreneur
text: Get Girls Going (GGG) empowers Black teen girls to create social enterprises that address pressing global issues. Through a six-week summer incubator program, GGG equips these young women with the skills and knowledge necessary to become leaders who challenge the racial and gender inequities that hinder their success. The program focuses on entrepreneurship, innovation, and changemaking, empowering participants to develop solutions that tackle real-world problems while fostering their leadership abilities and equipping them to advocate for a more just and equitable society.
requirements: Must be an upcoming sophomore, junior, or senior in high school

title: Stanford Institutes of Medicine Summer Research Program
text: The Stanford Institutes of Medicine Summer Research Program (SIMR) is an eight-week program designed to foster interest in biological sciences and medicine among high school students from diverse backgrounds. Through hands-on research experiences with Stanford faculty, postdoctoral fellows, students, and researchers, participants engage in medically-oriented projects. The program aims to provide insights into the methodologies of scientific research, cultivate a passion for the field, and promote diversity within the scientific community.
requirements:
1) Students must currently be juniors or seniors at the time of application (as of the fall of 2022).  Must be in the graduating class of 2023 or 2024.

2) Students must also be 16 years old or older by the start of the program.

3)  Students must be living in the U.S. AND must be U.S. citizens or permanent residents with a green card in order to apply.

title: Kendall Smith Healthcare Exploration Scholarship
text: Kendall Smith Healthcare Exploration Scholarships are awarded annually to high school juniors and seniors aspiring to pursue careers in healthcare. Recipients of these scholarships embark on a six-week summer immersion program within a hospital environment, where they delve into a specific area of healthcare of their choosing. Throughout the program, students receive a stipend and gain hands-on experience in their chosen field. As a culminating project, they prepare and present a comprehensive presentation showcasing their hospital experience to staff and guests, providing valuable insights into their healthcare journey.
address: 3075 Highland Parkway, Suite 600, Downers Grove, Illinois 60515
requirements: Potential candidates are accepted from among residents of the following towns: Arlington Heights, Buffalo Grove, Des Plaines, Elk Grove Village, Harwood Heights, Morton Grove, Mount Prospect, Niles, Norridge, Palatine, Park Ridge, Prospect Heights, Rolling Meadows, Skokie and Wheeling.

title: Teen Intern (Library)
text: The Santa Barbara Public Library offers paid internship opportunities for teens at the Central and Eastside Libraries. Interns will collaborate with Library Staff and enhance their social-emotional and career development skills. They can select between two tracks: Library Services, which introduces them to various library roles such as IT, administration, collection management, marketing, early literacy, and youth STEAM programming; and Maker Entrepreneurship, which provides training in financial literacy, target market identification, business opportunity recognition, and brand identity. Interns will shadow Library staff and contribute to projects in different library departments, gaining hands-on experience and developing valuable skills.
address: 735 Anacapa Street, P.O. Box 1990, Santa Barbara, California, 93102-1990
requirements: Be 16 years of age with ability to secure a work permit and enrolled in high school.

title: Engineering High School Intern
text: If you possess an unwavering determination to conquer challenges that others deem insurmountable, we invite you to explore a career with Lockheed Martin. We seek individuals who thrive on developing new skills and embracing a diverse range of responsibilities, including analysis, problem solving, and critical thinking. Our employment opportunity offers mentorship from industry-leading engineers who will guide your growth in computer, electrical, or mechanical systems, software development, integration, and testing. Join us and embark on a journey where your ingenuity will be challenged and your skills will soar to new heights.
requirements:
Positive attitude and a willingness to learn a variety of new skills & tools
Good communication skills
Excels in both team & individual work
Good working knowledge of Windows and Microsoft Office (Word, PowerPoint, Excel)
Some programming using languages such as Python, C, C++, or Java (for some positions)
Participation in STEM extra-curricular activities such as Science Olympiad, FIRST Robotics, Career Days, field trips, or summer camps
Intentional participation in STEM elective courses in Junior/Senior high school

title: YouthBridge-NY Fellowship
text: At the core of YouthBridge-NY lies its two-year Fellowship program, designed for high school juniors and seniors from diverse backgrounds. This intensive program provides participants with comprehensive training in leadership and diversity, empowering them to become effective change agents in their communities. Through a rigorous curriculum, Fellows engage in workshops, seminars, and mentorship opportunities that foster their understanding of social justice, equity, and inclusion. The program aims to cultivate a new generation of leaders who are equipped with the skills and knowledge to address the challenges facing their communities and promote positive social change.
requirements:
Must currently be a high school sophomore
Must be able to travel to NYC for every meeting (weekday evenings)
Must be willing to learn about new perspectives and share yours

title: High School Learn and Earn Program
text: The High School Learn and Earn Program is a four-week paid program for high school students, running from July to August. The program aims to employ eight to twelve students from MDC member town school systems. The program's focus is on providing students with hands-on experience and knowledge about careers in water and wastewater management.
requirements:
Must be at least 16 years of age or older
Must be enrolled as a student at an accredited high school within an MDC member town
Must be referred by a guidance counselor (applications submitted without a referral from a guidance counselor will not be accepted)
*Preference will be given to Juniors and Senior students

title: Journey to Leadership Program
text: At BALI, we firmly believe that all youth, including female-identifying and gender-expansive individuals, possess the potential for greatness. Our mission is to empower them to become influential, adaptable, and visionary leaders of the 21st century. This program equips young women with the essential skills and socio-emotional learning necessary to develop the knowledge and confidence required to lead in all aspects of life. By fostering their abilities, we aim to create a generation of active and creative participants in civic, political, corporate, and community endeavors.
address: Hunter College. Office HE1233. 695 Park Ave. New York, NY 10021
requirements: Our summer program is open to all youth, ages 13-21 years old, residing in or from NYC metropolitan area. There are no academic or skills criteria, however there is an application and a short interview that follows as part of the selecting process. Priority is given to youth coming from underserved neighborhoods and or schools.

title: Haggerty Scholars Program
text: The Haggerty Scholars Program offers high school juniors, particularly those from underserved schools or underrepresented communities, the chance to immerse themselves in Oregon's legal and civic landscape. Selected students are paired with attorney mentors for the 2023-2024 school year, who provide personalized guidance and support. Mentors assist with college essays, facilitate courtroom observations, and offer networking opportunities tailored to students' interests. Adhering to COVID-safe protocols, mentors foster a dynamic and enriching experience for students, empowering them to explore the legal profession and engage with the broader civic community.
host: Oregon Chapter of the Federal Bar Association
requirements: The Haggerty Scholars Program is for current high school juniors (graduating in 2024) with an interest in law and civil rights. Students must be willing to meet with an attorney mentor on a regular basis and attend on-line meetings or panel discussions related to law and civil rights during the 2023-2024 school year. In-person events, if offered, will strictly follow COVID-safe protocols.

title: High School Program
text: Through KP LAUNCH, Kaiser Permanente provides paid internship opportunities for young adults in its Oakland headquarters and medical offices across Northern California. Interns gain valuable work experience in administrative and support roles within healthcare environments, contributing to projects that align with the organization's mission. This program offers exposure to various career paths in healthcare, allowing interns to explore their interests and develop their skills in a dynamic and supportive setting.
requirements: Have a permanent residence in a Northern California Kaiser Permanente designated service area. Provide proof of eligibility to legally work in the United States. Be ages 16 – 19 by June 1st.

title: Research Internship
text: Established in 1992, the Base Pair internship program fosters biomedical research mentorship between University of Mississippi Medical Center (UMMC) faculty and high school students and educators from the Jackson Public School District (JPSD). This program provides JPSD students with authentic biomedical research experiences under the guidance of UMMC faculty researchers. Base Pair has also spawned two additional programs: the Rural Biomedical Initiative (RBI), which offers inquiry-based, hands-on curricula for rural high schools, and the Student Oriented Academic Research (SOAR), a two-year science curriculum emphasizing locally-generated student research and adaptability to individual school resources. Base Pair's impact extends beyond local boundaries, positively influencing science education throughout Mississippi and the southeastern United States.
requirements: To be considered for the Base Pair program at the University of Mississippi Medical Center, applicants must be a junior or senior in good standing enrolled in the Jackson Public School District, specifically at Murrah High School. Applicants should have a passion for science and be willing to commit to an intensive, long-term biomedical research experience guided by a UMMC faculty member. Applicants must complete an online application, which includes two essays, one from the student and one from a teacher or counselor, detailing the student's academic history, career aspirations, and reasons for wanting to participate in the program. Additionally, applicants must have a minimum GPA of 3.0 and must commit to attending the program for at least two consecutive academic years.

title: Medical and Scientific Exploration Program (MSEP)
text: This career exploration program immerses high school students in the realm of health and medical professions by connecting them with experts in the field. Simultaneously, it strengthens their foundational knowledge in basic science. Participants delve into the intricacies of cellular and molecular biology, exploring how these concepts manifest in various human illnesses. Through this program, students gain a comprehensive understanding of the biological underpinnings of health and disease, equipping them with a solid foundation for future exploration in the healthcare field.
address: 1 Gustave L. Levy Pl, New York, NY 10029
host: The Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai
requirements:
Full attendance for the duration of the 6-week program
Regular oral and written progress reports

title: California State Parks Student Employment Program
text: The California State Parks Student Employment Program offers high school, college, and graduate students opportunities to explore future career paths, develop professional skills, and earn income while serving in various roles. These roles include youth aides, student assistants (for undergraduates), and graduate student assistants. Many positions do not require prior work experience, and student assistants may earn credit towards graduation. Openings are available at the Sacramento headquarters, most district offices, and facilities during the school year and summer months. Special opportunities exist for students in engineering and architectural sciences, as well as second-year law program students who can collaborate with experts in their fields. Interested applicants should contact individual District and Division Offices for more information, as the recruitment and hiring process for student assistants is decentralized.
requirements: To be considered for the California State Parks Student Employment Program as a student assistant, you must be currently enrolled in high school, college, or graduate school. The program is open to students who want to learn about career opportunities in California State Parks, develop their professional skills, and earn money. Student assistants work in various district offices and facilities, performing tasks that require limited or no previous work experience. Students can earn credits toward graduation and may also have special opportunities in engineering, architectural sciences, and legal offices. Since recruiting and hiring for student assistant positions are decentralized, you must contact individual District and Division Offices to find out about openings in Sacramento and other locations. To learn more about the program, you can contact the California State Parks Student Employment Program Coordinator (Personnel) at the address provided.

title: Hands on Experience and Internships
text: The Missouri Innovation Campus (MIC) program is a practical, hands-on initiative that combines paid internships with professional mentorship to equip students with job-ready skills. Over a three-year period, MIC students engage in internships with industry-leading corporate partners, gaining valuable experience and guidance from professional mentors. The curriculum, developed in collaboration with these corporate partners, ensures that students acquire the necessary knowledge and abilities to excel in their chosen careers. By seamlessly integrating internships with a tailored curriculum, the MIC program empowers students to enter the workforce with the confidence and expertise to thrive in their respective fields.
requirements: To be considered for the Missouri Innovation Campus program internship, applicants must be high school juniors who are eligible for graduation in the spring of their senior year, have a cumulative 3.0 or higher GPA, and meet the admission criteria set by the University of Central Missouri. Students must provide their own transportation to the internship site and are required to interview with MIC business partners for their internships before the end of their junior summer. The internship is continuous with the same business partner each year, and students will be paid for the full-time internship each summer, fall, and spring. If a student is dismissed from their internship due to performance issues, they will be dropped from the program. Students must secure an internship to remain in the MIC program before starting their senior year in high school, based on internship availability. By completing these internships alongside a curriculum developed in part by MIC’s corporate partners, MIC students are positioned to enter the workplace with the necessary skills and experience to excel in their chosen careers.

title: Development Intern
text: The Development Intern will gain comprehensive experience in the Development Department, encompassing donor development, event planning, and communications. With a primary focus on event planning, the intern will play a pivotal role in assisting with the execution of successful events. Their contributions will directly impact the department's fundraising efforts, ensuring continued financial support for NAMI Mississippi's programs.
requirements: unknown

title: Creative Practice
text: This paid internship offers New York City teens the opportunity to delve into the realms of art, education, and museum careers. Interns will work alongside teaching artists, assisting in classes for students of all ages, thereby gaining valuable experience and building their résumés. Through this immersive program, teens will explore the multifaceted world of art and education, gaining insights into the inner workings of museums and the role of art in shaping young minds.
requirements: This program is open to all NYC teens, ages 15–19, who are enrolled in high school as a sophomore, junior, or senior as of the fall.

title: The Office of Undergraduate Research (OUR) Research Education Program (REP) for High School Students
text: Through this program, students will delve into the intricacies of the research cycle and its methodologies, gaining a comprehensive understanding of research paradigms and methodologies across various academic disciplines. They will engage in collaborative research projects with undergraduate researchers from diverse fields, fostering interdisciplinary perspectives. Moreover, students will develop essential transferable research skills, including critical reading, digital information literacy, and effective research writing and communication. These skills encompass abstract writing, presentation crafting, and manuscript preparation, equipping students with a solid foundation for future research endeavors.
requirements: Currently enrolled high school juniors and seniors in the greater Las Vegas community with a minimum of a 3.0 unweighted GPA intending to apply to UNLV or those who have already applied to UNLV are eligible for consideration. Interested students unable to meet these eligibility requirements should contact OUR directly at our@unlv.edu.

title: High School Internship (Venture Analyst)
text: This open listing seeks highly motivated high school juniors or seniors with a passion for business, finance, and entrepreneurship to intern at a specialized venture capital firm in the Northeastern US. The hybrid internship requires limited commuting to Princeton, NJ. Ideal candidates possess a thirst for knowledge, an entrepreneurial mindset, and a strong academic record. The internship offers an immersive experience in the venture capital industry, providing hands-on exposure to investment analysis, deal sourcing, and portfolio management.
requirements:
Strong academic record and demonstrated interest in venture capital and technology.
Strong financial and analytical skills, including proficiency in Google Sheets and Excel.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Self-starter with the ability to work independently and as part of a team.
Entrepreneurial mindset and passion for technology and innovation.

title: UVU Latinos of Tomorrow Summer Bridge Program
text: Utah Valley University's Latinos of Tomorrow Bridge Programs foster a vibrant community of aspiring scholars, empowering them to navigate the complexities of higher education. Through tailored initiatives, the program equips young minds with the skills and knowledge necessary to excel in university settings. Its mission is to cultivate a diverse and inclusive environment where students can engage actively with academic challenges, develop critical thinking abilities, and prepare for success in their future endeavors.
requirements: Students with a minimum of 2.5 GPA

title: High School Internship Program
text: Jersey 1st is dedicated to raising awareness about the detrimental effects of excessive taxation and regulation, as well as the improper utilization of state resources. Interns will actively participate in our mission by analyzing federal and state legislation, composing research reports, spearheading advocacy campaigns through social and print media, and delivering presentations.
requirements: Candidates must live or go to school in New Jersey and have a strong interest in government, politics, and making New Jersey a better place. Additionally, we welcome candidates with strong research, writing, and verbal communication skills. We accept high school juniors, seniors, and college, or graduate students into the program. We are currently accepting applicants to join our communications, research, and grassroots teams.

title: Teen Work Study Program
text: Individuals with a passion for sharing animal knowledge are invited to collaborate with Shedd's Guest Engagement team. Through this partnership, they will master the art of engaging guests with animals within Shedd's exhibits. They will lead theme-based interpretations, facilitate interactive engagements, and create educational experiences that foster a deeper understanding and appreciation for the animal kingdom.
address: 1200 S DuSable Lk Shr Dr, Chicago, IL 60605
requirements:
We're looking for bright, outgoing and motivated Chicago area teens for our work-study program.
Applicants should possess or want to develop strong communication skills and a connection to Shedd's collection and mission, and have a desire to work in a team environment interacting with the public. This is a professional paid work experience.

title: STEAM Team
text: The STEAM Team, a workforce development program and paid fellowship opportunity for Boston teens, is offered by the Museum of Fine Arts in Boston. This program delves into STEAM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Art, and Mathematics) careers within the renowned cultural institution. Through hands-on learning activities, fellows engage with MFA staff mentors in each STEAM discipline. They also visit local businesses, organizations, and artists involved in innovative STEAM work. Field trips and activities at various New England institutions further enhance their experiences. Fellows establish connections with professionals in their chosen fields, develop team building and leadership skills with their peers, and cultivate their workforce development, academic, and professional aspirations through social engagement activities and presentations by leading minds in STEAM disciplines. The program is available to rising sophomores attending Boston public schools or residing in Boston.
requirements: To be considered for the STEAM Team fellowship program at the Museum of Fine Arts Boston, applicants must be rising sophomores attending a Boston public school or living in Boston. They should be interested in exploring potential STEAM careers (Science, Technology, Engineering, Art, and Mathematics), and demonstrate a willingness to learn and participate in hands-on learning activities with MFA staff mentors in each corresponding STEAM discipline. The program aims to cultivate workforce development skills while introducing the fellows to various academic and professional options in the STEAM fields. Fellows are expected to build strong connections with professionals in their field of interest and cultivate team-building and leadership skills with peers. Applications are considered on a rolling basis and can be sent in by emailing teens@mfa.org.

title: Summer 2023 Youth Journalism Internship
text: This intensive program is designed for students eager to immerse themselves in the practical aspects of local media production. Participants are encouraged to bring story ideas and will receive comprehensive training and support to create short nonfiction multimedia pieces in various formats, including video, photography, audio, and written content. The program aims to provide hands-on experience and equip students with the skills necessary to produce compelling and impactful local media.
address: 3700 S Four Mile Run Dr, Arlington, VA 22206
requirements: Youth aged 14-19 years old who live in Arlington or surrounding areas (Falls Church, etc).

title: Student Internship Job
text: The Work-Based Learning Program provides an internship program that aids in placement for all Aztec Municipal Schools High School students. While internship availability may be limited, this program seamlessly integrates classroom learning with real-world experiences. Internships are closely aligned with related internship classes or advisory sessions, offering both paid and unpaid opportunities. These time-limited experiences are tailored to students' career aspirations and Next Step Plans (NSPs). Through internships, students gain valuable insights into specific career fields, allowing them to explore their interests and make informed decisions about their future endeavors.
requirements: Students must be in good academic standing and be on track to graduate prior to enrolling in the internship program. Must be enrolled in a high school part of Aztec Municipal School District

title: PrepareRI High School Internship Program
text: The PrepareRI High School Internship Program offers a 7-week work-based learning experience for Rhode Island public high school juniors, including public charter schools and home school students. Regardless of ability, learning style, or career interest, students can participate in the program. Selected students receive job readiness coaching, paid internships with one of SkillsRI's 180 employer partners, and the potential to earn up to $4,200 during the summer of 2023. Eligibility requirements include attending a Rhode Island high school, obtaining parental consent, completing an online internship application, and attending a 40-hour paid work-readiness bootcamp.
requirements: The PrepareRI High School Internship Program is a paid internship offered to current Rhode Island public high school juniors including public charter schools and home school students. The program lasts for seven weeks during the summer of 2023, and interns will earn $15.00/hour, with the potential of earning up to $4,200 in total. To be considered for the program, applicants must attend a Rhode Island public high school, public charter high school, or home school with an identified local LEA, must be a current junior in high school during the 2022/2023 school year, and have parental/guardian consent to participate. They must also be a Rhode Island resident, at least 16 years of age by March 1, 2023, complete the online PrepareRI High School Internship Application, and successfully complete an interview with both SkillsRI and employer(s). Additionally, they must attend the mandatory 40-hour paid work-readiness bootcamp, which is scheduled from June 26 – June 30, 2023, and complete a minimum of 175 hours of work over a six-week period between July 10 – August 18, 2023. Finally, they must have a flexible schedule for work during the summer of 2023 and be eligible to work in the United States.

title: QCaMP
text: QCaMP is a week-long virtual and in-person camp designed for high school teachers and students to jumpstart their pathway to quantum information science and technology. This program introduces students to a new field, teaching them computing fundamentals and applying quantum physics to solve computing problems in new ways. The camp is free and offers a learning stipend, with no advanced math or physics requirements. The program includes modules accessible and engaging for both teachers and students, featuring career talks, Q&A sessions, and hands-on experimental experience with quantum circuits. The only prerequisites are basic algebra and a strong interest in learning more. The next start date is in Summer 2023, with stipends available for both teacher and student participants.
requirements: The Quantum Systems Accelerator offers a week-long (virtual and in-person) QCaMP (Quantum Computing and Mechanics Primer) aimed at high school students and teachers interested in quantum information science and technology. The program is free and participants receive a learning stipend. The only prerequisites for this camp are basic algebra and an interest in learning more. Participants will get a primer on computing fundamentals, learn hands-on about quantum physics, create circuits on a real-world quantum computer, and gain access to learning resources. The modules and sessions are accessible and engaging, and no advanced math or physics are required. The teacher program includes pedagogical discussions, feedback, and resource sharing, while the student program includes career talks and lots of Q&A.

title: Young Scholars Program (YSP)
text: The Young Scholars Program (YSP) at Northeastern University provides Massachusetts high school seniors with an immersive research experience in science and engineering. Participants engage in laboratory research under the guidance of faculty from Northeastern's Colleges of Engineering, Science, and Health Sciences, exploring topics such as active particles in flow and cancer therapies. Beyond research, YSP offers seminars and workshops on engineering, education, career counseling, and college life. Participants also visit corporate and government sites to observe engineers in action. The program prioritizes students with limited access to similar opportunities and those within commuting distance to Northeastern. Applications open in January for the following summer, with results announced in April.
requirements: To be considered for the Young Scholars Program (YSP), applicants must meet the following requirements: 1) Applicants must be permanent Massachusetts residents who have completed their junior year of high school (i.e. rising seniors), and must live within commutable distance of Northeastern University, 2) Students from any school (public, private, homeschooled, etc) are eligible to apply, and an even number of males and females will be selected, from a diverse range of demographic backgrounds, 3) Priority is given to those students who have low access to similar programs, 4) Absences are not permitted unless in a documented emergency, 5) Applicants must submit a completed YSP application, a recent transcript, two letters of recommendation, and a short essay describing their interest in engineering, science research, and this program, and 6) Applicants must adhere to the application timeline, with applications typically opening in January, closing in March, and results being posted by April. YSP aims to provide selected students with laboratory research experiences, career exploration, education and career counseling, field trips, and exposure to college life.

title: UChicago Summer Session Pre-College Program
text: The University of Chicago's Pre-College Programs offer high school students a transformative summer experience. These programs foster intellectual growth and exploration through exposure to diverse ideas and a supportive community. Students engage in challenging coursework, delve into subject matter beyond their high school curriculum, and engage in thought-provoking discussions. The Immersion program immerses students in a specific academic discipline, while Research in the Biological Sciences (RIBS) provides hands-on research opportunities. Stones and Bones explores archaeology and paleontology, and Summer College offers college-level courses. The Summer Language Institute focuses on language acquisition, and the UChicago Summer Online program provides virtual learning experiences. Led by world-renowned faculty and instructors, these programs offer students the opportunity to learn and explore diverse areas of study, both in person and online.
requirements: To be considered for the University of Chicago's pre-college internship program, applicants must be high school students who are passionate about learning and willing to take intellectual risks. The program is open to students from all over the world, and applicants are exposed to diverse ideas and world-class faculty. The university offers many different programs, including the Summer College, Stones and Bones, and the Summer Language Institute. To apply, students must complete the application process, which includes submitting transcripts, essays, letters of recommendation, and other supporting material. These materials are evaluated by a selection committee, which then chooses the most qualified applicants for the program.

title: The Summer Bridge Programs
text: The University of Illinois Chicago (UIC) offers Summer Bridge Programs tailored to both high school students and admitted first-year students. These programs encompass diverse fields including health care, computer science, architecture, mathematics, engineering, and more. Designed to foster college and career readiness, they provide hands-on experiences, workshops, field trips, and mentorship support. High school students can engage in programs such as the Global Youth Ambassadors Leadership Program, Engineering Experience Camp, and Medicina Academy Apprentice Program. Admitted first-year students have access to seminars, workshops, and enrichment programs like Flames Leadership Network, Introduction to Blackboard 101, and LaHSEP 3. UIC's Summer Bridge Programs aim to empower students through engaging and challenging experiences, equipping them for academic and professional success.
host: University of Illinois Chicago's Office of the Vice Provost for Undergraduate Affairs and Academic Programs
requirements: The Summer Bridge Programs at the University of Illinois Chicago (UIC) offer opportunities for high school students as well as admitted first-year UIC students. Each program has specific requirements; however, most programs require applicants to be high school students with a minimum GPA (usually 2.5 or higher) and exhibit an interest in the program's field of study. Some programs, such as the College of Engineering Summer Bridge Program and the Latino Health Science Enrichment Program, specifically target students from underrepresented communities or low-income households. Admitted first-year UIC students can also participate in summer programs such as the Career Readiness Enrichment Program or the President's Award Program (PAP) Academy. The PAP Academy requires PAP Scholar and Sukuma Scholar students to attend the mandatory summer orientation, while PAP STEM Co-Lab is a research experience for PAP students in STEM majors. Ultimately, each program has its own set of requirements, which can be found on the UIC website or by contacting the Office of the Vice Provost for Undergraduate Affairs and Academic Programs.

title: Summer Internship Program
text: CSBI offers a six-week paid internship program to Chicago high school students during the summer. These internships are hosted by various banks, law firms, accounting and engineering firms located in the Loop and business districts. In addition to working 24 hours per week, students participate in half-day classroom seminars and workshops each week. These sessions cover topics such as financial markets, feature seminars led by successful business executives, and include team-building activities.
requirements: Applicants must be: A resident of the City of Chicago, a high school Sophomore or Junior (2022-2023 school year), maintain a “B” or 3.0 average on report cards, and have Family Household Income below $80,000/year

title: Summer Internship
text: The Museum of the Rockies (MOR), a 501(c)(3) non-profit institution affiliated with Montana State University and the Smithsonian, serves as a repository for state and federal fossils. Recognized globally for its exceptional research and historical exhibits, MOR boasts an extensive collection of dinosaur fossils, notably the fully-mounted Montana's T. rex skeleton. Visitors and members can immerse themselves in rotating exhibits from around the world, regional and natural history displays, planetarium shows, educational programs and camps, thought-provoking lectures, benefit events, and a museum store. MOR's dedicated staff and volunteers strive to foster an environment of exploration, discovery, excitement, and awe for all who visit.
requirements: unknown

title: Artslife
text: Artslife is a paid summer internship program for rising sophomores and juniors enrolled in New York City public and charter high schools. The program combines art and design with leadership training, museum studies, and community engagement. Participants are introduced to careers in all sectors of the museum, including Curatorial, Education, Development, Communications and Marketing, Visitor Services, Security, and Registrar.
address:
JEROME AND SIMONA CHAZEN BUILDING
2 COLUMBUS CIRCLE, NYC
requirements: unknown

title: Internship Program
text: The City of New Haven prioritizes education and recognizes the contributions of students to the workforce through its Student Intern Program. Internships offer students practical experience aligned with their academic pursuits. Participants gain high-level responsibilities that prepare them for future employment opportunities. The program fosters the development of new ideas, energy, and skills within the workforce, providing students with valuable hands-on experience and potential pathways to permanent positions.
requirements:
Must be at least 16 years of age. Must be enrolled as a student at an accredited high school, college or university; proof of enrollment must be submitted along with online application.
Student must complete the online application process and submit a resume and current transcripts. If we are accepting applications for Student Interns, you will find the posting online.
Preference will be given to those residing in New Haven.

title: Emerging Filmmaker Program
text: The Tallgrass Film Association's Class of 2023 Emerging Filmmaker Program (EFP) invites aspiring filmmakers in grades 8 through 12 (ages 13-18) to apply. Participants will engage with industry professionals in film criticism, directing, producing, screenwriting, audio production, lighting, camera technique, and video editing. Hands-on experiences include screening and reviewing over 125 peer-submitted films for the Tallgrass Film Festival, creating promotional videos for the festival, and producing a short film for festival submission.
address: 120 East 1st St North, Suite 113 Wichita, KS 67202
requirements: unknown

title: Public Policy Research Intern
text: NAMI Mississippi actively engages in advocacy efforts, participating in work groups and committees that address mental health concerns. The organization maintains a strong presence at the Mississippi Legislature, advocating for and supporting policies that benefit individuals with mental illness and their families. To support these efforts, the policy research intern will assist the executive director by conducting research on topics relevant to work groups, committees, and legislative goals.
requirements: unknown

title: BAC Summer Academy for High School Students
text: The Boston Architectural College's (BAC) Pre-College Program empowers high school students with an interest in design to embark on their future in the field. On-campus participants engage in live lectures, hands-on design and building, and site and firm visits in Boston. Virtual students explore case studies, attend virtual site and firm visits, and receive materials for hands-on activities. All students access cutting-edge design software through on-site computer labs or the BAC's CloudLab, fostering collaboration and innovation.
requirements: High school student

title: Internship Program
text: The Futures and Options Internship Program offers New York City high school students valuable work-readiness training and hands-on experience through paid, mentored internships with diverse business partners. These internships are tailored to align with students' skills and interests, providing them with an opportunity to gain practical knowledge and develop professional competencies. The program aims to prepare students for future careers in the business sector by equipping them with essential work-related skills and exposing them to real-world work environments.
address: Futures and Options, 120 Broadway, Suite 1019, New York, NY 10271
requirements: Students must be enrolled in high school in New York City and be at least 16 years old; have a valid working card; and be eligible to lawfully work in the United States.

title: Research in Science & Engineering (RISE) Internship/Practicum
text: The RISE program, offered by Boston University Summer Term, is a six-week internship/practicum designed for domestic high school juniors with a passion for STEM subjects. The program offers two tracks: Internship and Practicum. In the Internship track, students engage in research projects under the guidance of postdoctoral fellows, graduate students, and faculty, working 40 hours per week. The Practicum track provides a structured syllabus on computational neurobiology, led by a BU instructor, with four hours of group research in the afternoon and two-hour lectures in the morning. Both tracks include workshops to enhance academic and professional skills, poster symposium presentations, and weekly interactions with biotech or pharmaceutical firms. Students gain proficiency in reading research papers, networking in engineering and science fields, and understanding research ethics and the scientific process. With over 40 years of experience, the RISE program has fostered the careers of numerous students in science, engineering, and research.
requirements: The Research in Science & Engineering (RISE) program offered by Boston University's Summer Term caters to junior high school students who are interested in pursuing the sciences. Applicants who are domestic students must currently be in their junior year of high school to qualify. The program offers two tracks, the Internship track and the Practicum track, both of which span six weeks. The Internship track allows students to work on research projects supervised by faculty members, postdoctoral fellows, and graduate students, focusing on developing technical and analytical skills, insight into the scientific process, and STEM knowledge while spending 40 hours per week on their projects. On the other hand, the Practicum track, focused on computational neurobiology, is ideal for students who prefer a more structured research environment. Students in this track will be tasked with group research in a university laboratory setting guided by a BU instructor. Both tracks include weekly workshops aimed at building academic and professional skills, as well as off-site or on-site interactions with local biotech or pharmaceutical companies. A laptop capable of running programming software is required for Practicum students. Each student will present their research findings at the Poster Symposium that concludes the program.

title: Harvard Pre-College Program
text: The Pre-College Summer School Program for High School Students, offered by Harvard Summer School, is a two-week on-campus program designed for academically motivated high school students who are interested in exploring their potential majors, discovering their passions, and experiencing college life on the Harvard campus. The program features an immersive and supportive academic environment with around 100 non-credit courses, where students can test their intellect, take rigorous college-level courses for learning’s sake, and receive a written evaluation from their instructors. Additionally, students can participate in creative and social activities, engage in healthy debates, make new friends around the world, and attend informative workshops on college readiness.
requirements: Applicants must be rising juniors or seniors, at least 16 years old by June 17, 2023, and will not turn 19 years old before July 31, 2023. Applicants must meet both of these criteria, and be mature, academically motivated individuals who are interested in exploring a potential major or simply finding out what college is really like. The program is an intensive two-week summer program designed to offer students a glimpse of college life on the Harvard campus. Over 100 non-credit courses are offered in this program, and students will be challenged by Ivy League scholars as they immerse themselves in one subject in an average class size of 15 students.

title: Vermont Adaptive’s Apprenticeship Program
text: Vermont Adaptive seeks passionate individuals aged 14-17 to join their Apprenticeship Program. This program offers volunteers the opportunity to gain valuable experience in sports, working with athletes with disabilities, and non-profit management. Apprentices will receive training, participate in skiing, riding, mountain biking, and paddling activities, and potentially earn school credit or enhance their applications and resumes. The program aims to foster a love for sports and provide a platform for apprentices to share their passions while supporting the organization's mission of empowering individuals with disabilities through adaptive recreation.
requirements: Students ages 14-17.

title: The Columbia Climate School in the Green Mountains
text: The Columbia Climate School in the Green Mountains is a transformative 2-week campus-based program in Castleton, Vermont, designed for high school students passionate about addressing climate change. Immerse yourself in cutting-edge innovations and engage with experts from Columbia Climate School. Collaborate with like-minded peers, forge partnerships, and leverage collective strengths to drive impact and effect meaningful change in response to our warming planet. Through hands-on experiences and expert guidance, you'll gain a deep understanding of climate science, policy, and solutions, empowering you to mobilize action and become a catalyst for positive change in your communities and beyond.
requirements: Columbia Climate School Summer Programs are designed for and open to students in grades 9-12 across the United States, as well as motivated rising 9th grade students.

title: Legacy Youth Leadership Program
text: The Legacy Youth Leadership Program (LYLP), offered by the Birmingham Civil Rights Institute (BCRI), is a comprehensive training and internship initiative designed for high school students. Through a series of 12 weekly workshops, LYLP participants delve into BCRI's permanent galleries, archival holdings, and public programs, exploring African American history, culture, and leadership development. The program fosters confidence, character, community involvement, and leadership skills. Upon completion, students assume the role of Docents at BCRI, continuing their volunteer service throughout high school. LYLP aims to cultivate lifelong learners, productive citizens, and community leaders, equipping students with the knowledge and skills to make meaningful contributions to society.
requirements: Be a high school student that resides in Alabama

title: American Red Cross Teen Volunteer
text: Through Red Cross youth volunteerism, young individuals embark on a transformative journey where they acquire invaluable skills in collaborating effectively with diverse populations, mobilizing communities, and catalyzing positive change. They refine their leadership abilities, forge meaningful connections, and delve into novel interests within a supportive and age-appropriate environment that yields tangible outcomes. By embracing this opportunity, youth volunteers lay the foundation for a lifelong commitment to serving worthy causes with compassion and generosity.
address:
2610 Shackleford Road, Suite B
LIttle Rock, AR 72205
requirements: Must be 15-18+, but there are some limited opportunities for students under 15

title: Next Generation STEM Internship Program
text: The Next Generation STEM Internship Program (NGSI) offers rising juniors and seniors from select counties the opportunity to engage in STEM projects with researchers at Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL). Participants gain hands-on experience under the guidance of renowned scientists and engineers, while also attending professional development activities such as workshops, lab tours, lectures, poster sessions, seminars, and networking events. To qualify, applicants must be U.S. citizens or legal permanent residents, rising juniors/seniors or recent graduates, maintain a minimum GPA of 3.0/4.0, and be at least 16 years old by the time of appointment. The program provides weekly stipends of up to $500 based on 40 hours of participation per week.
address: 5200, 1 Bethel Valley Rd, Oak Ridge, TN 37830
requirements: To be eligible for the Next Generation STEM Internship Program (NGSI), applicants must be rising juniors/seniors or recently graduated seniors (within two years of graduation who have not yet enrolled in college) or in good standing at an accredited high school or enrolled in an accredited home school program in Anderson, Blount, Knox, Roane, or Loudon County. They should also be at least 16 years old by the appointment period start date and should have a minimum GPA of 3.0/4.0. Additionally, applicants must be U.S. citizens or legal permanent residents at the time of application. They are expected to participate 40 hours per week, and can miss a maximum of 5 days (without stipend) during the appointment period if necessary for other commitments. To apply, they will need to complete an online application via Zintillect, obtain two STEM teacher and principal (curriculum coordinator for home school students) recommendations through the same system, and complete pre- and post-appointment surveys. They will also need to behave in a responsible and professional manner, avoid activities that interfere with their appointment period, and complete a report at the end of the appointment.

title: Raleigh Summer Youth Employment Program (RSYEP)
text: The Raleigh Summer Youth Employment Program offers teenagers aged 15 to 18 within Raleigh city limits an opportunity to gain valuable workforce experience and skills. The six-week program, running from late June to early August, provides participants with employment at the City of Raleigh, along with mandatory training and orientation sessions. Beyond work experience, the program emphasizes skill-building and training, as well as networking opportunities. Participation requires availability for the program's duration, attendance at orientation and training sessions, and proof of residency via an NC State Issued ID or equivalent documentation. The program prioritizes health and safety, requiring full Covid-19 vaccination for in-person or hybrid work, while also offering a virtual work option for those preferring remote work.
requirements: Applicants to the Raleigh Summer Youth Employment Program must be between the ages of 15 and 18 as of May 31, 2023, live within the Raleigh city limits, and be available to work from June 20 to August 4. They must attend the mandatory in-person program orientation on May 20 and not miss more than four program days or be enrolled in summer school. They must be the only one in their household participating in the program and have computer and internet access if they choose the virtual option. Additionally, applicants must have an NC State Issued ID, Learner’s Permit, Driver’s License, or current school report card that shows a Raleigh zip code at the time of interview, with no exceptions. Finally, all new employees must be fully vaccinated against COVID-19 for in-person or hybrid work, and for virtual/remote employment, vaccination is not required.

title: UnitedHealth Group's Unified High School Internship Experience
text: The Optum High School Internship Program, offered by UnitedHealth Group, provides a transformative experience for rising juniors and seniors seeking hands-on immersion in the dynamic healthcare industry. This paid internship, ranging from 6-8 weeks and potentially remote in select locations, offers exposure to diverse career paths within Optum, a renowned health services and innovation company. Interns engage in real-world healthcare challenges, collaborating with experts in IT, finance, human resources, product management, and more. The program fosters the development of future healthcare leaders, emphasizing empathy, social impact, diversity, and inclusion as foundational principles.
requirements: The requirements for applicants to be considered for the UnitedHealth Group's Unified High School Internship Experience are as follows: they must currently be enrolled in high school as a rising junior or senior, must be authorized to work in the US, and must meet all requirements listed on the UnitedHealth Group application form, including submitting their resume. Additionally, applicants must live within a commutable distance to one of the specified locations or be located in Raleigh, NC; Basking Ridge, NJ, Cypress, CA, Eden Prairie, MN, District of Columbia, Texas and Georgia, which will allow for remote work. Authorization to work in the US is necessary and F-1 visa holders with Curricular Practical Training (CPT) or Optional Practical Training (OPT), TN visa holders, current H-1B visa holders, and/or those requiring green card sponsorship will not be considered. Applicants exhibiting a willingness to learn by asking questions and contributing ideas, demonstrating attention to detail, time-management skills, effective communication and written skills, and the ability to collaborate with others as part of a team are preferred.
